onAttack: onChord() is an empty function ('The growth and the light are in the plan'). makePlan(N,K) precomputes, from the whole note list, one entry per attack chord: wood segments (segData, birth = T[ci] + min(0.13, 0.006*k) stagger), leaf instances (birth = T[ci], at the loudest-note's pitch spot via spotOf; per-note counts round(want*n.v/sum)), a hit spot hitX/hitY[ci] (the first new leaf's site, else the last new wood segment) and a strength eOf[ci] = min(1, q^1.5 * (1+0.14*min(4,notes-1))), q = (vel-v5)/(v95-v5) clamped 0.04..1 against the recording's own 5th/95th percentile. frame(x) is a pure function of song time t=x.t and lastChord(T,t): the GPU draws every leaf/segment with birth<=t, plus an 'arrival' pass for leaves/segments born in the last 0.5 s, so the attack is seen on its own frame (age u=0) as a leaf at about twice its size, lit, plus a white-hot flare on the new twig, a local light break-through in the crown and a small sway kick at the hit point.
decay: All envelopes live in GLSL/frame() and are functions of age u = uT - birth (or w = t - T[ci]). Quote: leaf size pop = 1.0 + (0.5 + 0.75*loud)*exp(-u/0.1) (tau 0.1 s, so 1.5-2.25x at u=0, ~0.33 s to settle); arrival glow vE = (p1*1.1 + uFlash*0.16)*exp(-u/0.12)*(0.4+0.7*loud) (tau 0.12 s), arrival pass is dropped entirely at u>0.5 (#if MODE==2 'if (u > 0.5) return'); twig flash vFl = exp(-u/0.14) (tau 0.14 s), in E alpha as vFl*2.2 and in the FLARE pass as uFlash*vFl*exp(-d*d*2.6)*0.65; twig growth: b = mix(a,b0,clamp(u/0.03+0.5,0,1)) (extends in 0.03 s), radius ra = r*(0.6+0.4*smoothstep(0,0.1,u)) (0.1 s), stagger up to 0.13 s; thickness stage P = a + (b-a)*smooth(0,0.25,t-T[ci]) (0.25 s smoothstep swell between 8 radius snapshots); light break-through hitBuf.z = (0.3+0.7*e)*exp(-age/0.24) (tau 0.24 s), radius 50+90*e px, last 8 attacks, skipped at age>0.9 s; sway kick d += uKick.z*exp(-q.q/52000)*sin(uKick.w*24)*exp(-uKick.w*7)*(1.5+4f) (tau 0.143 s, uKick.z = eOf*0.7) and leaf wobble rot += uKick.z*exp(-kq.kq/40000)*sin(uKick.w*30+s0*20)*exp(-uKick.w*6)*0.5 (tau 0.167 s). What the attack made is NOT removed: leaves and wood are permanent until their planned fall (leaf life (0.42+0.8j)*P with P the year length, ripening young-to-mature colour over uRipen=7 s*(0.6..1.4), fall time snapped to a later attack's time; on dead limbs fall = t+1.4+j*5 s). The fast-dying part is only the arrival (0.1-0.24 s) and the hit-light (0.24 s).
lowPass: No smoothing of the attack itself (zero latency, the draw is at u=0 on the attack's frame). What softens the response: (1) loudness is ranked against the recording (5th-95th percentile) then q^1.5, so most attacks are weak in e and in the light/kick, only the loudest are strong; (2) soft chords share one wood pool and step at the first note; (3) at most 6 notes of a chord (loudest) make leaves; (4) a 0.25 s smoothstep on thickness P; (5) 8 hit slots, 0.9 s cutoff; (6) cell caps and a leaves-per-attack clamp min(34+80e, 1.3*160000/nc) mean dense passages place few leaves per attack; (7) the pop/glow strength depends on 'loud' (leaf's stored e) with factor 0.4+0.7*loud. Not any feat.rate damping. No use of x.feat at all.
snapKnobs: leaves (how many leaves): fewer/more leaves per attack, no timing
twigs (how much wood): amount of wood, no timing
wither: seasonal leaf life/fall, not the attack
size (how big the leaves are): scales the leaf, so also scales the pop
presence (leads): sets leaves/twigs/wither together
colours (season): palette preset only (PRESETS)
none of the existing knobs changes any attack or decay time constant; there is no snap or decay knob
howToSnap: Tree is already alert to the attack (same-frame, pop at about 2x). To make it also quick to die, change only the constants in the shaders and the hitBuf line, which are the whole 'aftermath': leaf pop exp(-u/0.1) -> ~0.05; arrival glow exp(-u/0.12) -> ~0.06 and the arrival drop 'u > 0.5' -> 0.25; twig flash vFl exp(-u/0.14) -> ~0.07 (vFl is shared by the E alpha and FLARE_F); hit-light exp(-age/0.24) -> ~0.1 (and the 0.9 s cutoff -> 0.4) at hitBuf in frame(); sway/rot kicks exp(-w*7) and exp(-w*6) -> ~14 and 12; P swell smooth(0,0.25,..) -> (0,0.1) and radius smoothstep(0,0.1,u) -> (0,0.04). A global scale works: add one uniform uSnap (default 1.0) and a CPU multiplier, dividing every u/tau by it (u*uSnap, age*snap, w*snap), so the knob at default is bit-identical. Also the biggest perceived 'doesn't die' is that leaves persist, which is by design and should stay; to make individual notes legible, increase pop amplitude (0.5+0.75*loud) and apply a brief dim/dark-out of the leaf for ~0.1 s after the pop, not a shorter life. It does not need onChord: everything is a function of t - T[ci].
risk: Safe in shaders because everything is a pure function of song time and the precomputed plan (seek and render stay deterministic; renderFrameHash would change only if the new knob is non-default). Limits: the arrival pass only draws leaves/segments from chords born in the last 0.5 s (before = lastChord(t-0.5)), hitBuf only 8 slots/0.9 s: longer envelopes would be clipped by these windows (shortening is safe). 'loud' is stored in the leaf (a2.x) and e in eOf, so a per-note value (picked-note intensity) would only reach it through plan inputs N (hashNotes -> seed -> whole tree layout changes with any note edit), not at runtime. Wood and leaf stagger (0.006 s per segment, up to 0.13 s) blur the attack of a big limb growth. Must keep the WebGL2 fallback (paintFlat path) and the plan cache (F.plan !== pl) untouched. No fluid sim, no post pass except the 4-pass bloom blur with uBloom 0.17 (stateless), so no persistence to break; but it is the only widget here with a precomputed plan, so envelopes baked into the plan (leaf life, fall times snapped to attack times, wood share) must not change.

onAttack: onChord(ch,x): sets mel = pitch01(ch.hi); takes up to the 9 highest notes (sorted by pitch, .slice(-9)) filtered by hardNote(v,presence) (all pass at presence 1); for each note pushes 1+echoes outline objects at the vanishing point {r: size0(p,v,mouth)/1.45^i, age 0, dim 0.62^i, big: only on a hard chord's first echo}, size0 = mouth*(8+70*(1-p)^1.6)*(0.55+0.6*v/110). A hard chord (punch = max(0,(vel-78)/30)*min(1,sqrt(n/3)) > 0.35) sets surge = max(surge, punch*1.3) and kick = min(1,punch). In frame(), on age 0 the new outline is drawn with flash = exp(-age/0.09) brightening and +0.3*dim*ink alpha, plus (big) a 0.25 s fill; so each note's attack is seen as a crisp ring/square/triangle that appears on its own frame at the mouth, then streams outward as the zoom grows it.
decay: Quote: outline alpha a = fog*(0.2+0.8*min(1,v/105))*(0.35+0.65*hold)*exp(-age/3)*dim*ink, with hold = exp(-max(0,age-o.d)/0.6) (tau 0.6 s, starts only when the note's transcribed length d has passed), exp(-age/3) (tau 3 s), fog = min(1,(r/70)^0.6) (small=far=dim), life ends at age>=10 s or r>=1500; flash = exp(-o.age/0.09) (tau 0.09 s) adds 0.3*flash alpha and 25% brightness; big-fill 0.3*(1-age/0.25) (0.25 s linear); surge *= exp(-dt/0.4) (tau 0.4 s, fall speed bonus surge*1.8), kick *= exp(-dt/0.15) (tau 0.15 s, mouth flash radial gradient 90+160*kick px, alpha 0.35*kick); outlines grow r *= exp(zv*1.15*dt) with zv = (speed*(0.42+2.2*rate^2.2+0.3*level)+surge*1.8)*calm (so the speed from rate and level makes outlines stream out); walls (the zoom feedback) decay with half-life trail*wallOf(pres) = 0.35 s default (b = pow(0.5, dt/(trail*wall))/0.88, trail range 0.05-1.5, drive -density); held notes keep tracing a faint outline at the mouth, a = 0.16*(v/127)*exp(-(t-start)/2) (tau 2 s, up to 6 sounding notes, alpha < 0.01 skipped); vp follows target with 1-exp(-1.6*dt) (tau 0.625 s).
lowPass: Several: (1) fold(): mouth = clamp(1+1.35*feat.level,0.3,3) and echoes = round(3-3*feat.density) so loudness/density (feat.level half-life 0.8 s, feat.density follows with 0.25 s half-life) change outline size and number; sparse quiet music gets up to 2.1x bigger outlines (1+1.1*max(0,1-rate/0.4)*(1-level)); (2) fall speed zv uses feat.rate^2.2 (half-life 1.0 s) and feat.level, so busy playing makes the outlines flee faster and gives smeary walls; (3) the vanishing point and drift low-pass the melody/bass (0.625 s tau, 0.5*rate drift); (4) per-chord echo cap min(F.echoes, floor(36/notes)) and 220 objects cap (older ones removed); (5) a soft note after a loud one is dimmer via v only (no max-kick), but hardNote gating applies only below presence 1; (6) the feedback canvas keeps trails: each frame's fade/lighten means the previous outlines persist as walls by trail, so the attack is smeared into streaks (parallax 1.15 makes heads streak). Echo dims 0.62^i.
snapKnobs: trail (how long the walls linger): 0.05-1.5, half-life of the wall feedback in seconds; at the left, 'crisp, single outlines'; its drive is -density (denser music shortens it)
speed (how fast you fall): scales fall; faster = outlines leave the mouth sooner
presence: lowers ink and wall length (wallOf = 1-0.75*(1-pres)), calm, and limits to the hardest notes
spin (turning, drive +bass): turn rate, not timing
shape (which outlines) and palette: shape/colour only
howToSnap: Alert part is already good: new outline appears on the attack's own frame with a 0.09 s flash. To die faster: set the existing trail knob far left (0.05-0.12 gives a wall half-life of 0.05-0.12 s; at default 0.35 s the streaks are what blur the attacks), and shorten constants: exp(-o.age/3) -> ~exp(-o.age/0.7), hold tau 0.6 -> ~0.2, and the held-note trace exp(-(t-start)/2) -> removed or tau 0.3 (it is the only thing that follows note length, i.e. the unreliable pedal), flash tau 0.09 stays, surge tau 0.4 -> 0.15, kick tau 0.15 -> 0.08. A global scaling works partially: add a 'snap' multiplier s (default 1) dividing the taus 3, 0.6, 2, 0.4, 0.15 and multiplying trail, by s, plus the object life cap 10 s -> 10/s. Also cut the low pass in fold(): mouth from feat.level (0.8 s half-life) so a soft note after a loud note is small (a per-attack size from ch.vel instead of feat.level) and the rate^2.2 speed term. Make per-note legible by making echoes not scale with density.
risk: Feedback sim: the canvas itself is the state (snap canvas copy, wall decay b, vanishing point drift), so changing outline lifetimes changes the emergent corridor shapes and the zoom of what is already on the canvas; frame-dependent (dt) and uses window.NOTES for hardNote quantiles. A very short trail makes the picture strobe/flicker since the 'lighter' second pass (b>1) gives back the shared fade (b=pow(0.5,dt/(trail*wall))/0.88, trail<=0.05 hits a floor at b->0). The objects cap 220 and the fall speed from feat.rate means shortening life changes how many are on screen. Not deterministic against a seek: the feedback accumulates, and spin/surge/kick/vp are accumulated state, so seeks/renders have to run the history (not stateless like the tree). Clip fades interact with global alpha only. The widget is not in the scenes, so a default change is safe for Liebesleid / Rach 2.

onAttack: onChord(ch,x): (a) every live tip jerks forward in the same frame: kick = (3+15*vel/127)*spread/(1+0.35*x.rate)*(1+3*young*hard), with hard=(vel/127)^2, young=max(0,1-live/1500), and v1 += kick/0.09 (a burst that covers about kick px in total), v2 = min(60*S, v2 + surge) with surge=(7+45*young*hard)*S, and t.flash = max(flash, 0.6); (b) for the first 6 notes (not sorted): each note's x = (0.05+0.9*pitchT(m))*W; the nearest non-curling tip within 0.17*W (or any if maxTips reached) receives energy e = (16+430*min(d,1.6)^0.9)*(0.6+0.6*v/127)*(1.5-0.8*branch) *0.45, widens to the note's width, flash=1 and spawns a bud (a white dot, radius 1.8+0.8*w+v/60); else shoot() creates a new stem from the nearest stem or an edge; (c) a chord of 3+ notes forks the taker min(4,n-1)*min(1,1.8b) ways; newly created tips get the kick as well. In frame(), the tips' heads are drawn live with a glowing disc radius (0.5+..)*(1+1.3*flash), and the settled network repainted offscreen at 5 Hz except tips and wither fronts.
decay: Quote: t.v1 *= exp(-dt/0.09) (tau 0.09 s, the instantaneous jerk: kick/0.09 px/s integrates to ~kick px = 3-18 px, up to 4x when young and loud); t.v2 *= exp(-dt/1.1) (tau 1.1 s, the run-on: adds up to (7..52)*S*1.1 px, capped at 60*S px/s) on top of crawl = (9+26*health)*S px/s; t.flash *= exp(-dt/0.18) (tau 0.18 s) drives the head disc 'r*(1+flash*1.3)' and the 0.4*flash green glow of radius 2.4r; buds: q.a += dt, k = 1-a/0.5, alpha k*k, radius r*(0.9+0.6k), dropped at a>0.5 (0.5 s); tip energy t.e drains at (6+70*(1-health)) per s so a tip curls into a spiral when it runs out (health follows 0.55*rate+0.3*level+0.25*density with tau 2.5 s up, 5 s down). What the attack makes (stems) is not removed on release; it stays and withers slowly: new growth is acid green for 0.5 s, then 1.6 s, then ageing to viridian over AGE_T=20 s; stems start dying only after s.cl > 8 (ageing = wK*(0.1+2.2*thin^2) per s, i.e. tens of seconds to minutes), front speed fv = wK*(5+10*thin) points/s, ZONE=26 points, dust life 1.4-4 s, rem 18-52 s for dry ones.
lowPass: Strong low-pass on the music: (1) kick divides by (1+0.35*x.rate), so fast music (rate half-life 1.0 s) gets smaller jerks; (2) health smoothing (2.5 s up, 5 s down) sets the crawl speed and tip energy drain; (3) tips only exist up to maxTips = 3+round(46*b^2) (about 4-14 at default branch 0.45), so 'which note' is merged into the nearest tip within 0.17*W: many notes of a chord can land on the same tip (and only the last one 'taker' forks); (4) only the first 6 notes of a chord are used; (5) energy depends on the transcribed note length n.d (min(d,1.6)^0.9), which is unreliable with the pedal; (6) young/hard gating: the kick is mostly small once live>1500 points, since young->0 (a mature network barely jerks); (7) the jerk is distance not a position change, in px: kick (3..18 px) is about 0.1-0.6 s of crawl, hard to see among crawl 9-35 px/s; (8) the tip is moved in steps of 5 px (st) with the head interpolated, and settled lines repainted only every REPAINT=0.2 s (live parts excluded) so the visual response is the head glow rather than the line. No percentile ranking and no use of x.sounding().
snapKnobs: spread (how fast it spreads): scales kick, surge, crawl and cap v2 (0.05-3), at the right the jerk is bigger
branch (how readily it forks): maxTips and fork count, energy factor (1.5-0.8b)
curl: what a tip does when it runs out (spiral size/turns)
wither (how fast it withers; drive -level): speed of dying back
weight (thickness): line width and bud/head size
presence (leads): sets spread, wither and branch together
howToSnap: Alert: the jerk is already same-frame (v1 tau 0.09 s) but too small and then drowned by the continued crawl and by the long v2 (tau 1.1 s) run-on. Smallest change: (1) v2 tau 1.1 -> ~0.25 (k2 = exp(-dt/1.1) in growTips) and keep surge area by scaling (surge*1.1/0.25 would keep distance; or lower to shorten); (2) make the crawl between attacks smaller after an attack (crawl baseline (9+26*health)*S -> a fraction when no recent attack, e.g. multiply by 0.3+0.7*exp(-sinceAttack/0.5)) so the jerk reads against stillness; (3) raise kick (3+15*vel/127 -> bigger) and drop the /(1+0.35*rate) divisor; (4) head flash t.flash tau 0.18 -> ~0.08 and bud life 0.5 -> 0.2; (5) per-note: do not merge notes to one tip (allow up to one new tip per picked note, maxTips raise) and use ch.vel/n.v instead of n.d for energy. A global attack/decay scaling works only on the transient parts: scale k1, k2, flash and bud life by one factor (default 1) and the kick/surge distance by its inverse so travelled distance stays. It cannot make the stems 'die quickly' since stems are meant to persist (wither is minutes): the only things that can be made to die fast are flash, buds and the v1/v2 burst.
risk: The vine is stateful and uses Math.random() (not x.rnd) in newStem, shoot, advance and forks, so it is not deterministic against a seek or a render (renderFrameHash cannot be stable); the whole network (stems, occ grid, tips, dust, buds, live count) is accumulated state with a CAP=6500 point budget and wither dynamics tied to health; changing growth speeds changes how fast the screen fills (live > CAP triggers forced wither 'force' up to 34 fronts). The offscreen settled canvas repaints every 0.2 s except the live parts (sb = last-1 for tips), so an extremely short effect on the line itself would not show; only the head, buds and dust are drawn live. Not in the two scenes (no vine in liebesleid or rach-concerto-2), so default changes are safe for them, but stored knob values must keep their meaning (lab/README rule).

onAttack: onChord builds the limbs if the 'limbs' knob changed, then takes the loudest note (sorted by v), ranks its velocity against the whole song (rank(), a percentile) and computes a=(0.35+0.65*v^1.2)*(1-0.4*feat.rate). If clock>=nextJolt (or v>=0.85 and clock>=nextJolt-0.3) it 'jolts': shove(pitch*W,a,lazy) adds a velocity kick to every limb point's flesh spring qv (42*a*up/m*(0.25+0.75*exp(-d^2)), capped 60), flush+=0.7a, limb.fl+=1.1a (acid tint of the limb under the pitch), ask() maybe lifts a limb, and dimple() pushes up to 2 'sour smear' marks (radial gradient clipped to a limb). Otherwise the attack is ignored except swellT+=2.2a. Seen in its own frame: the smear colour and flush/fl tint appear in that frame at full strength (age 0, alpha 0.42); the bodies move via the spring, so the visible shape change builds over ~1 s (deliberately 'bodies do not land').
decay: Everything is deliberately slow. flush *= exp(-dt/0.28); limb.fl *= exp(-dt/0.45); marks: linear f=1-age/life, life=1.1-0.3*rate seconds (about 0.8-1.1 s), radius r=(50+70*v01)*(1-0.3*rate), gone when age>=life. Flesh spring q: qv += (((swell*up - q)+0.8*lap)*w*w - 2*w*qv)*h with w=1.25/sqrt(m), m=(0.7+0.9f)*(0.55+0.9*lazy) (about 0.5-1.4 for default lazy 0.5), a critically damped spring with natural freq ~1.1-1.8 rad/s, so a push shows over ~1 s and takes several seconds to die (settle time of order 4/w, 2.5-4 s). Swell: swellT *= exp(-dt/2.5); swell follows swellT with exp(-dt/1.6). Lift: lift T=(3.2+3f)*(0.6+1.4*lazy)*(1+0.6rate) s (about 4.5-9 s at lazy .5), hang until until=T+0.8..2.2 s, fall T=(1.8+1.6f)*(0.7+0.6lazy) s; ask gated by gapUntil=(4+12*lazy)*(1+1.5*rate) s and limb free time (6+14*lazy) s. Limb rest damping DAMP=3.4/s, pull time const (1.8 or 2.4)*sqrt(m); sink time const 22 s; slide 2.4 s; hl 1.5 s; yawn 8 s after 5 s quiet.
lowPass: Heavily gated and smoothed by design: nextJolt refractory = (0.9+1.6*rate)*(0.6+0.8*lazy)*rnd(0.8,1.3) s (about 0.7-3 s) after each jolt, so most attacks are ignored (they only feed swellT); a = ... * (1-0.4*feat.rate) damps busy music; ask() refuses unless velocity rank >= 0.35+0.4*lazy, only 1-2 limbs up, gapUntil 4-16+ s, and a random rate-based rejection; only the loudest note per chord is used (colour dimples use top 2); the flesh is a critically damped spring (low-pass ~1 s up, several s down); the fixed 1/60 s substep acc is clamped to 0.1 s. Intensity is by percentile rank of velocity across the song, not absolute.
snapKnobs: lazy: lower value shortens nextJolt refractory (0.6+0.8*lazy factor), lowers the ask threshold, and lightens mass m (0.55+0.9*lazy) so springs have higher w=1.25/sqrt(m) and respond/settle faster; this is the only existing knob that sharpens response
lift: height a lifted limb reaches (liftH), not timing
fat: amplitude of the landing squash and stain width, not timing
limbs: number of masses
green: palette only
presence: sets lift/fat/limbs less-values, not timing
howToSnap: Cheap partial snap: raise the colour channel only. Change dimple's life from 1.1-0.3*rate to ~0.25 s (marks[].life, line 118; and optionally alpha m.a 0.42->0.7), flush decay exp(-dt/0.28) to ~0.1 and fl decay exp(-dt/0.45) to ~0.12 (lines 366, 368); and remove the jolt gate for the colour part: move flush/fl/dimple out of the 'if (jolt)' branch so every attack (not only one per 0.9-2.5 s) lights its own spot, keeping shove/ask gated. That makes the colour alert and quick-dying while the heavy bodies stay slow. Making the bodies snap (the flesh spring w=1.25/sqrt(m) to e.g. 6-10 and the refractory nextJolt to ~0.1 s) would contradict the widget's identity (lazy mass) and its blurb; recommend leaving the bodies and snapping only the colour. A global attack/decay time scaling would NOT work cleanly: time constants are spread over spring physics, the 4-16 s gating, and 6-22 s settling in song seconds, and the lift/fall sequences are long set-pieces; scaling them would change gating/behaviour, not just sharpness. A scale applied only to the colour constants (0.28, 0.45, mark life) would work.
risk: Physics is a fixed 1/60 s verlet with persistent positions (px,py), qv springs and a seeded build from window.NOTES, plus x.rnd draws inside onChord (jolt gate, ask, dimple jitter, nextJolt) whose consumption order changes if the gating changes, so un-gating the colour path would shift random draws and change every later lift/gap decision (determinism between seek and live play is kept since x.rnd is seeded, but the whole sequence differs from today). Marks are drawn inside picture() via an offscreen 320x180 blurred wash with per-frame filter, so shortening marks is safe; the wash is repainted fully each frame (opaque ground fill) so there is no persistence to break. Note: widget paints its own opaque ground, hiding widgets beneath it.

onAttack: onChord pushes one mark per note via addNote (figs.push with age 0, type by pitch: pillar <46, zig/ring <62, coil <77, spark above; hold=min(4,q.d), life=max(hold+tail,0.14), tail=life_knob*(0.35+0.65v)*(1+1.2*(1-rate))), plus a 'burst' fig + flash + extra dirt on loud chords (ch.vel>=86 and relative to meanV, at most once per 0.3 s, flash once per 0.7 s), jitters all existing figs (x+-22*J, y+-14*J, ph), and sets cut=true and jump=max(jump, 2+6*J*clamp(vel/110)). In its own frame: cut forces filmFrame immediately in that same frame() call; a new mark with age<0.09 is drawn as a 'strike': overexposed (alpha base*1.3), scaled 1.1+0.08v, with a wide extra halo (HALO=0.5+0.8v), never dropped; the whole film wipes to black and every mark is re-scratched with a gate jump, so the attack is a hard cut.
decay: Already frame-snappy: the layer is wiped each film frame (fps knob 12 by default, i.e. every 1/12 s, plus a forced cut on every attack). Strike phase lasts f.age<0.09 s exactly (hard step). After the strike brightness = base*settle*R(0.7,1) with settle=0.62+0.38*exp(-age/0.3) (tau 0.3 s) while held. Mark visibility: end=1 while age<hold (the note length, up to 4 s), then linear ramp clamp((life-age)/max(0.06,min(0.35,(life-hold)*0.8))) over 0.06-0.35 s; whole mark ends at life=hold+tail where tail=life_knob(0.4 default)*(0.35+0.65v)*(1+1.2*(1-rate)) s, i.e. about 0.14-0.9 s after the note ends. Flash: flash*=0.25 per film frame (so gone within about 2-3 film frames, ~0.2 s at 12 fps). Burst fig life=0.2+0.2*b s, grows 0.7->1.15 over its first 0.1 s. Dirt: life R(0.4,2.5) s, burst dirt R(0.15,0.5) s. Random 7% dropped frames per mark. Bloom is a blurred copy of the same frame (no persistence). The shared canvas background fade does not matter much since it draws the layer with 'lighten' at alpha gain (0.86-1) each frame.
lowPass: None on attacks (every attack makes marks and cuts a frame immediately). Mild: burst rate-limit lastBurst 0.3 s and flash 0.7 s; size shrinks with feat.rate and chord size; tail lengthened in sparse music (1+1.2*(1-rate)); meanV is a slow average (0.06 per attack) deciding 'loud'; hold=min(4,q.d) makes a mark follow note length. Cap 70 figs.
snapKnobs: life: 'how long a mark stays after its note' (0..2, default 0.4, less 0): at 0 the tail is 0 and the mark ends at the note end (still min 0.14 s overall)
fps: how many film frames per second (6..24, default 12); a note always cuts a new frame regardless
burst: size of burst and flash on loud chords (0 = none)
wriggle: jitter amount and the attack jump (J)
presence: lowers life, burst and dirt together
howToSnap: Already close to the target. The remaining slowness is that a mark lasts for its note's written length (hold=min(4,q.d)) which is long for pedaled piano. Smallest change: add a cap such as hold=Math.min(hold, 0.25..0.4) in addNote (line 140), or a new knob 'hold cap' defaulting to 4, so the scratch dies about 0.3 s after the attack regardless of the transcribed note length; and shorten settle's tau 0.3 s (line 198) and strike window 0.09 s (line 194) if desired. Optional: raise default fps. A global attack/decay time scaling would work reasonably well here because all constants are explicit seconds (0.09, 0.3, 0.06-0.35, flash 0.25/frame, tail), but the strike window is already as sharp as a frame lets it be; scaling the hold is the real lever (and note it uses q.d, not x.sounding()).
risk: Uses Math.random (R()) throughout, not x.rnd, so it is not deterministic in song time: renders, seeks and live play will differ frame to frame by design (the film boil), and a render.html frame hash cannot be stable. Film frames are driven by an accumulator acc/fps plus forced cut on each attack, so changing fps or cut changes draw cadence; the layer canvas is cleared each film frame so there is no persistence to break; bloom is a quarter-size blurred copy regenerated each film frame. Changing hold/life changes how many figs are alive (cap 70) and so the dirt/flash behaviour only slightly. Draws with 'lighten' onto the shared canvas.

onAttack: onChord runs carry(ch,x), which for each note computes a lattice point (pitch by x, note name by y; a repeated note steps a few pixels aside) and adds pencil strokes (add(): s.age=-delay, dur=0.1+min(1,len/5200)*0.45) according to the current rule (corners, through, arcs, squares, sides, chain, centre), k=lines knob (default 3, drive -rate), colour by direction/anchor, lw=0.5+pencil*1.6, alpha 0.4+pencil*0.3; delay is ni*0.018 + j*0.01 (+ j*0.012 for squares lines). Each note also pushes a 'flash' {x,y,age,v}. onChord also may start a new wall (new section/rest>1.6 s/full wall) which cross-fades the old wall over 2.2 s. In its own frame the attack appears the same frame as a dark dot (radius 2+3k*min(1,v/100)) with a red expanding ring, and the strokes begin to draw out (growth e=1-(1-u)^3) from age 0 (after delay).
decay: There is no decay of the music's marks: lines are committed permanently into the wall buffer (multiply blend) and only vanish when a new wall begins (old wall fades over 2.2 s: prevA -= dt/2.2, drawn at alpha prevA^2). Transient attack parts: stroke grow-in over dur = 0.1+min(1,len/5200)*0.45 s (about 0.1-0.55 s, ease-out cubic); while drawing it is heavier and darker: lineWidth s.lw*(1+1.4*(1-u)), alpha min(1, al+0.4*(1-u)) with u linear in age/dur; flash dot: k=max(0,1-age/0.45) linear over 0.45 s (dot alpha 0.8k, radius 2+3k*v/100; red ring alpha 0.7*k^2, radius 4+14*(1-k)); a tiny permanent graphite dot 1.6 px, alpha 0.55 is laid at the point. Caption fade-in dt/1.2 s. The wall is repainted every frame (opaque WALL fill), so nothing depends on the shared fade.
lowPass: None on attacks, but strokes are delayed by ni*0.018 + j*0.01 s (and up to cnt*0.012 s across a squares block), capped at 90 strokes per chord; lines knob has drive -rate which reduces lines per note in busy music (k lower when feat.rate high); accumulated 900 active cap. Rule changes are rate limited by lastSwitch (4 s). Strokes growing from the point outward over 0.1-0.55 s are a soft attack (not instantaneous): long lines (corner to corner) take ~0.5 s to finish drawing.
snapKnobs: lines: lines per note (1..4; lower = fewer strokes, drive -rate)
pencil: line weight (drive +level)
full: lines before the wall is repainted
rule / colours / presence: rule choice, colours, and presence scaling lines and full
howToSnap: Alertness: the dot flash is already instantaneous but the strokes take up to ~0.55 s to draw: shorten dur in add() (line 79 region: s.dur = 0.1 + min(1,len/5200)*0.9*0.5) to something like 0.04 + min(1,len/5200)*0.12, and the ease-out cubic already front-loads it. Dying quickly: the flash decay 0.45 s (k=1-age/0.45) to ~0.15 s. But the widget is cumulative by design (the lines never die, the drawing piles up), so 'die off quickly' only applies to the transient overlay (heavier/darker fresh stroke, flash dot and ring), not the pencil lines, which are the artwork; making lines die would turn it into a different widget (needs a 'wall fades' knob rather than a snap). A global attack/decay time scaling could be applied cleanly to dur and the 0.45 flash and the heavy-fresh phase, since all are explicit constants, but should leave the 2.2 s wall fade and commit permanence alone.
risk: Strokes accumulate in off-screen buffers cur/prev (committed permanent lines, 900 cap in active); changing dur changes when strokes commit into cur (group-batched by col|lw|al), so a faster commit changes ordering of multiply blends only subtly. The wall is also the opaque ground (WALL fill each frame), hiding widgets beneath it. State persists across frames in cur/prev (not re-derivable per frame), though it is fully determined by the sequence of attacks; point() uses a module-level hits Map per note so repeats shift (state that must be reset on seek: reset() clears it). The rule picker uses window.NOTES length and x.t for seek-determinism. Uses x.rnd? No randomness in strokes; only deterministic note geometry.

onAttack: onChord pushes one shape el per note into els (kind arc <48, petal <76, bead above; age 0, a0=pitch class angle, f=radiusOf(m), v=max(v,40), d=clamp(nt.d,0.2,6), n copies=(k+1)*mirrors clamp 3..16, diss=dissonance vs sounding notes within 1.2 s), a flash ring {f,v,age} per note, sets kick=max(kick,(vel/127)*(0.025+0.05*low)*min(1.6,0.8+k*0.15)), core=max(core,vel/127), star=n. In its own frame the attack is immediate: shapes open with overshoot openOf(age)=1+3.4t^3+2.4t^2 (t=min(1,age/0.22)-1) over the first 0.22 s (reaches about 1.2 and settles to 1), white-hot colour mix HOT*0.8*max(0,1-age/0.4), rays from the centre out to each new shape along every copy (age<0.32 s), a ring flash at each note's radius (0.5 s), the whole figure radius kick, and the central star lit.
decay: Explicit time constants: kick *= exp(-dt/0.12) (the radius kick of Rb=R*breath*(1+kick)); core *= exp(-dt/0.5) (central star brightness and size); hot (white-hot) = max(0,1-age/0.4) linear over 0.4 s; rays: k=age/0.32, alpha (1-k)^1.5 over 0.32 s, start radius r0 moves 0.12->0.87 of r1 (k^2); flash rings: k=fl.age/0.5, alpha (1-k)^2, widen 7% over 0.5 s; pop overshoot 0.22 s; sounding shapes are fully alive for their whole note duration e.d (0.2-6 s from the note length); after the note ends (rel=age-d>0): alpha a=(1-rel/life)^1.4 with life knob default 3.5 s (drive -rate: shorter in busy music), fill drains exp(-rel/0.16) (0.16 s), outline lingers as lace; drift outward 9%*(1-a); radius of let-go shapes eases from Rb to Rs with exp(-rel/0.15); breath eases to size with exp(-dt/0.3); spin rot += dt*spin*0.55 (drive +rate). Elements are dropped when alpha<0.02 and age>=d; cap 180 els and 48 flashes.
lowPass: None on attacks (every note makes a shape immediately). The cap of 180 elements; crowd = min(1, sqrt(60/els.length)) dims lingering lace when many; kick uses max (not sum); share=1/sqrt(max(1,k/2)) divides ray brightness for big chords; breath eases to the size knob over 0.3 s (the size drive +level modulates the target through feat.level, which has 0.8 s half-life, so the size swell is slow); 'life' knob drive -rate shortens linger in busy music via feat.rate (1.0 s half-life). Shapes follow note length (e.d up to 6 s): a held petal grows with 'held' and fill stays while the note sounds, so for pedaled piano the 'attack' look lasts the transcribed note length.
snapKnobs: life: how long shapes stay after their note ends (0.3..8 s, default 3.5, drive -rate); at 0.3 the lace is gone quickly
size: overall size (+level drive swells on loud)
mirrors: copies per note
spin: turning speed (+rate)
jag: spikes on clashing notes
presence: scales mirrors, size and life
howToSnap: The attack side is already alert (instant overshoot, white-hot, rays, kick with tau 0.12 s). What makes it feel late/mushy is the sounding phase lasting the full note duration e.d (0.2-6 s) with fills and growth (petal length grows 1+0.5*min(held,3); arcs grow with held/2.5; beads string out with held*2.2), then life 3.5 s of lace. Smallest change: cap the live duration, e.g. d: Math.max(0.2, Math.min(nt.d, 6)) in onChord (line ~ 'd:') to Math.min(nt.d, ~0.35), and lower the default life or add a knob 'live cap'; shorten openOf window 0.22->0.12 and the hot 0.4 s, rays 0.32 s, flashes 0.5 s, core tau 0.5 s. Existing x.sounding() is used only for dissonance. A global attack/decay time scaling would work well because the constants are explicit seconds in frame(): scale 0.22/0.4/0.32/0.5/0.5/0.12/0.16/0.15 together, and clamp e.d.
risk: State is a list of els and flashes aged with dt (deterministic, no randomness, no precomputed plan; only reads x.sounding() and x.feat). The canvas is translated to the centre via g.translate without save/restore (relies on the host resetting the transform each frame); fills build up over frames because the shared 12% fade is used, so shortening fill/live times changes how much accumulation of fill (the code comments warn soft fills must be faint to stay see-through). The 'lighter' composite for rays/flashes must be reset to source-over (it is). Capping d changes dissonance only via near set (unchanged) but changes how long fill stays: visual weight on the canvas will drop noticeably. Note the opposite constraint: no persistence besides the shared fade.

onAttack: onChord builds ink rings for each note (up to 6 notes thinned from the chord): per note a clear-water ring (radius^2 R2*GAP^2 with GAP=0.45) and an ink ring (radius^2 R2), each created as a tiny circle (0.6 px) then immediately pushed by drop(px,py,r2*INST) with INST=0.6, i.e. 60% of the drop's area appears on the attack frame; R2 shares Rc^2 across notes weighted by loudness and low pitch, Rc = drop*(40+220*loud^1.6)*...capped at RMAX 270*drop and by an area-rate budget AMAX=0.45*W*H. The remaining 40% blooms later in frame(). Also may start a comb stroke (on a new phrase, accent, or every `every` attacks) and moves the pen (a phrase walks across the bath). Seen in its own frame: the drop is on screen at the attack frame at ~77% of final radius (sqrt 0.6), with a fresh-strike flash (flash=1+(0.35+0.8*loud)*fl^2 colour brighten, plus a cream rim stroke of width 1+2.5*loud*fl, alpha (0.15+0.5*loud)*fl*strike) fading over 0.35 s; the older ink is instantly displaced outward by the area-preserving push.
decay: The ink itself does not decay with a time constant per attack: it persists up to LIFE=16 s of 'ink age', where ink age advances at dt*(0.35+1.4*feat.rate) (so 16 s of ink age is about 11-46 s of song time depending on how busy the music is, 0.35x in sparse passages), brightness f=(1-age/16)^1.3; also removed if it leaves the bath or the total point count exceeds CAP=11000 (oldest first) or a later bath-wide sheet of ink covers it. Attack-specific transients: the rest of the bloom: e=1-(1-u)^3 over dur=0.14+0.1*min(1,n.d) s (about 0.14-0.24 s; the clear-water ring takes 0.6x that); strike flash fl = max(0,1-fresh/0.35) (0.35 s linear, squared in brightness); comb stroke duration max(0.25,min(1.1,2.2*ioi)) s with e=1-(1-u)^2.4 and tines glow al=glow*(1-u)^2; areaRate *= 0.5^(dt/0.7) (a 0.7 s half-life budget); vortex follows with 0.8 s half-life; ioi/slowGap/fastGap smoothers.
lowPass: Several: per-chord and per-second ink area caps (areaRate budget with 0.7 s half-life shrinks drops by up to 0.45x when loud notes follow quickly); phrase detection via ioi smoother (ioi += (gap-ioi)*0.1/0.25), velMean 0.12 smoother and fastGap/slowGap smoothers (0.5 and 0.05) deciding phrase/section/accent; accent requires vel>=velMean+14 and >=60 or >=100, with a 0.35 s refractory; comb every `every` attacks=max(3,round(16-9*combing)); notes thinned to 6 per chord; ink ages with the music (rate-dependent), vortex 0.8 s half-life. The drop size is driven by absolute velocity (and relative to the last few chords: rel in 0.85+0.3*rel), not by a percentile rank.
snapKnobs: drop: drop size (0.1..1.8, default 1, less 0.3); below 0.4 'calm' also fades the comb pull, tine glow and strike halo
combing: how often and hard the comb rakes (0..1.5, default 0.6, drive +rate)
twist: swirl by bass (drive +bass)
fill: lines vs solid (affects how the strike and fill show)
palette: ink colours
presence: sets drop and combing
howToSnap: The attack is already immediate (77% of the drop on the attack frame). Dying quickly is the problem: ink stays 16 s of ink time (11-46 s real) and is permanent artwork, so there is no 'decay' to shorten without changing the nature of the picture. A snap variant would need a new knob (e.g. 'ink life' scaling LIFE=16 and the rate coupling 0.35+1.4*rate), plus shorter fl strike (0.35 -> 0.12) and a brighter stronger flash and shorter bloom dur 0.14+0.1*n.d (use fixed 0.06); but the real snap is to make the transient (the fresh drop flash and rim) the visible event and let the ink age fast (e.g. LIFE=3 s). A global attack/decay time scaling would only partly work: the long-lived marbling bath is cumulative geometry (deformations of existing rings), not an envelope, so scaling the bloom/flash/comb durations is safe but scaling LIFE changes how much of the bath remains.
risk: A genuinely stateful fluid-like geometry simulation: rings of polylines are deformed in place by drop(), rake() and stir() (area-preserving pushes applied incrementally across frames: the 40% bloom and comb strokes apply increments e-s.e each frame so the sum is exact), resampled each frame, with global caps (CAP, area budget). The result depends on all history and on the order of pushes, so changing durations (bloom dur, comb dur) changes the final geometry slightly even though the totals match; changing LIFE or removal changes the older-ink layering and which 'bg' sheets cover what. It uses x.rnd (seeded) for positions, so determinism holds in song time, but the consumption order of x.rnd must not change. Stats() is used by test scripts. Cost scales with total points (CAP 11000). The widget paints bath fill opaque rects for bg rings.

onAttack: onChord, for each note, computes its band b=floor(semiOf(m)/6) (10 bands, bass at the bottom) and raises that band's target inkT[b] = 1-(1-inkT[b])*(1-a), with a=clamp(0.42*quiet(v)*mark*(0.7+0.3*min(1,d/0.6))), where quiet(v)=clamp((108-v)/50,0.06,1) (soft notes count fully, fff about 0.06) and mark default 0.6 (drive -level). It is a gentle, one-sided target: no new object is made. In its own frame the shown band ink[b] rises toward the target with rise = 1-0.5^(dt/0.09) (half-life 0.09 s). Also held notes (sounding for >=0.25 s) tint their semitone stripe via x.sounding() in frame (not in onChord).
decay: Target decay: inkT[b] *= fall where fall = 0.5^(dt/(stay*0.45)), stay default 10 s (drive -rate), so the target's half-life is 4.5 s at defaults (range 0.45 s at stay=1 to 9 s at stay=20); the shown ink ease rise has half-life 0.09 s (so it also follows the fall with that lag). Stripe tint: held target tg=clamp(quiet(v)*mark*1.5), rises with up=1-0.5^(dt/0.7) (half-life 0.7 s, only after the note has sounded for 0.25 s), falls with tfall=0.5^(dt/(stay*0.3)) (half-life 3 s at stay=10). The resting wash breathes with period 53 s (+-12%). Final alpha: ink[b]*markA (0.5-0.62), so the visible pulse is a faint wash.
lowPass: By design a heavy low-pass: loud notes (the interesting attacks) are almost ignored (quiet(v) down to 0.06); amplitude is a combination 1-(1-inkT)(1-a) saturating; ink eases toward the target with 0.09 s half-life (slight smoothing of the attack); the stripe tint appears only after a note has sounded 0.25 s and rises with a 0.7 s half-life; drive '-level' on the mark knob reduces marking in loud music; stay drive '-rate' shortens linger in busy music. Its decay is slow (4.5 s half-life) and the whole picture is meant to be quiet.
snapKnobs: stay: how long a mark stays (1..20 s, default 10, less 2.5, drive -rate); at the left end half-life is 0.45 s
mark: how strongly a note deepens its band / tints its stripe (default 0.6, drive -level)
wash: resting colour of the bands
grid / paper: static look
presence: lowers mark, stay and grid
howToSnap: Not intended to be snappy (it is 'a quiet widget for quiet music'); the response is a faint band wash, so snapping it would change its character. If wanted anyway: raise a (the 0.42 multiplier, line in onChord) and make quiet(v) not suppress loud notes (e.g. floor 0.06 -> 0.5) so loud attacks show; make the rise 0.09 s half-life even shorter (0.03) and the fall faster (fall half-life stay*0.45 -> stay*0.05, i.e. stay=1 gives 0.05 s), and drop the 0.25 s delay for stripe tint to 0.04 s with up half-life 0.7 -> 0.1 s and tfall stay*0.3 -> stay*0.05. Most of this is reachable through existing knobs: stay at its minimum 1 gives a 0.45 s half-life for bands and 0.3 s for stripes, and mark at 1. A global attack/decay time scaling would work cleanly because every constant is an explicit half-life (0.09, 0.7, stay*0.45, stay*0.3), but loudness suppression (quiet) is the real obstacle to individual-note snappiness for loud piano attacks, and band granularity (10 bands of 6 semitones) means single notes are not distinguishable (a note only deepens its band, the semitone stripe appears only when held >=0.25 s).
risk: Paints its own opaque canvas (ground drawImage each frame), hiding widgets drawn before it. State is only ink/inkT/tint arrays updated with dt (deterministic, no randomness except fixed ICON.rng seeds for static layers); static ground/grid/strip canvases are cached by knob-key and rebuilt when day/grid knobs move. 'time' accumulates for the 53 s breath (depends on wall dt, not song time exactly but fine). Home key computed from window.NOTES. Changing the quiet() mapping changes the picture for the existing quiet pieces it was designed for (chorale, oboe cadenza); stripe tint depends on x.sounding() note lengths, which are unreliable under pedal.

onAttack: onChord computes vel=loud(ch.vel) (velocity against the recording's 93rd-percentile note velocity) and power=clamp((vel-40)/70,0,1); a single non-big note tears one thin horizontal slice (tear(...,{slice:true}), w=W*R(.3,.95), h=R(3,12)*(1+power), offset mag=jump*(16+150*power*0.8)*R(.4,1)) with probability min(1,amount); otherwise k=floor(amount*power^2*n^1.1*2.4) random-note rectangles are torn out of the picture, plus 1-2 full-width inverted 'difference' bands when 'big'. In its own frame a torn block is shown displaced at once (age<0.12 holds e=1) with a bright 1px seam, a red/bone colour-split ghost and sometimes a frozen copy; the attack is visible in the very frame it happens, and the base bars of sounding notes flash white-hot for 0.15 s.
decay: Tear offset: e = age<0.12 ? 1 : Math.exp(-3*(age-0.12)/settle); settle default 1.6 s so tau = settle/3 = 0.53 s (knob range 0.15-5 s gives tau 0.05-1.7 s); block removed at age >= 0.12+settle*1.6 = 2.68 s (0.36 s at settle 0.15). Shown offset is stepped, not smooth: each frame it catches up with probability 1-Math.exp(-dt*11) (about every 0.09 s) in 4 px steps. Frozen fragment alpha min(1,e*1.6); seam alpha 0.55*min(1,e*1.5)*(0.4+0.6*power); colour split s=round(split*(0.4+0.6*e)) only while age < 0.15+settle*0.8 (1.43 s), alpha al*min(1,e*2). Base bars: own canvas cleared by destination-out alpha 1-Math.pow(0.5, dt/(0.25+BASE*2.2)) = half-life 1.9 s; struck flash fl=max(0,1-held/0.15) so 0.15 s; the bars are redrawn every frame while the note sounds (x.sounding()). Inverted band: drawn once, then only the shared 0.12/frame fade (~0.09 s half-life). energy accumulator (run of loud attacks) halves every 0.4 s: energy*Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.4).
lowPass: Mild gating, no smoothing of the pulse. (1) 'big' needs vel>=92&&n>=3, or vel>=98&&n>=2, or vel>=104, or energy>2.6 (energy = running sum with 0.4 s half-life, only vel>=85 attacks add power*sqrt(n)); resets to 0 after a big one. (2) Count k scales with power^2, so soft chords tear almost nothing. (3) The 0.12 s hold, then the choppy stepped catch-up (rate 11/s) delays and quantises the return. (4) Random placement: Math.random picks which of the chord's notes tears, 30 % land anywhere. (5) jump has drive '+level', so the shared 0.8 s half-life level pulse scales the throw distance. (6) block cap 64. No percentile ranking per attack beyond loud().
snapKnobs: settle (how long until it heals, 0.15-5 s, default 1.6): the one exponent time constant tau = settle/3 and the lifetime 0.12+1.6*settle; at 0.15 a tear lives 0.36 s
jump (how far they jump, 0-2, default 0.9, drive +level): amplitude of the displacement
amount (how many tears, 0-3, default 1.2): number of pieces per attack and probability of the single-note slice
size, form: shape and size of the torn pieces
presence: moves jump, amount and settle together via their 'less' values (0.35, 0.2, 0.4)
howToSnap: Already decays fast through settle (turn it to about 0.2-0.3 and tears live under 0.5 s); the hardcoded constants that blunt the snap are: the 0.12 s hold (line 156: age < 0.12 ? 1), the stepped catch-up probability 1-Math.exp(-dt*11) (line 158), the base-bar fade half-life 0.25+BASE*2.2 = 1.9 s (line 133) which leaves the picture 'lit' for seconds, and the split cut-off 0.15+settle*0.8. Making them knob- or scale-able (hold 0.12 -> 0.03, catch-up rate 11 -> 40, bar fade 1.9 -> 0.4) would make it fully snappy; a global time-scale factor on those four constants plus settle would work directly on this widget without touching its look at default scale 1. Big/power gating (vel>=85 etc.) is separate and would still make soft single notes show only a thin slice.
risk: Uses Math.random (not x.rnd) throughout, so tears are not deterministic between renders (not pixel-reproducible); a persistent base-bar canvas (bc) with its own fade; 'snap' canvas copy of the shared canvas every frame (needs real canvas size and supersample S); frozen-fragment copies are taken at the attack time; the colour-split is the costly part and is gated by age; loud() caches VQ from window.NOTES on first call; shortening the hold/fade changes how many tears are on screen at once (cap 64) and the cost; the 'difference' band must be drawn once (a longer or repeated draw strobes).

onAttack: onChord makes every existing block bank hop=x.p('hop')*(0.45+0.65*min(1.3,(vel/100)^1.2)) of a step and hop by whole steps (acc += hop; k=floor(acc); tgt += k*cell*d); then for each of up to 8 notes (lowest first) drops a new square block (with a trail of up to 3 for loud or long notes) where the note's pitch column crosses its circle-of-fifths row, or if one is already there sets near.lit=1 and resets its age; it also sets the lane glow gv/gh to 0.45; loud big chords (score=(vel/100)^3*(1+min(8,n)) >= 8.5-6.8*flash, flashCool 0.22 s) land a large coloured plane on a crossing and set both lane glows to 1. In its frame the new block appears at full size in white (lit=1) in the same frame.
decay: Struck flash: b.lit *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.09), half-life 0.09 s (tau 0.13 s); the block is drawn WHITE while lit>0.45, so the white lasts 0.09*log2(1/0.45)=0.10 s, then its own colour; size is multiplied by (1+0.25*lit). Hop motion: b.pos += (b.tgt-b.pos)*(1-Math.exp(-dt*24)), tau 0.042 s (settled in ~0.15 s). Lane glow: gk=Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.32), half-life 0.32 s; beads drawn while glow > 0.05, so a 0.45 glow shows for 0.32*log2(9)=1.0 s (a 1.0 flash for 1.4 s), emptying bead by bead against a hash threshold. Block life: age < life, default 6 s (knob 1-12 s), full size until 75 % of life then linear shrink to 0 over the last 25 % (1.5 s at 6 s). A re-struck block has age=min(age,0.2) reset (its life is renewed). Planes: size s=min(1,age/0.06) (0.06 s grow-in) held until 65 % of life then linear shrink over 35 %; life = 1.3+1.6*rand*big, so about 1.3-4.6 s (big up to 1.3).
lowPass: Mild. The hop is accumulated across attacks (acc), so with hop 0.6 the traffic moves a step on roughly 2 of 3 attacks (hop knob has drive '+rate'). flashCool 0.22 s between planes. A note landing on an existing block only lights it (no new block). 420-block cap. Lit and glows are max-kicked (gv=max(gv,0.45)), not summed. No percentile ranking, no hesitation.
snapKnobs: life (how long blocks stay, 1-12 s, default 6): lifetime of blocks; at 1 a block is gone in 1 s with 0.25 s shrink
hop (how far they jump on each note, 0-2, default 0.6, drive +rate): amount of travel per attack
flash (big-chord flashes, 0-1, default 0.7): how easily planes land and their size
lanes (6-16): grid density
presence: moves lanes, hop, life and flash together via 'less' values (6, 0.15, 1.2, 0.1)
howToSnap: Already quite alert (white strike in the same frame, 0.04 s glide, 0.09 s flash half-life). What keeps it from being snappy is the slow stuff that remains on screen: block life (6 s knob, pile of up to 420 squares), lane-glow half-life 0.32 s (line 322, gk), plane life 1.3-4.6 s, and the hop acc (<1 step per attack). Minimal change: a time-scale factor on gk (0.32 -> 0.1), lk (0.09, keep), ease 24 -> 40, plane life -> 0.5-1 s, and life default via knob (already exposed: set to ~1.5 s). A global attack/decay scaling would work on this widget with those four constants multiplied (it is almost entirely made of per-frame exponentials and linear ages).
risk: Block count/cap (420) and the 'traffic wraps around' positions depend on the accumulated hop, so shortening life changes the picture density; Math.random decides colours and plane choice (not deterministic across renders); grid G is rebuilt (blocks and planes dropped) when lanes or width change; flashCool is a song-time counter reset in reset(); background is a full opaque fill each frame (no trails to rely on).

onAttack: onChord takes only the chord's TOP note: it sets the stroke's target pitch offset mel.offT=(top.m-mean)*leap, press=0.3+0.7*(min(1,v/112))^1.3, resets since=0 (which restarts the speed and width envelopes) and reloads the bristles with ink; accompaniment below the line (top.m<melTop-9 within 0.9 s) instead makes an ink dot (a teardrop gesture, dur 0.12 s) under the stroke. If no phrase is running it starts a new one. Strong chords (loud>=106-40*gestures, n>=3 or n>=2 with +6) lay a red slash (gesture dur 0.13-0.2 s, laid immediately) or after a pause/long chord an ensō (dur 0.8-1.05 s). In its frame the stroke is already drawing; the attack shows as a sudden speed-up and a width swell, not as a new object.
decay: Speed: SPAN*(0.28+1.1*Math.exp(-m.since/0.3)) with SPAN=130: 179 px/s at the attack falling with tau 0.3 s to 36 px/s. Width target: wt = 32*size*press*(0.3+0.7*Math.exp(-m.since/0.6))/(1+speed/450), with tau 0.6 s; actual width follows m.w += (wt-m.w)*min(1,dt/0.05), a 0.05 s smoother. Pitch offset follows m.off += (m.offT-m.off)*(1-Math.exp(-dt/tau)), tau = 0.012+0.7*0.6*0.6 = 0.264 s. Ink on the page: layer faded every 0.25 s by destination-out alpha 1-Math.exp(-fadeAcc/stay), stay default 8 s (knob 1-30), so tau 8 s; strokes are never redrawn, they stay drawn and dry away. Held note ink pooling begins at since>0.3 s. A phrase ends (flick gesture) when since > 3 s (note sounding) or 1.6 s (nothing sounding), or at the screen edge. Bristle ink runs out with distance (b.ink -= seg*dry*0.0024*dep), so streaks appear along the stroke, not in time.
lowPass: Strong smoothing by design. (1) One continuous phrase per melody: a new attack changes the direction/width of an existing stroke rather than creating anything (no per-note object). (2) Pitch offset has a 0.264 s tau, the width a 0.05 s tau and a 0.6 s decay: a note shows as a swell lagging 0.05 s and fading over about 1 s. (3) mean pitch follows with mean += (top.m-mean)*0.12 (0.35 when no phrase). (4) accompaniment filter: notes >9 semitones below the line within 0.9 s are not melody. (5) slash/ensō gating: clock-lastGest>0.4, ensō cooldown 6 s, loudness percentile via loud(). (6) only the top note of a chord is used. (7) size has drive '+level', dryness '+rate'.
snapKnobs: stay (how long the ink stays, 1-30 s, default 8, less 1.5): ink layer decay time
size (brush size, 0.3-3, default 1.2, drive +level): stroke width and slash width
dryness (0-1, default 0.3, drive +rate): how broken the stroke is
gestures (0-1, default 0.5): how many strong chords add a slash
leap (2-24, default 5): pitch-to-height gain
presence: moves stay, size, gestures via 'less' values (1.5, 0.5, 0.05)
howToSnap: It is fundamentally a continuous brush, not an attack-envelope widget, so a pure scaling is partial. The hardcoded constants that would need to change: speed decay 0.3 s and its 1.1 gain (line ~170), width decay 0.6 s and smoother 0.05 s, the pitch smoother SMOOTH=0.6 (tau 0.264 s), and per-attack ink dabs. To make it snappy: SMOOTH 0.6 -> ~0.1 (tau 0.019 s), width decay 0.6 -> 0.15 s, speed decay 0.3 -> 0.1 s, plus per-note dab/stamp for every chord note (new) rather than only the top. A global attack/decay scale could multiply these three time constants without changing defaults; slashes and dots are already instant (0.12-0.2 s).
risk: Ink is painted once into a persistent layer (lay) with bristle state (ink, dist, noise) and only the layer fade removes it, so any change in the envelope must act on the paint, not on a redrawn object; uses Math.random (R) throughout, not x.rnd, so nothing is deterministic or seekable (a render or seek will not reproduce the same strokes); stroke state depends on the full history since the phrase started (mel, mean, melTop, lastMel, clock as module state) and clock/dt-based accumulation; gesture sub-stepping (every ~6 px, max 30) is tied to dt; fade is stepped every 0.25 s so very short stay values step visibly.

onAttack: onChord (keep=0, the default) calls lands(ch,x) and, only on the hardest attacks (vel above a per-song percentile bar, spaced by cutAt: every 3 to 20 s, always true for sparse music or an attack more than 2 s after the previous), land(): sets meltAge=0, draws n=round(drips*(1-keep)*(8+2*min(6,notes))) falling drips from above, makes one slashing cut at once (the canvas is copied and the two sides are redrawn shifted by d=(14+(vel-90)*2.2)*gap along a random line, shake=14*shake, a scar line pushed) and stores a copy 'held' of the cut picture to melt over the live one. Between strikes the widget draws nothing and copies nothing. The strike is seen in its own frame: cut, jolt and scar all appear at once.
decay: Melt: u=1-meltAge/MELT_LONG with MELT_LONG=1.1 s; extra melt speed melt*(1-keep)*MELT_KICK*u*u with MELT_KICK 2.6 and melt default 2.2 (a quadratic ease-out, finished at 1.1 s); the held ghost has alpha 0.95*(1-keep)*u*u*min(1,melt/2.2) and run=melt*MELT_KICK*60*MELT_LONG/3*(1-(1-u)^3). Jolt: shake *= Math.pow(0.86, dt*60), so half-life 0.077 s (tau 0.11 s), stops below 0.3 px; jolt starts at 14*shake px. Scar line: alpha al=max(0,1-age/0.9), line width 1+5*al, so linear over 0.9 s. Drips: d.y += d.v*dt; d.v *= 1+0.6*dt, start v 200-420 px/s accelerating, off screen in about 1.5-2 s (they are removed at y>H+60). The columns slide sp=(1+sin..)*melt*dt*60 px/frame.
lowPass: Heavy gating, by design. lands() rejects most attacks: the picture rests for 0.6*spacing after a strike (spacing = 3 s*(20/3)^((cutAt-80)/38); cutAt default 92 -> about 4.6 s; so no strike for about 2.8 s after one), then only attacks above a velocity bar (the hardest fraction giving about one per spacing from the song's CHORDS velocities), with the bar falling the longer it has rested ('starved'). Sparse music (<=4 chords or <=1 per 1.5 s) lets every attack land; an attack >2 s after the previous one always lands. 'keep' crossfades to the old always-on behaviour. This is a ranked, spaced gate, plus no smoothing of the strike itself.
snapKnobs: cutAt (which attacks strike, 80-118, default 92, less 108): the threshold and spacing; lower means more strikes
melt (0-6, default 2.2, less 0.7): how far the picture slides, and with it the ghost strength
drips (0-1, default 0.5, less 0.1): number of drips
gap (0-3, default 1): shear distance of the cut
shake (0-2, default 1): jolt
keep (0-1, default 0): crossfade to the old continuous casket
presence: moves melt, drips, cutAt through 'less' values (0.7, 0.1, 108)
howToSnap: The strike itself is already instant and short (cut and jolt immediate, jolt half-life 0.077 s, melt over 1.1 s, scar 0.9 s). The constants that could be tightened are MELT_LONG (1.1 s) and the u*u easing (0.9 s scar, 0.86^(60*dt) shake). A global decay scale would work directly on MELT_LONG, scar life 0.9 and the shake base 0.86 (line 153). The real obstacle to 'reacts to each note' is the gate lands(): it is built to suppress most attacks, so to make it snap to individual picked notes a mode would have to bypass it (the same effect as keep/ALONE: for sparse picks, 'h.sparse' is already true and every attack lands). Because it lives in the Rach 2 show it must stay opt-in (new knob, default = today).
risk: In rach-concerto-2 it sits over the other widgets and 'melts' whatever is on the canvas (it copies the canvas each frame while melting), so changes to MELT_LONG or timings change what the other widgets look like under it; heard() caches song = vels/rate from the global CHORDS once per page (not per instance in the lab, so a picks-routed instance still uses song CHORDS when CHORDS is the part's); module-level state (meltAge, phase, lastHit, held) is shared by instances; the 'held' canvas copy is taken at the strike and the pixel-identical render proof (renderFrameHash) would change if any default constant moves; x.rnd is used for most randomness (cut position, drips) but Math.random picks red drips and keep behaviour; the shake translate is applied with g.translate that is not undone inside the widget (relies on the host resetting it).

onAttack: onChord, for each note in the chord, buds a new Voronoi cell (power-diagram seed, x by pitch over the song range, y by the chord's row from a golden-ratio step, weight starting at -45000 = no area) or, if the same key is still open, re-flares that cell (pulse=max(pulse,..), lit=0, kern raised). It sets hit=max(hit, vel/115), and for loud attacks (amp=((vel-55)/55)^1.4 > 0.02) pushes a travelling ring of light (wave) from the chord's centre. In its frame the cell grows from a point to full weight over SPLIT_T=0.38 s (ease), swells its neighbours aside, shows a pale inset 'kernel' and thickens and blackens the border at once.
decay: Pulse (the swell and border): s.pulse *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.22) (half-life 0.22 s); the visible swell s.sw follows pulse with half-life 0.035 s on the way up and down (1-Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.035)); border width 1.2+(1-fill)*1.3+edge*(7*flare+2.5*hit), flare=clamp(pulse); border darkness dark=clamp(edge*(0.8*flare+0.35*hit)). Global hit: hit *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.16) (half-life 0.16 s). Fill brightness: bright = Math.exp(-s.lit/GLOW) with GLOW=1.1 s (tau 1.1 s); fill alpha has a 0.42+0.5*exp(-lit/1.1) term and 0.55+0.45*sounding. Kernel: s.kern eases to 0.34 while sounding with half-life 0.25 s, to 0 after the note ends with half-life 0.18 s; kernel alpha clamp(kern/0.22)^2, so it is gone about 0.4-0.5 s after the note ends. Size: s.sz eases (half-life 0.25 s) down to 0.6 of size when the note ends. A cell closes after its note ends plus stay (default 2 s, knob 0-5): then dying += dt/MERGE_T with MERGE_T=0.7 s (ease), colour washes into the nearest neighbour. Ring of light: radius grows at WAVE_V=760 px/s, width WAVE_W=90 px, amplitude amp*exp(-d^2/WAVE_W^2)*(1-r/1500); gone after 1500/760 = 1.97 s. Drift T += dt*(0.4+drift) (slow, 26 px/s).
lowPass: Moderate. (1) The swell is driven by the pulse, which decays with half-life 0.22 s and is max-kicked (pulse=max, not a sum). (2) The cell weight is eased to its target over 0.38 s for birth and by half-life 0.25 s (sz), and the neighbours' reaction is spread by power-diagram geometry (everything moves continuously). (3) A re-struck key within an open cell only re-flares (no new cell). (4) MAXN=40: the oldest open cells close first. (5) The kernel follows the note's length (n.d via s.end = ch.t+max(0.3,n.d)), so brightness is tied to the note ending (cells follow note lengths through the chord data, but not x.sounding()). (6) The ring only for vel>55ish and it fades along its path; the 'edge' knob drives '+level' from the shared 0.8 s pulse. No percentile ranking.
snapKnobs: edge (how hard attacks land, 0-2, default 1, drive +level): size of the swell, border thickness/darkness, ring brightness
stay (how long cells linger, 0-5 s, default 2, less 0): the time a cell remains after its note ends before closing; 0 = closes at once
drift (0-2, default 0.6, drive +rate): the slow current
pebble (0-1, default 0.25): cell gaps and rounding (changes geometry, no timing)
fill (0-1, default 0.85): solid vs outline
presence: moves stay and similar via 'less'
howToSnap: Already per-note and fairly alert (a cell flares in the very frame), but the swell/border response decays with half-life 0.22 s (line 208), the cell growth takes 0.38 s (SPLIT_T) and the closing 0.7 s (MERGE_T), and a cell is held for 'stay' 2 s after the note ends. Minimal: pulse half-life 0.22 -> ~0.08 s, hit half-life 0.16 -> 0.06, SPLIT_T 0.38 -> 0.1, MERGE_T 0.7 -> 0.25, stay -> 0 to 0.3; GLOW 1.1 -> 0.3. A global time scale would work on these constants (they are all independent exponentials/linear ramps); stay is already a knob. The cell's long life is the largest 'smear' because it lingers as a coloured tile in the mosaic.
risk: Geometry is a power diagram recomputed every frame (cost O(n^2) with up to 52 seeds) and its look depends on the cell weights evolving continuously, so a very short SPLIT_T/MERGE_T makes cells jump (visible pops, flicker and polygons appearing without area growth); drift uses a global T clock; module-level seeds/waves/tint state; colours use window.NOTES (study()) for the home key and range; cells close early only through stay (>=0) and MAXN; outlined mode relies on slow motion to avoid stacked trails; fill uses black wash for outline mode; it is deterministic through x.rnd (cell placement) but uses song time x.t for sounding; shortening lifetimes affects how many cells are alive (MAXN) and so the whole mosaic layout.

onAttack: onChord -> attack(): song=x.t; ranks the chord's force (vel*(1+0.07*min(8,n-1))) among the song's chords (fr, a percentile); may move the goal; then 'kicks' shapes: for a big or very loud chord (many>=5 or fr>0.95, at most every 0.42 s) every shape gets kick(); otherwise hits = max(n, ceil(crowd*(0.08+0.4*fr^2+0.3*gap+0.02*rate)*...)) shapes chosen by pitch (budget gate) get kick(). kick() sets vertical velocity vy=-sqrt(2*G*(h-above)), where h=(16+210*loud^1.9)*disorder*..., random vx and spin w, sqV squash, and s.next=song+rnd(0.08,0.34)*dope (a late reaction); the loudest also tilt the floor (jolt=16). In its frame (a 120 Hz rigid-body physics step) the shape leaves the floor in the same frame: velocity change is immediate, the visible motion is a hop.
decay: Gravity G=2600 px/s^2 so a loud hop of ~226 px rises/falls in about 0.53 s total (airtime = 2*vy/G); a landing squash via spring: s.sqV += (-540*sq - 6.5*sqV)*h (a damped oscillator, damping 6.5/s, so settles over about 0.5-1 s); spin damping on the floor Math.exp(-h*0.9) per second (or 2.2+10*calm when settled), horizontal Math.exp(-h*(1.3+8*calm)), global s.w *= Math.exp(-h*0.15) (tau 6.7 s); quiet = clamp((song-max(kicked,lastGoal))/0.85,0,1), so the crowd 'calms' over 0.85 s; kick latency s.next = song + 0.08-0.34 s * dope (dope 0.6-1.5, one shape 2.6) before a shape starts its return crouch; crouch (0.15-0.1*panic)*rnd(0.7,1.3)*dope/rush seconds; shapes then hop back to the goal line (repeated hops of 0.3-0.6 s each) until content, which can take several seconds; floor tilt: tiltV += (-46*tilt - 3.4*tiltV)*SUB (underdamped spring, period 0.93 s, decay tau 0.59 s); jolt *= exp(-SUB*14) (tau 0.07 s). float (reduced gravity after a long note) = long*0.25 s.
lowPass: Heavy. (1) Percentile ranks: fr and rankIn(velsN, q.v) turn velocity into a rank within the song, so equal notes give different strength by position in the piece. (2) Budget: budget = min(9, budget + dt*(4+1.3*rate)) and each kick costs 1 (except when fr>=0.75), so in dense music only so many get through. (3) Hesitation: s.next delays the reaction by 0.08-0.34*dope s, and the hit shapes cannot be re-kicked within 0.2 s (song-s.kicked<0.2); everyone-kick at most every 0.42 s; goal moves at most every 0.9 s (1.1 in storms). (4) dense = 1/(1+0.11*rate) damps kicks in fast music. (5) kick has randomness (rnd 0.8-1.2, 0.55-1, 18 % x0.4) and the shape chosen is by pitch rank plus noise, not the note itself. (6) The aftermath (hopping home, tipping, bumping, retrying) is a long, random chain that does not look like the attack, and the settling is the dominant visual: 'quiet' 0.85 s, 'content', 'still'. (7) disorder has no drive; the shared level pulse is not used.
snapKnobs: disorder (how hard an attack knocks them, 0.2-2, default 1, less 0.5): hop height, velocity and spin of kicks; also how far the goal moves and the roof
rush (how fast they scramble back, 0.3-2, default 1): shortens crouch and re-hop delay (divides dope by rush)
hop (how high they hop, 0.25-2.2, default 1, less 0.5): hop height and roof
crowd (3-30, default 16, less 4): number of shapes
size (0.5-2, default 1.25): size of shapes
presence: moves crowd, disorder, hop via their 'less' values (4, 0.5, 0.5)
howToSnap: This is a physics simulation with a deliberately late, comic reaction, so snapping needs several constants, not one: (a) kick latency, s.next = song + rnd(0.08,0.34)*dope (line 111) and the landing wait rnd(0.04,0.22)*dope/rush; (b) hit gating: budget (4+1.3*rate per s), 0.2 s re-kick lockout, 0.42 s 'everyone' lockout, percentile ranking; (c) the aftermath hopping home. A global attack/decay scale would NOT work on it as a whole (gravity, bounce restitution and spring constants are physical, and scaling time breaks the stacking and contact logic); only the latency terms (dope multiplier, the 0.2/0.42/0.9 s lockouts) and quiet/calm constants (0.85 s) and rush could be scaled safely. 'rush' already shortens the scramble back to about half at 2. Its character (clumsiness, lateness) is the point, so a true snap would be a different mode or a separate widget.
risk: Rigid-body physics with fixed sub-step SUB=1/120 and acc capped at 0.06 s: it is a state machine of a history (positions, velocities, content, slot, zc) and so it is not a pure function of song time, a seek or a render at a different frame rate gives a different outcome; changing the kick or latency changes the entire trajectory. Uses x.rnd, so repeatable only given the same call sequence. The first call to build()/scales() depends on window.NOTES and CHORDS; module-level state (shapes, goal, tilt, budget etc.) is shared by instances; the bounce/contact logic (bump, closing speed thresholds 110-170 px/s) is tuned for the current time scale; velsN is cached once; tilt/jolt affect the floor and every shape's fy(). Also, high 'rush' or small dope values can produce jitter or perpetual bouncing with a dense crowd.

onAttack: onChord() is empty ({}); the whole plan (one key per picked note, plus a stomp) is precomputed from CHORDS by planOf(), and frame() shows a key as soon as x.t >= k.t (seen(t) filters keys by k.t <= t). The key is then drawn rising out of the ground over k.rise seconds with a cubic ease-out, so it is visible and already moving in the very frame of the attack, at full alpha, with no fade-in.
decay: Rise: k.rise = RISE/hardness(i) = 0.2/(0.4+0.6*i) s (i = note intensity amount, default 1 gives 0.2 s; i=0.5 gives 0.286 s; i=0 gives 0.5 s); a=(t-k.t)/k.rise, risen = a>=1 ? 1 : 1-Math.pow(1-a,3), keyTop = -k.h + (1-risen)*k.full + sunk*(k.h+8). Individual keys never decay on their own: they stand until the last note. Press-back (notes after the stomp): sunk = smooth((t-k.press)/k.sink), k.sink = SINK/hardness(i) = 0.16/(0.4+0.6*i) s. Stomp (sh = t - stomp - 0.06): jolt = 2.4*strike*Math.exp(-sh/0.08)*Math.cos(sh*55) (tau 0.08 s); crater onset pressed = smooth(sh/0.09), crater ring alpha = pres*Math.exp(-sh/0.3)*0.35*deep (tau 0.3 s) and ring radius grows R*(1+sh*1.1); ripple front run = sh*FRONT (FRONT=430 units/s), per-row ox = amp*e*Math.sin(y*0.24+sh*30)*Math.exp(-sh/1.1) (tau 1.1 s), e = exp(-d*d/500) ahead of the front / exp(d/60) behind, active only while sh < RIPPLE_FOR = 3.2 s. Whole-widget end: after = (t - plan.last - HOLD)/AGE with HOLD = 2 s, AGE = 1.5 s: keys are multiplied by aged(after) (white to cream to honey to umber to black), gone = 1-smooth((after-0.8)/0.2), drawing stops at after >= 1, i.e. at last note + 3.5 s. The shared canvas fade (12%/step) is compensated by settles(want) = want*0.12/(1-want*0.88) so the keys sit at a steady alpha.
lowPass: none on attacks: no rate damping, ranking or gating at run time. The one filter is in the plan: if the listened set has more than MAX_ATTACKS = 60 note hits (i.e. not hand-picked) thin() keeps the THIN_TO = 36 loudest, spaced at least span/(36*1.5) apart. Only notes up to the stomp become keys (h.t > stomp is skipped), later ones become press-backs. Intensity i only scales hardness, size and brightness (k.show = min(1, 0.1+0.9*i)).
snapKnobs: No timing knob exists. floor: where the crater is (0/1). crater: crater depth 0..1 (default 0.35). ripple: ripple shake amplitude 0..8 (default 2.6). cracks: hairline cracks 0..8. presence: overall alpha. Picked-note intensity (0..2, note-values.ts) already shortens rise and sink via hardness(i) = 0.4+0.6*i, so a hard note rises up to 1.6x faster at i = 2 and the picked-note bar is the only existing way to sharpen the attack.
howToSnap: Attack: shrink RISE (const 0.2, line 16) and/or raise the ease-out exponent in `risen = a >= 1 ? 1 : 1 - Math.pow(1 - a, 3)` (cubic to 5 or 6), e.g. a new 'snap' knob s in 0..1 with default 0 that scales k.rise by (1 - 0.7*s) and the exponent; k.rise is baked into planOf() but could be applied in frame() as k.rise*scale, so the plan stays untouched. Decay: the widget deliberately never kills a key per note (the keys stay until the last note, then HOLD = 2 s and AGE = 1.5 s dissolve), so 'dies off more quickly' means only the stomp's jolt (0.08 s), ripple (exp(-sh/1.1), RIPPLE_FOR 3.2), crater ring (0.3 s), SINK (0.16 s) and HOLD/AGE; a per-key quick death would change the concept (a standing bar chart). A global attack/decay scale applied to the consts RISE, SINK, HOLD, AGE, RIPPLE_FOR would work, and the plan does not depend on them except through k.rise/k.sink and plan.last (HOLD is read in frame()).
risk: Ivory is in both protected scenes (13 instances in liebesleid, 1 in rach-concerto-2), so every default must stay pixel-identical: any new knob must default to today's constants. The plan is cached module-wide (let plan = null; planNow() builds it once from CHORDS, never invalidated) and the per-key textures are cached (k.img, keyed on rs and cracks), so the envelope constants may change but the plan shape (keys, foot, h, w) and the textures must not. Ripple/crater use the shared-canvas settles() compensation, so changing the 0.12 fade assumption or the alpha math changes the look. The stomp timing (sh offset 0.06) and the press-back timing (k.press) are coupled to the notes, not the envelope.

onAttack: onChord(ch, x) only does ensure(x); pending.push(ch). In the next advanceFrame() (same frame) each note of the chord sets joints[i].flash = 1 for the joint chosen by pitch (PAIRS[floor(pitch01*6.999)][m%2 ? 0 : 1]), lights that joint's stars at flash = max(.35), and for the 4 loudest notes gives the joint a velocity impulse away from the pelvis. The footfalls themselves (13 dots form a walking figure) are NOT driven by onChord but by a precomputed plan() of chosen chords: strikePtr fires joints[11 or 12].flash = strike = 1 plus a push on the 16 nearest stars at s.tStrike, and the gait phase is lerp(phiStart, phiEnd, u) over [tStart, tStrike].
decay: flash and strike: `q.flash *= Math.exp(-dt/.22); q.strike *= Math.exp(-dt/.22)` per frame for all joints and stars (tau 0.22 s; note the decay runs BEFORE the pending chords add flash = 1, so the first frame shows the full 1). Spring on displacement: spring(q,dt): q.vx += (-28*28*q.dx - 2*.45*28*q.vx)*dt (omega 28 rad/s, zeta 0.45: period 0.224 s, amplitude envelope exp(-12.6 t), tau 0.079 s), but it is integrated only `if (moving)` with moveDt, so it freezes while the figure stands. Impulse sizes: joint push D = (6+24*lastLoud)*(phrase.h/540)/(1+.35*x.rate) times 49 px/s per unit; star push 18*s.loud*(1-d/140)*49. Visual: dot radius r*(1+max(.9*flash*lastLoud, strike)) and a white sprite overlaid at alpha flash*fade. Arm lift: critically-ish damped spring `liftRV += (49*(target-liftR) - 2*.55*7*liftRV)*moveDt` (omega 7, zeta .55, tau about 0.26 s) to target x.p('arms')*150*pitch01(top.m)**1.6*(.4+.6*lastLoud)*(1-.8*run). Slow mood states: run += (s.run-run)*(1-exp(-moveDt/.25)); sad and proud: tau 3 s each, driven by x.feat.level and x.feat.pitch. Figure fade-in/out clamp((t-tStart)/.3). The layer wipes the canvas each frame itself: fillRect rgba(0,0,0,.85*presence) over everything, then blacks out the previous dot positions.
lowPass: Heavy. plan() picks which chords become footfalls: after the previous footfall it skips chords before t+0.30 s and picks the loudest chord within [t+0.30, t+0.42]; if none, the first later one (the step then waits up to maxStep = 1.15 s gap before standing). So only a subset of attacks make a step, and each step's strike is a precomputed time. Joint impulses: only the hardest 4 notes per chord, damped by 1/(1+.35*x.rate); loud rank is a percentile rank (rank(sortedV, vel)) across the whole piece; run/sad/proud smoothing (0.25 s and 3 s); arm lift spring (tau about 0.26 s) and lift target uses x.top() (highest sounding note), plus its zero-lift gate lastCount >= 4 && lastLoud > .7 for the left arm; mood of the gait amplitude via sad (1-0.35*sad).
snapKnobs: stride (how big its steps 0.5..1.4) scales footfall amplitude
maxStep (how soon it stops 0.7..1.6) changes which gaps the figure keeps walking through
arms (how the melody lifts it 0..1.2) scales the arm lift from x.top()
height (how near 0.6..1.3)
presence (how many stars 20..170 and the 0.85 black wipe alpha)
None changes flash/strike tau (0.22 s) or the spring (28 rad/s, zeta 0.45)
howToSnap: Joint/star flash and strike are alert already (instant 1 in the attack frame) but die with tau 0.22 s: replace the two literals `Math.exp(-dt/.22)` in advanceFrame (the line `for (const q of [...joints, ...stars]) { q.flash *= ...; q.strike *= ... }`) by a snap-scaled tau (about 0.08 s), and raise the spring stiffness/damping literals in spring() (28, .45) for a quicker settle. The alert-to-the-attack part is limited by design: the footfalls are scheduled by the plan on chosen chords only (every >= 0.30 s, loudest within 0.42 s), the ensuing gait phase is scheduled earlier (tStart), and the per-note flash is the part that sees every note. A global attack/decay scale (a multiplier on the 0.22 s tau, the arm spring and the spring omega) would work cleanly; do not touch plan() or solvePhase().
risk: The walk is precomputed in plan() and cached by ensure() (settings string and CHORDS identity trigger reset), and the gait phase, projection, shift (star field scroll) and lastActual are stateful integrators of the walk, so changing walking timing (tStart/tStrike, maxStep, spring frequency used inside moveDt) changes where the stars and figure end up for the rest of the piece and breaks seek consistency. The springs only integrate while moving, so a faster spring will still freeze when standing. Body dots feed the next frame's black-out (prev) and the dot size uses flash*lastLoud, so reducing flash tau also shrinks the pop. Not in any protected scene.

onAttack: onChord(ch, x) builds one shape per note (the bass notes below 48 merged into a single longer bar) at once: the element is born in this frame, at full alpha (fade = (1-age/life)^1.3 is 1 at age 0), with a size pop and a white flash, and a cream outline ring springs out of it (rings.push({e, age:0})). It also creates constellation and melody lines, and for loud chords (vel >= 92, >= 2 notes, cooldown 0.5 s) long straight lines across the canvas; loud low notes may add a faint colour field (cooldown 2.5 s, probability .3+.6*paint).
decay: Shape life = lerp(2.5, 7.5, paint)*(1-0.35*feat.density) * (0.7+0.6*vk) (vk = v/100); at default paint 0.45 that is about 4.8 s*(0.7..1.3)*(density factor); fade = Math.pow(Math.max(0, 1-age/life), 1.3) (linear-ish, no hold, gone at age = life). Size pop: land = max(0, 1-age/0.5); kk = 1+0.35*land^3 (0.5 s, cubic). Colour flash to white: flash = max(0, 1-age/0.3)^2*0.5*min(1,v/100) (0.3 s). Attack ring: f = max(0, 1-age/0.5), alpha 0.5*f*f, lineWidth 1+1.5f, scale 1.1+0.7*(1-f) (0.5 s). Lines: f = 1-age/life with life = shape life*0.6 (chord lines, grow over 0.3 s with 1-(1-grow)^2) or *0.9 (melody lines, grow 0.45 s), alpha (0.4 or 0.75)*f*sqrt(min fade of its ends). Cross lines: life 1.8 s, grow 0.35 s cubic ease-out to 1700 px, bold flash width 1+1.6*max(0,1-age/0.25), alpha 0.6*f^1.5. Colour fields (planes): life*1.2, fade-in min(1, age/0.4), alpha .025+.03*paint, (1-age/life)^1.5. Held notes (cls != 0 and d > 0.3 with probability): arc sweep min(2π*.9, min(age, d)*2.6). Drift: velocities vx,vy (16..26 px/s) times drift*dt*2, drift = 0.05+0.6*restless. Draws directly on the shared fading canvas (g.globalAlpha restored).
lowPass: No explicit smoothing of attacks. Gates/randomness: Math.random (not x.rnd) decides arcs, lines (probability L), planes, grids/suns and the draw; crossCool 0.5 s, planeCool 2.5 s; shape count capped at 170 (elements) and 160 (lines). feat.density (0.25 s half-life) shortens life by up to 35%; restless is driven by feat.rate (drive '+rate'). Bass notes of a chord are merged into one bar. The long life is itself the main smoother: shapes linger for seconds so the picture reflects the last ~5 s rather than the current note.
snapKnobs: paint (how much paint 0..1, default 0.45, less: 0.1): life lerp(2.5, 7.5, paint) and shape scale lerp(0.55, 1.1, paint); lowering it to 0 gives life 2.5 s
presence (leads paint, web...): moves those knobs
web (connecting lines, less: 0.05): fewer lines
restless (calm or restless, drive '+rate'): drift
rings and edges (round or sharp) drive '-level' and '+level'
howToSnap: Attack is already instant (pop 0.5 s, flash 0.3 s, ring 0.5 s). To make it die quicker: in onChord the `life` line `lerp(2.5, 7.5, paint) * (1 - 0.35*density)` and the `fade` function (exponent 1.3; a snap value of 2 to 3 makes the fade fall off sooner), plus the lines' life multipliers 0.6 and 0.9 and the cross line life 1.8. A new knob 'snap' (default 0 = today's constants) that multiplies life by (1-0.6*s) and raises the fade exponent would work; a global attack/decay scale would work because everything is age/life based. For an alert attack: shorten the pop (0.5) and flash (0.3) and ring (0.5) constants in frame().
