risk: Kandinsky is in the protected rach-concerto-2 scene (two instances), so defaults must stay identical; and it already uses Math.random, so even today two renders do not match pixel for pixel (the pixel-identical proof cannot cover it). State is a plain array sim (els, lines, rings, planes) and reset() clears it. Life values feed the line fades (fade(l.a), fade(l.b)) so changing life or fade changes the lines too; the held arc relies on e.d (note duration) not envelope; capping at 170 elements means shorter life also changes density. Drift velocity fields (vx/vy) are tied to drift not life.

onAttack: onChord(ch, x) turns each note into a 'run' for its voice (six voices by register, dynamic-programming voice leading) and immediately calls reveal(0), which lays the first tile on the attack frame: amt[v][i] = max(a, base*wgt)+0.15*wgt, flash[i] = max(flash, fl*(k===0 ? 1 : 0.6)) with fl = 0.6+0.5*vk, body/grain set, and for loud notes (vk > .72) a spray of lit tiles around the first column (flash .95*q). The remaining tiles of the run (L = 2..18 tiles, 1+n.d*4.5+vk*2+sparse*5) are NOT laid at once: want = 1+floor(age/d*L) shows them progressively across the note's duration d, and a sounding tile deepens (a += dt*.55*wgt, up to 1.6) and holds a glow (hold floor .16).
decay: Per frame: flash[i] *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.14) (half-life 0.14 s, tau about 0.20 s); hold[i] *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.25) (half-life 0.25 s). Paint: keep = Math.pow(0.5, dt/Math.max(1, stay*0.6*(1+1.2*sparse))) applied per voice amount (default stay = 14: half-life 8.4 s; with sparse music (sparse = 1-clamp(feat.rate*4) up to 1) 18.5 s); fine-grained tiles (grain=1) take keepF = keep*keep, i.e. half the half-life. Pop: sz*(1+0.34*fl*fl), the rim stroke is drawn only while flash > 0.62 (about 0.1 s after the attack). Tile size from body: wt = clamp((bd-0.35)/0.6) etc. A resting voice pitch pv drifts home: rk = 1-Math.pow(0.5, dt/6). The veil of dots scrolls at 7 and 3.2 px/s and is level-driven. The layer repaints its own opaque canvas every frame (drawImage(under) first), so the shared canvas fade does not matter; the mosaic persists in the arrays amt/flash/body/grain, a stateful sim.
lowPass: Yes, mostly through duration and persistence: (a) the run reveals across d (a long, pedalled note spreads its tiles over up to d seconds, so the attack is smeared into a staircase), (b) the colour stays with a half-life of seconds so the mosaic is 'the last stretch of music' by design, (c) sparse = 1-clamp(rate*4) lengthens persistence (up to 2.2x) and run length, (d) thick is driven by feat.level ('+level'), veil by '-level', (e) voice assignment is by nearest voice position pv, so successive notes of one voice walk across rows, (f) cursor advance and x.rnd() breath. Attacks themselves are never skipped.
snapKnobs: stay (how long the colour stays 3..40, default 14, less: 3): scales the paint half-life
thick (how wide each voice paints 0.6..4, drive '+level')
size (tile size 12..40)
mix (colour mixing)
veil (veil of dots, drive '-level')
presence (leads: stay, thick, veil)
Nothing changes the 0.14 s flash or the reveal-over-d
howToSnap: Attack: the first tile of each run is already lit on the attack frame, but the rest of the run trickles over d: set want = u.L (or min(L, a small snap-controlled count)) so the full run appears with the attack: in reveal(), `const want = u.age >= u.d ? u.L : Math.min(u.L, 1 + Math.floor((u.age / u.d) * u.L))`. Decay: shorten fk (0.14) and hk (0.25) and the amt half-life `stay*0.6*(1+1.2*sparse)`; stay is already a knob (min 3 gives half-life 1.8 s). A new knob 'snap' (default 0) multiplying those constants would work; a global attack/decay scale would work because all of it is dt-based exponentials, and the persistent arrays need no replanning.
risk: Not in a protected scene. State is the persistent tile arrays: changing size rebuilds the grid by resampling (build(s)), so decay changes just scale amt. The 'a' amounts also drive the colour mixing (top, unc, cov), so faster paint decay changes the colours where voices cross, not only brightness. Grain (twice as fast decay) and the body weight depend on the n.d note duration, which the pedal makes unreliable. reveal() relies on runs filtered by age < d || shown < L; making the run appear at once ends it immediately.

onAttack: onChord(ch, x) first ranks the chord (loud = 0.6*percentile of vel across the piece + 0.4*rel vs a 1.2 s running average) and, if it counts as big (score = .55p+.45rel+.25quiet+.03*min(n-1,4) >= thresh .8, or gap >= 2 s with p >= .25, and at least 0.34 s since the last strike), creates a huge bar with strike() (older bars get dim += 0.1), possibly a girder beside it and a wipe of the oldest bars beyond MAX_LIVE = 6; any other chord creates one short brush mark with mark(). One object per chord, not per note. The bar/mark is in the list in the attack frame and swept into view by a reveal.
decay: Reveal (not decay): stroke reveal = 1-Math.pow(1-Math.min(1, s.age/s.dur), 2.2) with dur = 0.06+L/(3200+4000*velN) (about 0.15 s for L around 600); marks: reveal = 1-(1-min(1, age/dur))^2 with dur = 0.04+L/2400 (0.05..0.12 s). Bars: s.q += dt/life where life = x.p('stay') (default 4, drive '+level' adds depth*(24-1.2)*feat.level), fade = 1-smooth(0.25, 1, s.q) times faint, i.e. solid for the first 25% of life then an eased fade to zero at life (about 1 s then 4 s at default), s.a += (1-s.dim-s.a)*(1-Math.exp(-dt/0.4)) (greying tau 0.4 s, dim up to 0.3). Wipe (over-paint): wipe += dt/WIPE with WIPE = 0.3 s; cover slides in vis = full*(1-Math.pow(1-k,1.7)); bar fades 1-smooth(1,4,wipe) (0.3..1.2 s) and the cover 1-smooth(4,5,wipe) (to 1.5 s). Marks: mLife = life*0.3 (default 1.2 s); m.q += dt/(m.q<1 ? mLife : 1.4); alpha q<1: 1-0.78*smooth(0.1,1,q) (down to a grey ghost 0.22), then ghost alpha 0.22*(1-smooth(1,2.6,q)) over 1.4*1.6 = 2.24 s; marks removed at q >= 2.6; cap MAX_MARKS = 44, MAX_LIVE = 6. The layer repaints the opaque ground every frame (drawImage(ground)), so the shared fade does not apply.
lowPass: Yes: the whole point is selection. Only 'big' chords strike (percentile of vel against the entire piece, relative loudness vs a 1.2 s running mean localV, silence-breaking bonus), minimum 0.34 s between strikes, 'firm' hand (weight < .35) drops soft chords; other chords only leave a mark; marks chain into a line (new chain after 0.9 s gap or 16 marks). No time smoothing of the attack itself; bars appear in the same frame.
snapKnobs: stay (how long they stay 1.2..24, default 4, drive '+level'): the main decay knob; bars solid for 25% of it, marks 0.3x
thresh (which chords strike 0.5..0.97, default 0.8)
weight (how heavy 0.1..1.9; below .35 also thins which chords land)
order (loose or rigid, drive '-rate')
ground and colour
howToSnap: Decay: stay already goes down to 1.2 s (bars gone in 1.2 s, marks mLife 0.36 s) but the default drive adds level on top and the fade starts at 25% with an eased curve; a 'snap' multiplier on life and on `smooth(0.25, 1, s.q)` (start the fade at 0 and use a steeper curve) would make bars die quickly. Attack: the reveal durations (0.06+L/(3200+4000*velN) and 0.04+L/2400) are already about 0.1 s; scale them down for sharper sweeps; the WIPE (0.3 s) as well. A global scale on life and reveal durations would work; mark and bar share the same life. The hard limit is that Kline answers once per big chord, not per note, with a 0.34 s minimum between bars.
risk: Kline is in the protected rach-concerto-2 scene (two instances), so the defaults must stay identical, but note it already uses Math.random (strike/mark/seeded sprites with seed from Math.random) so output is not reproducible pixel for pixel. Sprites are cached per bar/mark/colour (s.sp, s.cv, s.un, pool) and the 'cover' and 'under' canvases are prepared one per frame ahead, so changing durations does not break caches, but the overpaint (wipe) is triggered by MAX_LIVE and by attack time, not by decay. The knobs 'stay' and 'weight' persist in stored shows; weight < .35 changes behaviour (firmOf), do not alter.

onAttack: onChord(ch, x) spawns a colony for each of the chord's (up to 7, lowest first) notes (a note answers only if hardEnough(vel) against the piece's percentile, always at presence 1): a big dot at its pitch (x = W*(0.06+0.88*p)) plus n = round((8+34*min(1,v/110))*(.55+.45*min(1,dur/1.6))*(.6+.4*size)) satellite dots, and for chords of >= 3 notes a patch of net; a harmony change may start a flood. The big dot is drawn at full radius R0 on the attack frame with an overshoot; the satellites appear one after another afterwards.
decay: Big dot: q.rv[0] = R0*(1 + 0.22*still*Math.exp(-age/0.07)) (overshoot dies with tau 0.07 s; still = 1-0.7*calm, 1 at full presence). Satellites: at[k-1] = 0.05+(k/n)*min(2.4, 0.5+dur*1.1) seconds (a staggered appearance, spread over 0.55..2.4 s depending on the held duration), each grows with easeBack(a/0.2) (s = 2.2 overshoot, 0.2 s). Colony life = x.p('stay')*(0.75+0.5*min(1, v/110)) (default stay 6 s gives 4.5..7.5 s); then the exit: the outermost dots go first, dot k shrinks starting at age = end + (1-k/n)*0.7 over 0.3 s linearly (r *= max(0, 1-out/0.3)), the big dot at age >= end+0.75 shrinks over 0.3 s, colony removed at end + 1.1 s. Nets: radius grows 1-(1-min(1,a/0.9))^3 over 0.9 s, life = stay*1.2, shrinks over 0.6 s; throb kick = max(kick, (vel-70)/57*0.16*pres), kick *= Math.exp(-dt/0.18) (tau 0.18 s) scales the net 1.7*0.2^tight*(1-kick); tight eases with tau 0.6+3*calm s. Flood: radius rmax*(1-Math.pow(1-u, 2.2)) over dur = 0.5+1.5*calm s. Seed dots breathe sin(breathe+ph) at 1.3 rad/s. The scene is repainted opaque every frame (ground fillRect), on the shared canvas at full presence; below presence 1 it is drawn on a sheet and composited faintly.
lowPass: Yes in parts: presence-based hardEnough() gates attacks by velocity percentile (every one at 1, hardest 40% at 0.4, 5% at 0) with a fallback `due` note every 0.5+5*calm s; colour changes are slow: pitch classes decay exp(-dtc/0.7), a candidate colour pair must hold 0.5 s unless >= 3 notes or vel > 95, and floods need gap = 8*0.08^flip*(1+4*calm) s (about 2.3 s at flip .5) since the last; tight/netSize follow with tau 0.6..4 s. Individual colony spawns themselves are not delayed or merged, but the satellite stagger spreads the energy of one note over up to 2.4 s.
snapKnobs: stay (how long the dots stay 1.5..18, default 6)
size (how big the colonies are 0.4..1.8, drive '+level')
tight (net tightness, drive '+rate')
wild
flip (how often the colours change)
presence (calm gates which notes answer and slows tight/netSize, flood dur)
Nothing shortens the 0.07 s overshoot, the 0.2 s dot growth, or the 0.3/0.7 s exits
howToSnap: The big dot is already instant (0.07 s overshoot). Make the satellites snap: the stagger `at.push(0.05 + (k / n) * Math.min(2.4, 0.5 + dur * 1.1))` is the main smear (a pedalled piano note with a long d takes up to 2.4 s to fill in): cap the span (for example 0.15 s) and shorten easeBack's 0.2 s. Make the death quicker: the exit stagger `(1 - k / q.n) * 0.7`, the 0.3 s shrink, the 0.75 s big-dot hold and `life = stay * ...`; and the kick tau 0.18. A new knob (default off = today's numbers) or a global scale on these durations would work; the colour logic and flood durations can stay. Timing is `time += dt`, not x.t, so seeking depends on reset replay.
risk: Not in a protected scene (default on: false). Colony state is simulated from accumulated `time` (time += dt), not from x.t, so a quick-snap change must remain dt-based; satellite positions and radii are drawn from x.rnd at spawn (deterministic), and the plan is the per-note array. The MAXDOTS = 1100 trimming ('the oldest start to go now') couples life with density: shorter life means fewer colonies alive but trimming still works. Presence below 1 draws to an offscreen sheet (lay) with a settles-style alpha equation tied to the 12% shared fade, so do not touch that when changing envelopes. The flood redraws the scene twice using rv, and update() is called once per frame in cols.filter(update).

onAttack: onChord cuts a paper piece for the chord's lowest, highest and (if 4+ notes) one middle note only (not every note), with age=0 and full opacity on the very first frame (p.col filled flat, no fade-in); it also calls gust(p.x,p.y,rad,amt) which adds velocity impulses vx/vy/vr = f*1100/heavy to every neighbouring piece, and a chord of 2-3+ notes (moveCool<=0) lifts k older pieces to move/turn them over 0.5-0.75 s. In its own frame the attack is seen as the new piece landing oversized (k = 1 + (0.1+0.32*loud)*(0.4+0.6*stir)*land^2, land = max(0, 1 - age/ldur)) on a lifted shadow (off = 2.5 + lift*17) while the neighbours get shoved and spring back; a ch.vel>=92 chord gusts the whole wall and may start a 0.5 s ground wipe (groundCool 5 s).
decay: The piece itself does not decay: 'nothing fades', it stays at full colour until swapped out by the pieces cap (default 18): then die += dt/0.32 (linear shrink in 0.32 s, sx *= 1-u, sy *= 1-0.25u). The attack signature decays as: land pop ldur = 0.24 s (low, reg0) / 0.18 s (mid) / 0.13 s (high), shape land^2 = (1-age/ldur)^2, i.e. half height at age = 0.293*ldur = 0.070 / 0.053 / 0.038 s; pop size max +42% at loud=1,stir=1 (+10% at loud 0). Neighbour sway is a damped spring: vx += (-w*w*ox - z*vx)*dt with z = 2*0.32*w, so zeta=0.32, w = TAU*1.05 / TAU*1.6 / TAU*2.5 = 6.6 / 10.05 / 15.7 rad/s (reg0/1/2), envelope time constant 1/(0.32*w) = 0.47 / 0.31 / 0.20 s, ringing with periods ~0.95 / 0.63 / 0.40 s; clamped to |o|<=0.35*s, |or|<=0.6. Lift while the note sounds: sounding = (p.end > x.t) ? (0.35+0.65*loud)*(0.35+0.65*stir) : 0, p.lift += (sounding-p.lift)*(1-exp(-dt/(sounding>p.lift ? 0.05 : 0.22))), so rise tau 0.05 s and release tau 0.22 s, but the plateau lasts the transcribed note length n.d (p.end = x.t + n.d), which is unreliable with pedal. Shadow alpha 0.13+0.15*lift, offset 2.5+17*lift, trembles sin(ph)*0.03*lift. Moves: dur RR(0.5,0.75) s with cubic ease; flip 0.4 s; grow 1+0.45*min(1,min(age,d)/2.5).
lowPass: Not smoothing of the attack itself, but: only 2-3 notes of a chord cut pieces (others ignored); gust strength damped by calm = lerp(1, 0.5, min(1, feat.rate*1.4)) (feat.rate has 1.0 s half-life) and piece size by busy = lerp(1.3, 0.78, min(1, rate*1.6)); moveCool 0.45 s between rearrangements (and only chords of 3+ notes or 2 notes with vel>=88); groundCool 5 s; trimCool 0.18 s per forced removal; loud = (v-30)/80 so soft notes get small pop and pale paper; the pieces cap swaps the oldest piece rather than adding. Release of the lift is slow (0.22 s) and tied to note length.
snapKnobs: move (0..1, default 0.6, drive +level): scales land pop by (0.4+0.6*stir), lift height (0.35+0.65*stir), gust strength, and chord move count k; at 0 pieces are laid flat
size: piece size
pieces: wall capacity, how fast old pieces are swapped (cap 6..40)
presence: sets pieces/size
no existing knob changes any time constant
howToSnap: The cut and its pop are already instantaneous and short (half-pop 0.04-0.07 s); the slow parts are the neighbour spring (z = 2*0.32*w at the sway block: raise 0.32 toward ~0.7-0.8 and the tau drops from 0.2-0.47 s to ~0.1-0.2 s with no ringing), the lift release tau 0.22 (line 'dt / (sounding > p.lift ? 0.05 : 0.22)' to ~0.08) and the note-length-dependent plateau (cap n.d, e.g. p.end = x.t + min(n.d, 0.15), so pedalled notes don't keep the piece raised), and the swap-out die 0.32 s (-> ~0.12). A global attack/decay scale would work well here because every time constant is a visible literal (ldur 0.24/0.18/0.13, 0.05/0.22, 0.32, damping ratio), but the base look (paper stays on the wall) means the response IS the pop/shadow/gust, so it should be made sharper (higher peak pop at shorter ldur), not by fading the piece.
risk: Uses Math.random (R, RR, pick) throughout: not deterministic in song time, so seeks/renders will not match live play (x.rnd is not used). Pieces and the wall are persistent state with placement dependent on prior pieces (spot() best-of-9, colour avoidance via nearCols), so changing the number of pieces or timing changes the whole collage. The spring is integrated with plain Euler (vx += ...*dt); raising damping or w makes it more stable but raising w with large dt could go unstable. Wipe/ground logic and move (0.5-0.75 s) are separate timelines that would look slow next to a snapped pop. Not part of either protected scene.

onAttack: For each of up to 5 notes (loudest per pitch class, sorted by velocity) onChord pushes one 'print' (a card of bars) onto every panel within reach of the note's home panel (home = circle-of-fifths slot of pitch class), with age = -d*0.045 s for echo panels at distance d (d=0 for the home panel: no delay). On the first frame with age>=0 the card lands: p.y = p.D and p.len = p.D, i.e. the strike punches D = max(P*1.15+4, H*(0.05 + 0.42*vel^1.6)) pixels of bars instantly at full width (wide = (0.2+0.72*vel)*(0.4+0.6a)), the panel ground is lifted (flash[s] = max(flash, vel^2*(home?1:0.45)*a/(1+1.6*heat[s]))) and a bright wider 'struck edge' bar is drawn, so in its own frame the attack is a complete full-strength card plus a panel flash on frame zero.
decay: Card shape: while age < hold (hold = max(0.05, min(n.d, 6)), the transcribed note length) f = 1 and the card keeps lengthening (len += run, run = (70+600*scroll)*dt px/s = 280 px/s at default scroll 0.35); after the note f = (max(0, 1-(age-hold)/life))^1.3 with life = 1.4 s default (knob 0.15..4, 'less' 0.5), half strength at (age-hold) = 0.413*life = 0.58 s, gone at hold+life; bar width scales (0.4+0.6f), bar thickness th*(0.25+0.75f); card removed when age >= hold+life or its tail leaves the panel (p.y - p.len >= H). Birth highlight: born = max(0, 1-age/0.2) (linear 0.2 s), widening the bar 15% and mixing 20% white in the ink, plus the bright edge bar at 0.55*born white. Panel flash: flash[s] *= 0.5^(dt/0.07), half-life 0.07 s (tau 0.10 s); a flash>0.55 turns the panel negative; ground brightness lit = 1+1.8*flash. heat[s] (share-out so busy music does not strobe) decays half-life 0.6 s (hd = 0.5^(dt/0.6)) and is bumped +0.6+vel (home) or +0.2. Global glow = max(glow, ch.vel/115) halves every 1.2 s and shifts ground brightness by (0.7+0.3*glow). Harmony hue chroma half-life 1.6 s, hue follows half-life 0.6 s, panel-count weights half-life 0.18 s.
lowPass: At most 5 notes per attack; echo delay 0.045 s per panel step; heat division (1+1.6*heat) damps repeated flashes in the same panel with half-life 0.6 s (a rapid repeat flashes much less); panels count driven by +rate (busy splits into more, narrower panels); per-panel cap CAP=40 drops the faintest card; hue/chroma follow with 0.6-1.6 s half-lives; hold uses transcribed note length, so a held (or pedalled) note stays at full strength and keeps growing for up to 6 s. No ranking or gating of attacks otherwise.

howToSnap: Hardly any change needed on the attack (it already lands full-strength at once). The tail is the issue: the card holds at f=1 for hold = min(n.d, 6) (use min(n.d, ~0.12) so pedalled notes do not hold the card), then fades over life (setting life low via the existing knob already snaps the decay, but its default 1.4 and min 0.15 are the only handle; a snap preset of life ~0.3, spread ~0.2 would work with no code change), shorten the born window 0.2 and flash half-life 0.07 only if the flash needs to be sharper; the glow half-life 1.2 s and heat 0.6 s could be shortened. A global decay scale could multiply life, hold-cap, glow/heat/flash half-lives; global attack scale has little to act on, since the attack is already a single-frame event.

Opaque-card occlusion culling assumes newer cards cover older ones, which stays valid. Deterministic (no Math.random; uses n.d/x.H only). Echo timing (age < 0 deferred landing) means echoes land up to 0.18 s after the home panel (4 steps). Not in either protected scene.

onAttack: For each note in the chord onChord may create one element (dot, star, blob, crescent or bow-tie; chosen by pitch, velocity, duration n.d >0.38 (or >0.2 and loud/sparse) and Math.random) pushed with age 0 and life = life*(0.75+0.5*rand) (default 16 s, so 12-20 s); the chord's top note draws a star or dot exactly on the pen's current position (suppressed if the last mark was within 30 px or 0.22 s earlier, 'near'), and the melody step bends the pen (pen.kappa += step*0.11*wander, kick zigzag on a repeat). In its own frame the attack is a flat shape appearing at full alpha, 35% oversized, shrinking to size over 0.16 s: pop = 1 + 0.35*max(0, 1 - age/0.16), plus thin tie lines drawing out over 0.3 s; the pen line itself only turns slowly (kappa).
decay: Shapes do not die with the note: a = min(1, max(0, (life-age)/(0.3*life))), k = pop*grow*(0.1+0.9*sqrt(a)), fa = min(1, 5a): full strength for the first 70% of life (about 11 s at default 16 s) and then a shrink and fade over the last 30% (about 4.8 s). Blobs and crescents also grow while the note sounds: grow = 0.42 + 0.58*(1-(1-min(1, age/hold))^2) with hold = max(0.12, min(n.d, 3.5)) (note length, not x.sounding()). Pen trail points are kept for `life` seconds (chunk alpha min(1,(1-age/life)/0.3)); pen.kappa *= exp(-dt*0.7) (tau 1.43 s); pen speed = 18 + 150*feat.level + 90*feat.rate px/s (level half-life 0.8 s, rate half-life 1.0 s); trail width 1.3+1.4*level, pen dot radius 2.2+1.5*level. Ties (age ease (1-(1-t/0.3)^2) draw-out 0.3 s) live as long as their two shapes. Stains: alpha ramps in over 1.2 s, fades over life*0.8 s (about 12.8 s), max 0.16, radius grows over 3 s; stainCool 1.2 s.
lowPass: Heavy gating: lastMark 'near' check (30 px / 0.22 s) drops quick melody marks (only a loud repeat can still add a dot, 50%); fewer shapes when 22+ are live (full): held notes mostly become dots, lifeK = clamp(1.2 - shapes/40, 0.6, 1) shrinks shapes; probabilistic Math.random choices (a star needs n.v>=70 or 60% luck, crescent 50%, bow 25%); sparse = clamp(1 - feat.rate*2.5, 0, 1) enlarges shapes in sparse music; element cap 220 (excess given 0.4 s life) and 400; ties 200; pen heading/speed follows feat.level and feat.rate (smoothed with 0.8-1.0 s half-lives), so the pen line is a very low-passed response. Only the top note per chord marks the line.
snapKnobs: life (4..40 s, default 16, less 5): the only decay handle, scales shapes, pen trail, stains; its minimum of 4 s still means 3-5 s
swell (0.4..2, drive +level): blob size
wander (0..2, drive +rate): pen turning strength
web (0..1, less 0.05): how many ties
colour
presence: sets life, web, swell
howToSnap: Hard: the widget is a persistent sky, so snapping means changing its premise. The smallest change is a new opt-in knob (default off) that fades each element quickly after the pop: in the age block 'e.a = min(1, max(0, (e.life - e.age)/(e.life*0.3)))' replace e.life by a short fixed life (e.g. min(life, 0.4 + hold)) for non-line marks so a star/dot/blob lives ~0.5-1 s, and shorten the pop window 0.16 to 0.08 with a larger peak. The line itself would need its own `life`. A global attack/decay scale would only act on the pop (0.16, 0.3) and the stain/tie timings, not on the 12-20 s sky, so by itself it would change nothing visible at defaults.
risk: It IS in the protected Liebesleid scene, so any change must be opt-in (new knob default = today's look, never altering p('life') meaning). It already uses Math.random (not x.rnd) for shape choices, positions, shapes and the pen jitter, so pixel-identical hashing via render.html cannot hold for it today (it also paints a wash canvas once via its own LCG, deterministic). Pen path and trail are integrated per frame from clock += dt, so renders with a different substep would differ. Because the stars sit on the wandering line and the line is built from feat.level/rate, shortening the shapes' life would leave the line alone and look unmotivated unless the line also shortens. A drive of 'life' on '-rate' is absent; presence writes life and web.

onAttack: onChord handles the whole chord at once (notes only feed its clock-face figure and a hi/bass/mean summary): if the chord is loud enough (score = vel + 3*(n-3) >= bar = 112 - 30*strike, default 94; n>=2; ch.hi>=60; more than 0.2 s since the last strike; and passes the presence percentile test) it re-forms the 900 birds into that chord's figure by overwriting every bird's velocity (vx = vx*(1-calm) + (dx - dy*tw)*f with f = pow*(0.5+R0*0.9), pow = same ? 2.5 : 1.5 + calm*(4+w*9), times (0.6+0.4*panic)*live) and returns; otherwise a radial startle within R = (70+200w)*... of the note's bird/ribbon head gives vx += dx/d*P*f, P = (0.3+w^2*5)*panic*mood factors, plus heat (red) up to 1.6, a dread throb pulse, and a shard kick. In its own frame the attack is a velocity impulse on the flock followed by a staggered re-gathering: it is not visible as a single event in frame zero.
decay: Figure hold: formHold = 1 on the strike, decremented dt/hold (hold knob default 2.6 s, min 0.8); wf = min(1, 1.7*formHold), so the figure is fully weighted for (1-0.588)*hold = 1.07 s (0.33 s at hold 0.8) and then fades linearly over 0.588*hold = 1.53 s (0.47 s), gone at hold (2.6 s). Re-gathering: ramp = clamp((sinceStrike - (0.06+D0*0.3)*calm)/(0.04+0.3*calm)), so after a quiet spell (calm=1) each bird starts 0.06-0.36 s late and takes 0.04-0.34 s to engage (figure legible in ~0.3-0.7 s); in a fast run calm=0 and the figure engages at once. Spring/damping per 60 Hz tick: ks = ((0.004+0.03*coh)*... *rest + wf*(0.05+0.07*coh))*glide (about 0.092 in figure at coh 0.6), damp = dB + (dN-dB)*ramp with dB = 0.9^k (tau 0.16 s) and dN = 0.86 - 0.16wd - 0.1wa - 0.1wf per tick (0.76 in a figure, tau 0.06 s; 0.86 plain, tau 0.11 s). Heat (the red flash) *= 0.5^(dt/0.55) (half-life 0.55 s) and bins colours by heat*3.2. fpulse (repeated-chord swell of 13% size and 60% thickness) *= 0.5^(dt/0.12); pulse (dread throb) half-life 0.35 s; mood A half-life 1.2 s (agit/dread follow with half-life 0.6 s via sm = 1-0.5^(dt/0.6)); low half-life 3 s; bassS half-life 1.5 s; melody ribbon: SPAN 7 s smoothed 3 passes, mvel half-life 0.8 s of the held note. Trails: T = trail knob history points (default 9, HM=16 stored per frame, so 9 frames = 0.15 s at 60 Hz), capped by (40+16T) px of path.
lowPass: Very heavy: strikes need the chord to be in a high score and 0.2 s apart; presence <1 requires a percentile rank (hardest 5%/3% of this song's chords: startles(), figures() use sorted chordVels/chordScores); calm = ss(0.7, 2.2, x.t - lastStrike) (after a quiet spell it explodes first); per-bird staggered ramp 0.06-0.36 s; panic = min(2, 1+feat.rate) rescales the force; moods agit/dread mix by 0.6 s half-life and are squared/normalised so the flock commits to one character (wa, wd, ws); melody ribbon smoothing 3 passes; one return after a figure means no startle on that chord. The song-mood (A half-life 1.2 s, bassS 1.5 s) governs the rest state.
snapKnobs: hold (0.8..6 s, default 2.6): how long a figure stays
tight (0..1): how crisply the birds keep formation (spring strength 0.004+0.03*coh, 0.05+0.07*coh in a figure)
trail (1..16, default 9, drive -rate): streak length in frames; 1 = short dashes
strike (0..1, default 0.6): which chords re-form it
bleed (drive +level): red heat on loud notes
presence: fewer, fainter birds, only hardest chords act
howToSnap: Set `hold` toward its minimum and trail to 1-4 (both existing knobs) for a quicker decay; for a sharper attack, cut the calm-staggered ramp (0.06+D0*0.3)*calm and 0.04+0.3*calm toward ~0.02/0.06 and raise the figure spring wf*(0.05+0.07*coh), and make the wf plateau 1.7 -> larger so the dissolve starts earlier (the figure-fade is the slow tail, 1.5 s of linear fade). Heat half-life 0.55 s and the mood half-lives (0.6 s) can be shortened. Global attack/decay scaling is only partly workable: dt-based half-lives (heat, pulse, fpulse, A, mood, formHold) scale cleanly, but spring/damping constants are per-60Hz-tick (ks, dN, dB, dB**k) and a scale on them changes stability and the figure legibility.
risk: Birds are a persistent physics state (px, py, vx, vy, history rings), the figure is a precomputed plan (buildFigure fills FX/FY/FNX/FNY per bird), and mood weights (wa, wd, ws) are blended smoothly; snapping the figure decay fights the mood blending and may leave birds mid-flight between targets. Spring/damping are per-tick (k = dt*60) and trail history is one point per frame (hp++ each frame), so results depend on frame rate and render substeps. Uses Math.random for init and jitter (jit = wa*panic*1.4*k*live, shard kicks use x.rnd) and the `notes` list is module-global, reset by reset(). Percentile gating reads global CHORDS at first use (readSong), so it depends on the whole song's chord list. Not in either protected scene.

onAttack: For each distinct pitch class in the chord (so same-pitch-class notes merge; up to 12 attractors, one per pitch class) onChord sets S[k] = max(S[k], 0.3*sqrt(vv)) (the pull starts on the attack), flares FL[k] = min(1.6, max(FL[k], vv*(0.55+0.45*min(1,burst))) + 0.15*vv), re-seeds cnt = min(420, share, round(burst*(20+190*vv^2)*(0.75+0.6*low)*(0.35+0.65*calm))) grains at the note's position as lit-near-white newborns (heat 0.7+0.3*vv, speed (45+210*vv)*..., spiral velocity) and shoves the dust within 200 px in a ring (kick = burst*200*vv*calm); the global flash = max(flash, ch.vel/127). In its own frame the attack is a core flare plus a puff of bright grains born at the note's circle position and a ring of nearby dust flung sideways, all on frame zero.
decay: Pull strength S follows sounding notes: TG[k] += sqrt(v/127)*(0.5+0.5*exp(-age/1.5)) over x.sounding() (note-length driven), then S += (min(1.8,TG)-S)*(1-exp(-dt/tau)) with tau = 0.04 s rising and tau = 0.8 s falling (so the knot lingers 0.8 s after the note stops sounding, up to 8 s windows of x.sounding()). Core flare FL[k] *= exp(-dt/(0.18+0.3*low)), tau 0.18 s for high notes up to 0.48 s for the deepest; core brightness lit = 0.18*s + 0.75*f, radius (7+12s+34f)*(0.6+0.9*low). Newborn grains: heat *= exp(-dt/0.55) (cool tau 0.55 s), drawn 'hot' (near-white) while heat > 0.45 (about 0.35 s from heat 0.85), 'fast' while heat > 0.12 (about 1.1 s), hot grains brake with hotDrag = exp(-dt*3.2) (tau 0.31 s) vs normal drag exp(-dt*0.95) (tau 1.05 s); grains keep the puff colour while heat>0.02, then ease to the colour of their strongest attractor with tau 0.5 s (kc). Global alpha: flash *= exp(-dt/0.3), stroke alpha (0.22+0.25*flash)*sqrt(4000/n). Pull force G*S/(d^2+E)*(RANGE2/(d^2+RANGE2)) with RANGE=240 px; streak length L = threads*dt (threads default 1.4). Grains are never removed, only recycled (cur++ % n) or reseeded off-screen.
lowPass: calm = 1/(1+2.5*feat.rate) divides the puff size and the ring kick (rate half-life 1.0 s); share caps one chord to half the dust shared between its pitch classes and cnt to 420; pitch classes merge (same pc notes do not show apart); REG[k] eases to the register-weighted pitch with tau 0.15 s (and a held note jumps only if S<0.05); S release tau 0.8 s; pull normalised by G = 52000*pull/max(1,total)^0.3 so many notes pull less each; quiet = 0.35 if any attractor is lit. The flare FL also is a max-kick (a soft note after a loud one adds only +0.15*vv).
snapKnobs: burst (0..2, default 0.9, less 0, drive +level): puff size, ring kick and flare strength; 0 = only a glow and the pull
threads (0.5..6, default 1.4): streak length per grain
pull (0.2..2, drive +density): how hard notes gather
amount (1000..7000): number of grains
swirl
presence: sets amount, pull, burst
howToSnap: All the slow pieces are literal tau's in frame(): the pull release 'tg > S[k] ? 0.04 : 0.8' (0.8 -> ~0.12-0.2 s makes knots vanish with the note), FL decay '0.18 + 0.3*low' (-> ~0.08 + 0.12*low), heat cool 'cool = exp(-dt/0.55)' (-> ~0.2), hotDrag 3.2 (-> ~6), the exp(-age/1.5) note-age weight and flash 0.3 s. Adding a new knob 'how fast it dies' (default 1 = today's values) that divides these taus would work and a global attack/decay scaling would apply cleanly since almost everything is an exp(-dt/tau) with a visible constant; the attack side is already instantaneous (S set to 0.3*sqrt(vv) in onChord, 0.04 s rise).
risk: S follows x.sounding(), which depends on transcribed note lengths (unreliable with pedal): a shorter release would be shortened further than the tail is long; grain positions (7000 persistent particles with velocity) are the visible 'memory', so killing them fast needs a per-grain fade or reseed, not only the field; when the field collapses the remaining grains still drift ('drift' and the elliptical wall), so the cloud would stay visible as dust. Uses Math.random (R) in seed and ignition (not x.rnd), module state `time` and `spin` are never reset in reset() (spin accumulates), stroke alpha/threads depend on dt (L = threads*dt) and jitter on sqrt(dt), so renders at different substeps will differ. Not in either protected scene.

onAttack: onChord only does pending.push(ch) (max 6 kept); the real work happens in post(), a microtask queued from frame() so it runs after every other widget has drawn this frame, which makes one streak per register group present in the chord (notes <52 go down, >=74 up, the middle sideways with the melody, an extra full-width 'tear' for pw>0.86 with 2+ notes and 0.6 s spacing), not one per note. Each streak copies the lit runs of the picture under a band of n lines (cell grid 256x144, 5 px cells), sorts each run by brightness and lays it toward the tip, with its own colour chips leading; it is drawn in the same frame that the attack happened. A caveat: the picture comes from `pix`, refreshed from a worker at most every 0.12 s of song time (a frame or two of async latency), so it sorts a picture that is typically 0.06-0.2 s old and which does not contain the shape another widget draws on this very attack; the streak's own chips and the 'seam of light' are the only parts that depend purely on the attack.
decay: Streak lifetime life = max(0.3+0.2*pw, life_knob*(0.65+0.45*pw)*(0.7+0.6*clamp(held/1.5,0,1))*(tear ? 0.6 : 1)) with life_knob default 1.3 s (0.2..3; drive -rate), so for pw=1, held=0: 1.3*1.1*0.7 = 1.0 s; held>=1.5 s: 1.86 s; soft pw=0.1: 0.63 s; minimum 0.3+0.2*pw (0.32-0.5 s), where held is the longest n.d in the streak. Growth: grow = 1-(1-min(1, age/s.grow))^3 with s.grow = 0.07 + 0.16*(1-pm) s (treble 0.07 s, bass 0.23 s, tear 0.1 s), cubic ease-out (87.5% by half the time). Then u = clamp((age - 0.35*life)/(0.65*life), 0, 1): the streak holds full length for 0.35*life and shrinks vis = round(L*grow*(1-0.75u^2)) while alpha = (0.84 + 0.16*max(0, 1-age/0.25)) * (1-u)^1.3 (so brighter by 16% for the first 0.25 s). Seam of light: seam = 0.1 + 0.12*pw s, alpha (0.7+0.3pw)*(1-age/seam) linear, width 1.5+3*pw px. Length L cells = (34+100*pw^1.15)*(1-0.3*dense)*len knob(0.75) (about 25 to 100 cells, 125-500 px), the picture it sorts is refreshed every 0.12 s of song time.
lowPass: The picture snapshot lag (refresh when |t - lastKick| >= 0.12 s, plus the worker round trip) is the main delay; pending keeps only the last 6 chords per frame; loudness is a rank relative to the recording (loud() uses the 93rd percentile velocity, floor 70) so chords are scaled by pw = 0.1+0.9*loud; dense = feat.rate thins and shortens streaks (1.25-0.55*dense lines, 1-0.3*dense length) and the life knob has drive -rate (busy shortens it); tear spacing 0.6 s; MAXSTREAKS 40; per-register aggregation (several notes -> one streak); the grow time is slower for bass (up to 0.23 s).
snapKnobs: life (0.2..3, default 1.3, less 0.2, drive -rate): streak lifetime, but floored at 0.3+0.2*pw
len (0.2..1.6, drive +level): streak length
band (0.3..2.5): lines grabbed
pick (0..0.7): what gets sorted
own (0..1): its own colour chips
presence: sets len, life, band, pick, own
howToSnap: Three literal handles: (1) the floor and plateau in the life formula: Math.max(0.3+0.2*pw, ...) -> lower floor (e.g. 0.12) and u = (age - life*0.35)/(life*0.65) -> start the shrink at ~0.1*life so the hold is short; (2) the seam and chip are the true attack: lengthen the seam peak or make own-colour chips immediate and not dependent on `pix`; (3) the 0.12 s snapshot interval (refresh) -> every frame (a readback cost) or draw a streak using last frame's own canvas, to get rid of the stale picture. Global attack/decay scaling works well: grow (0.07-0.23 s), the 0.25 s highlight, seam, life are all time constants in post()/streak(), but the picture lag is a cadence, not a time constant.
risk: Asynchronous worker + createImageBitmap readback: `pix` arrives frames later and depends on wall time/hardware, so renders are not deterministic by song time (plus Math.random for placement, ragged tips, chips). It runs from a microtask queued in frame() with `x` and `dt` captured, so any change of draw order or the 'draws AFTER all other widgets' assumption breaks it; the snapshot refresh (0.12 s) is also what makes fast streaks sort a picture which no longer matches; snappier (shorter) streaks make the stale picture more visible. The knob 'less' values and the life floor are part of presence mapping, so changing the floor affects what presence maps to unless opt-in. Not in either protected scene.

onAttack: onChord does not create a per-note object: for each chord note it finds the pen of its register (bandsFor(pens)) and kicks that pen: `p.press = Math.max(p.press, clamp(Math.pow(v,1.3)*pp))`, `p.burst = Math.max(p.burst, v)` (v=q.v/127), `p.hv += R(-1,1)*7*v` (a heading kink) and pulls `p.ty` halfway to the note's pitch. Chords with `amt = clamp((ch.vel-58)/45)*clamp(0.35+n/6) > 0.12` (almost any note above about vel 68) queue a retrace (or hatch for vel>=95 and >=4 notes) over the pen's own last 25-85 history points, plus a taper stab if `(vel>=92 && n>=3) || vel>=102` and 0.7 s since the last. In its own frame the pen is already drawing a continuous looped line, so an attack is only a brief change of speed, tremor and weight on an always-moving line, not a new mark; the retrace/stab strokes (the only discrete marks) start drawing in the same step and finish over 0.05-0.22 s.
decay: The attack is carried by four state variables, all in continuous frame() code. burst: `p.burst *= Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.14)`, half-life 0.14 s (tau 0.20 s); it adds to pen speed `vd = min(700, 120*speed*(0.6+0.6*level+2.2*p.burst))` and tremor `tr = jit*(1.2+3*p.burst)`. press (line weight/alpha): `p.press = Math.max(floor*pp, p.press*Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.8))`, half-life 0.8 s down to `floor = 0.22+0.45*x.feat.level`; width `w=(1.25+7*pr^1.3*(0.4+0.6*pp))*weight`, alpha `0.32+0.8*pr`. Heading kink hv: `p.hv -= p.hv*2.5*sdt`, tau 0.4 s. Screen shake: `shake *= Math.pow(0.82, dt*60)`, tau 0.084 s, cut at 0.3. Drawn strokes: retrace `rate = pts/2/(0.12+0.1*amt)` (0.12-0.22 s to draw), hatch `N/(0.05+0.025N)`, stab `15/0.07` = 0.07 s. Ink itself lives on a persistent layer that fades with a half-life equal to the `stay` knob: `every = stay*Math.log(1-0.08)/Math.log(0.5)` seconds per 8% step (default 7 s, min 1 s, 'less' 2.5 s; stepwise, about 0.84 s between steps at 7 s) plus a color-burn. So whatever the attack draws lingers 1-20 s; only the kick on the line is quick.
lowPass: Heavy. Tension `tension += (tgt-tension)*(1-0.5^(dt/0.5))` with `tgt = clamp(0.55*diss + 1.0*feat.rate)` (half-life 0.5 s) sets loop tightness; diss decays `0.5^(dt/1.2)` (half-life 1.2 s) and is a max over chords; pen loop radius R eases with half-life 0.3 s (`1-0.5^(dt/0.3)`); the shared feat.level/feat.rate (0.8 s / 1.0 s half-lives) set floor weight, speed and jitter; stab refractory `time - lastStab > 0.7`; burst/press are max() kicks so a soft note after a loud one does nothing; notes in the same register merge into one pen kick (per pen, not per note). The line is continuous with a speed of 120*speed px/s, so a kick shows as a short wiggle that is smeared along the path.
snapKnobs: stay: half-life of the whole sheet's fade, 1 to 20 s (default 7, 'less' 2.5); the only knob that shortens how long a stroke stays
speed: pen speed, drive +rate; scales vd including the burst term
pens: how many pens (1 to 6, default 3), one pen per register: more pens = more separate places that react to separate registers
weight: line thickness (0.3 to 2.5, default 1.2)
presence (leads): moves speed, pens and stay together
howToSnap: Two or three constants: (1) the press half-life `Math.pow(0.5, dt/0.8)` to about 0.12-0.15 and the floor `0.22+0.45*level` lower (e.g. 0.12) so the weight/alpha contrast is a spike that drops fast; (2) burst half-life 0.14 s is already quick, but raise its gain `2.2*p.burst` (and `3*p.burst` in tremor) so the kick is visible, and keep it in frame(); (3) `stay` default 7 down to ~1.5-2.5 (the less value) so the stroke drawn by the attack disappears, or add an opt-in 'sharp' knob that does 1 and 2 at once. Also `FIX.press`/the `v^1.3` power can be sharpened to `v^2` so soft notes do not press. The retrace/stab strokes are already short (0.07-0.22 s) but the persistent layer keeps them; the quick way is a shorter `stay`. A global attack/decay scaling would only partly work: `0.14`, `0.8`, `0.084` (shake) and the `every` formula could be multiplied by one `snap` factor, but the pen is always moving so the contrast comes mostly from `press` and `burst`, not from a decay time alone.
