onAttack: onChord raises the peg of each pitch class (node[pc]=max(node[pc], 0.35+0.65*n.v/110)), adds to the key histogram, and creates one polygon P per attack (attacks within 0.09 s merge into the same P, and a later note of a merged attack does P.age=min(P.age,0.03), i.e. re-strikes it). The polygon's corners are one per pitch class (plus notes still held from x.sounding()), so the attack is seen as a bowed polygon appearing in the same frame with a white-hot stroke (land), a glow, beads on the new corners, a lit peg on the rim and a shiver of the strings; a loud chord (vel>=92, >=3 notes) also kicks flash and a 5 percent scale pulse.
decay: Per polygon, age in s: atk=exp(-age/0.3) (tau 0.3 s, used in lit(), fill, glow, beads; beads and glow stop at atk<=0.05/0.06, about 0.9 s). lit(P)=atk+(1-atk)*0.45*sus with sus=pow(max(0,1-age/hold),0.7) and hold=0.5+0.85*min(4,max note duration n.d) (so a sustained 'dimmer glow' lasts 0.5 to 4.4 s, set by the transcribed note length). land=max(0,1-age/0.16): linear 0.16 s white-hot overlay. ring=exp(-age/(0.22+0.25*P.loud)): shiver envelope tau 0.22 to 0.47 s, shake=shiver*(24+36*loud)*ring*cos(TAU*(ph+age*(3.5+5*reg))). The weave remnant: a=pow(1-age/decay,1.4) with decay=9 s (knob, 0.5..30), drawn as one thin line once lit()<0.03, alpha (0.14+0.4a)*dens, width weight*(0.55+0.6loud), plus sink radius sinkK=1-0.55*0.8*min(1,age/decay)^1.5. Pegs: node[i]*=0.5^(dt/0.3) (tau 0.43 s) with a floor of 0.25*n.v/105 while the note is in x.sounding(). flash*=0.5^(dt/0.18); scale chases 1+0.05*flash with min(1,dt*30) (tau 33 ms). Trail head dot radius 2+2.5*max(0,1-age/0.4); trail points live 'decay' s. Slow context state: key histogram half-life 5 s, key rotation chase half-life 2.25 s, spinAcc half-life 1.2 s.
lowPass: Yes, several. (1) 0.09 s merge window folds rolled/jittery notes into one polygon, so two attacks within 90 ms are one. (2) Light sharing: kf=1/pow(max(1,freshSum/1.3),0.75), skf=sqrt(kf), freshSum=sum of lit(P) over all polys, so in busy passages every fresh chord is dimmed (the attack is dimmed by how many chords are still lit); dens=min(1,sqrt(28/polys.length)) dims the weave. (3) The long sus phase above keeps a chord at up to ~0.45 brightness for note-length seconds. (4) Key/rotation/spin are slow (2.25 s, 1.2 s, 5 s) and drive spin from feat.rate. Not a gate: every attack makes a polygon.
snapKnobs: decay: how long old chords stay in the weave, 0.5..30 s, default 9, less 0.8; only shortens the thin remnant, not the lit/sus phase or the shiver
shiver: amplitude of the strings' wobble, 0..1, default 0.5 (amplitude only, the tau 0.22-0.47 s is fixed)
line: string thickness 0.3..3, default 1.2
fill: shape fill 0..1, default 0.2, drive +level
bow: string curvature (not a time knob)
presence: leads decay (down to 0.8 s via less)
howToSnap: All the snappy-relevant constants are literals, so a single scale k (default 1) would work: replace 0.3 by 0.3*k in the two atk formulas (lit() and the frame body), 0.16 by 0.16*k for land, 0.22+0.25*loud by k times it for ring, the 0.5+0.85*min(4,d) hold by k times it (or drop the 0.45 sus floor, which is the part that lingers), and the 0.3 s peg half-life by 0.3*k. With k about 0.3 the lit chord is gone in roughly 0.3 s and only the thin weave line (decay knob) remains. The 0.09 s merge window should stay, and the kf/skf light-sharing is what dims fast repeated notes, so a snap mode may want freshSum computed with the shorter atk. A global attack/decay scaling works well on this widget.
risk: Low. Pure function of polys and dt, no precomputed plan, no persistence beyond the arrays; the figure is drawn on its own offscreen canvas and laid on with 'lighten', so the shared 0.12 fade does not matter. Careful points: atk is used in 5 places (fill, glow gate, core, beads, lit) and must change together; the weave switch is lit()<0.03, so shortening atk and sus moves the moment a chord drops into the weave and thus the weave's brightness step; hold from n.d depends on unreliable pedal lengths. Non-determinism: R() uses Math.random for P.j and P.ph (jitter and shiver phase), so renders are not pixel-reproducible; this must be switched to x.rnd for the pixel-identical check.

onAttack: onChord gates the attack (drops it if clock-lastBurst < gap), then queues one burst per chord: pitch of the top note chooses x (0.12+0.76*pitchRank) and the velocity rank chooses height; the burst is created in the next frame() before the fluid steps. In its own frame: a ring of n=round(7+5*power) velocity splats and dye splats plus a bright dye 'flash at its heart' (w=0.25+0.6*power) are written into the fluid on the attack frame, and m=round((26+90*power)*min(1.6,size)) sparks leave at once at sqrt(rnd(0.1,1))*(280+860*power)*size px/s, so the onset is visible in the same frame as a flash and a spark spray.
decay: Sparks: age/life with life=rnd(0.8, 1.5+0.8*power) s, alpha a=1-t^2 (t=age/life; still above 0.75 until t=0.5, then drops fast), white '#fff4e0' for t<0.2, width 1.2+1.6*(1-t); velocity vx*=exp(-1.8*dt) (tau 0.56 s) and vy=vy*drag+110*dt (gravity 110 px/s^2). Every 4th spark is a 'wake': while age<0.7*life and speed>50 (up to 18 per frame) it splats velocity s.v*0.5*swirl and dye 0.035*col into the fluid each frame, so the attack keeps feeding the smoke for 0.55 to 1.6 s. Fluid dye: advect keep=exp(-dt/(0.25+1.8*linger)), default linger 0.45 gives tau 1.06 s (linger 0 gives 0.25 s, 1 gives 2.05 s). Fluid velocity: keep=exp(-dt*0.9) (tau 1.11 s). Pressure: press*=0.8 per step (fade) then 20 Jacobi iterations; vorticity confinement k=8+26*swirl. Display: c=1-exp(-1.5*dye), so bright dye saturates and its visible life is a few tau (about 3 s at defaults). Burst ring dye 0.03+0.08*power per splat; heart flash 0.25..0.85.
lowPass: Yes, a hard gate on attacks plus a rank. Gate: gap=0.16+0.75*x.feat.rate*(1-v*0.8) with v=rank(ch.vel) (percentile of velocity among all window.NOTES); any chord arriving within gap seconds of the last burst (clock-lastBurst) is dropped entirely, so at rate about 2 per second (rate gains 1/1.44 per attack, half-life 1.0 s, so it is roughly the attacks per second) the gap is up to 1.7 s for a soft note and 0.16+0.75*rate*0.2 for the loudest. Strength: power=pow(v,1.3)*(1-0.35*rate)+0.08, a percentile, not the velocity, and damped by rate. The fluid itself low-passes: the ring of pushes needs the pressure solve and vortex roll-up to become curls, and the sparks' wakes keep stirring. One burst per chord, so a chord's notes are not separate.
snapKnobs: linger: how long the smoke hangs, 0..1, default 0.45, less 0.08; sets dye tau 0.25+1.8*linger s (the only existing way to shorten the smoke)
size: burst radius (26+60*power)*size and spark count/speed, 0.4..2.4, default 1, less 0.55
swirl: force (40+190*power)*(0.2+1.6*swirl) and vorticity, 0..1, default 0.55
hue, range: colour only
presence: leads size and linger
howToSnap: Cheapest: lower the three decays and the gate. (1) spark life rnd(0.8,1.5+0.8*power) times a factor s, and alpha 1-t^2 into a steeper (1-t)^2 or (1-t^3), (2) the wake window 0.7*life and the 18 per frame cap, (3) dye keep 0.25+1.8*linger and velocity exp(-dt*0.9) divided by s, (4) gap 0.16+0.75*rate*(1-0.8v) multiplied by something below 1 (or dropping the rate term) so each note gets its burst. A global attack/decay scaling works if it multiplies these constants and defaults to 1; the fluid onset is already sharp (the splats and heart flash are written on the attack frame).
risk: Medium. The fluid is a stateful WebGL sim whose state depends on dt (substeps n=clamp(ceil(dt*40),1,3), h=min(dt,0.1)/n), not on song time alone, so renders are only reproducible at a fixed frame rate; shortening dye keep or velocity keep alters vortex roll-up (the petals), so the look is not just 'faster'. Shorter spark life shifts the sparks' wakes that feed the fluid. The rank tables (vels, pitches) are built lazily from window.NOTES (whole song, not the clip's picks), so the percentiles stay as they are. Context limit: the fluid is dropped if the context is lost. Both scenes use it, so any change must be opt-in to keep the hashes identical.

onAttack: onChord, for every attack, hops all arrived dancers toward you (d.z=max(0.78,d.z-(0.03+0.13*vk)); d.vz-=1.1*vk, vk=clamp01((ch.vel-30)/80)), kicks the ground glow (glow=max(glow,vk)), calls a formation from the lowest note for chords of 3 or more notes (or 2 loud ones; form=((lo%12)*5+(n>=5?3:0))%9, and a loud repeat turns it by pi/6), and creates one dancer per note (bar for m<48, disc for m<76, ring above, radius lerp(40,15,...)*(0.72+0.5*nv)) that flies in out of the depth over arrT=lerp(0.14,0.03,nv) s and lands with a pop, flash and ring. The visible attack is therefore two things: the company's hop and the ground glow on the attack frame itself, and each new dancer's landing 2 to 8 frames later (loud notes fastest).
decay: Landing: arrival ease e=1-(1-arr)^3 over arrT (0.03 s loud to 0.14 s soft, minimum 0.016 s); on landing d.z=1-0.24*nv-0.04 (a pop past its size, toward you), then the z spring (omZ=om*1.25+4, zeta 0.45, with snap 0.55: om=11.15, omZ=17.9) rings and settles with envelope exp(-0.45*omZ*t)=exp(-8.05 t) (tau 0.124 s, about 0.4 s to rest). Flash: d.fl=0.25+0.75*nv, d.fl*=0.5^(dt/0.13) (tau 0.19 s), lifts the colour by fl*0.5. Ring: life 0.4+0.45*nv s, light (0.18+0.42*nv)*(1-k)^1.4, width r*(0.16+0.1*nv)*(1-0.6k), radius growth 1.08..(1.5+2.2*nv). Ground glow: glow*=0.5^(dt/0.22) (tau 0.32 s), tint alpha 0.1*glow. The dancer itself lives d.life=life*(0.75+0.5*nv)*(bar?1.15:1), with life knob 4 s, so 3.0 to 5.75 s regardless of the note's length; then it leaves over (age-left)/(1.5 s) (0.6 s if pushed out by the 26-dancer cap) and is removed at left+1.6 s. Let-go sink: after age>dur+0.05, rel rises linearly over 0.5 s (shrinks 14 percent, fog +0.1). Formation moves: x,y springs om=lerp(4,17,snap)=11.15, zeta=lerp(0.95,0.42,snap)=0.664 (tau about 0.135 s, 4 tau about 0.5 s), plus a staggered start wait=(rank/(n-1))*0.35 s on a new figure. Echoes follow with half-life lerp(0.16,0.06,snap)=0.105 s.
lowPass: Yes. (1) Arrival delay arrT: a soft note (nv=0) takes 0.14 s to land and arrives fogged (f=clamp01((z-1)/7)*0.85, zFrom=1+depth*7*(0.45+0.55*nv)+rnd*depth*0.6), so soft attacks are late and pale; a loud one is 0.03 s. (2) place() re-sorts all dancers by pitch on every attack, so every dancer's target slot moves on every note and the whole company glides (spring tau about 0.135 s, plus the 0.35 s stagger on a new figure); the individual new note is hard to isolate in that motion. (3) Cap of 26 live dancers (older ones leave early). (4) Crowd scaling crowdScale(n)=lerp(1.2,0.68,clamp01((n-3)/19)), smoothed with half-life 0.35 s, shrinks every shape when many are alive. (5) Long life 3 to 5.75 s with echoes (2) behind each. No gate or rank, but the percentile-free vk is absolute velocity.
snapKnobs: snap: glide or snap, 0..1, default 0.55; om=lerp(4,17,snap), zeta=lerp(0.95,0.42,snap), echo follow half-life lerp(0.16,0.06,snap); the only knob that sharpens motion
life: how long they dance, 1..10 s, default 4, less 1.5; the only existing way to make them die sooner
echoes: 0..4 copies behind each shape, default 2, less 0
depth: how far they fly in from, 0..1, default 0.6, drive +level; at 0 the shape pops up in place, so no arrival delay
scatter: bloom of fast runs, drive +rate
presence: leads life and echoes
howToSnap: Smallest change: make the arrival time and the death time short and the flash/z-ring tighter. arrT=lerp(0.14,0.03,nv) to a flat 0.03 (or times a snap factor) so soft notes land as sharply as loud ones; the flash half-life 0.13 to about 0.06; ring life 0.4+0.45*nv to about 0.2+0.2*nv; z-spring damping 0.45 higher (the pop rings for 0.4 s); the rel/out ramps 0.5 and 1.5 s shortened; life 4 to 1.5 by default for a snap mode (that is the 'life' knob). Making it alert to each note also needs place() to stop re-ranking old dancers on every attack, or the new note drowns in company motion; a snap mode could freeze old dancers' u (fixed slot by pitch, not rank). A global attack/decay scaling would work for flash, rings, glow, arrT and the leave ramps, but the formation slots are not time-constant based.
risk: Medium to high. Precomputed state: none, but everything is stateful (ds, rips, form, formRot, fyOff) and uses Math.random (zFrom, inner, jx, jy, spin), so renders are not pixel-reproducible; the shared 'ground' gradient and fog colours depend on d.z, so changing the z spring or arrT changes the colour of every shape. Shortening life interacts with the 26 dancer cap, place() ranks and the formation staggers (d.wait) and so changes the picture in dense passages, and the removal condition d.z>1+depth*7+2.5 || d.age>d.left+1.6 depends on the knob 'depth'. The scene uses it (liebesleid), so defaults must stay identical.

onAttack: onChord does three things: it may add a threat (a loud chord of >=3 notes with vel>=avgVel+12 bursts inside the flock (void, hairline ring, plus a ring of already-running shapes), a low chord (lo<50) rises a bass threat from the bottom at the bass note's x, and a melody leap >=7 semitones in a note>=57 blows up the old spot); it makes every frozen shape (and 30 percent of the others) flinch on the attack frame (position jitter 2+10*tw px, heading kick s.off, flash=max(s.flash,0.25)); and it spawns one new shape per upper note (the highest 4, or 6 when panic>0.5, only for m>=57 and with probability pSpawn=0.4+0.6*panic). The visible attack is the white-hot flash of a new shape (flash=1) plus the flinch of existing ones, in the attack's own frame; the new shape is then frozen and only bolts after the hesitation.
decay: Per shape (age s): fin=min(1,age/0.05) fade-in; flash*=0.5^(dt/0.08) (tau 0.115 s), heat=max(s.heat,s.flash) picks the sprite's heat bucket and the shape's size grows by 0.35*flash and alpha by (0.45+0.55*heat); s.heat chases max(target,0.06) with rate min(1,dt*14) (tau 0.071 s) where target=pow(min(1,v/2400),0.85). Hesitation: shape is frozen with tremble until age>0.06+s.hes, hes=hesOf(x)*rnd(0.5,1.5) and hesOf=clamp(0.55-0.6*feat.rate, 0, 1.2) (so 0.28..0.83 s when calm, about 0.06 s when busy). Bolt: position D*(t/T)^e, speed v=min(3200, e*D*t^(e-1)/T^e)*slow, e=3, T=rnd(0.8,1.2)*(1.15-0.45*panic) (0.9..1.4 s calm, 0.55..0.8 s panicked), D=rnd(0.8,1.2)*(260+420*panic) px; shapes live until age 7 s or until they leave the screen (margin 260 px), with fout=min(1,(7-age)/1) in the last second. Threats: life 0.9 s (loud) or 0.7 s, void alpha (1-age/life), hairline ring only for age<0.12 s expanding at 1400 px/s; push w=str*resp*exp(-d^2/R^2)*(1-age/life); bass threat vy*=0.5^(dt/0.5). Panic: panic chases smooth(0.12,0.6,feat.rate) with half-life 0.4 s.
lowPass: Yes, many. (1) Spawn probability pSpawn=0.4+0.6*panic (calm music: 40 percent of the upper notes show nothing; rnd via Math.random) and only m>=57, highest 4 (or 6) notes per attack. (2) The hesitation freeze 0.06+hes (0.34 to 0.88 s) before any motion, so the shape that the note made only does something after about half a second when calm. (3) Cooldowns: loud threat 0.25 s, bass 0.2 s, leap 0.3 s, plus avgVel running average (avgVel += (vel-avgVel)*0.04) so a loud chord must exceed the average by 12. (4) panic smoothing half-life 0.4 s. (5) Shapes persist up to 7 s; the speed curve t^3 starts slowly, so at the start the shape is dim (alpha 0.45*...) and nearly still. With presence below 1: hardNote/hardChord percentile cuts and slow=1-0.8*(1-pres) clock scaling.
snapKnobs: exp: how sudden the bolt, 1..5 step 0.1, default 3; larger = slower creep then faster shoot (speed curve t^(exp-1))
twitch: how jumpy 0..1, default 0.25, drive +rate; sets flinch size/heading kick on every attack (jitter 2+10*tw) and heading snap rate
streak: trail length 0..3, default 0.8, drive +rate
mix, pal: shape and colour only
presence: 0..1, default 1; sets which attacks count (percentile cut), flinch/twitch amplitude, fade and slow, but lowers presence = fewer shapes, not snappier
howToSnap: The flash (tau 0.115 s) and the flinch are already sharp; what blunts the attack is the freeze and the 7 s lifetime. Smallest change: cut the hesitation (0.06+hes) to about 0.04 and the hesitation default 0.55 in hesOf to about 0.1 so the bolt starts within a few frames, tighten e*D*t^(e-1)/T^e by smaller T (T=rnd(0.8,1.2)*(1.15-0.45*panic) to about 0.4), and set the death by lifespan (age<7 to ~2 s with fout over 0.3 s) so the shape does not hang around dim; plus pSpawn to 1 so every upper note shows. These are literal constants (hesOf's 0.55 base is a drv base), so a global time-scale factor works in principle (multiply hes, T, 7 and the 0.08 flash half-life), but note that hesOf and threatOf explicitly keep the drives of removed knobs, and the T/D curve is intertwined with 'slow' from presence; any scaling must be 1 at defaults.
risk: Medium. Uses Math.random heavily (pSpawn, type, twitch, flinch, 30 percent flinch pick), so frames are not reproducible; it uses a sprite cache (get(), budget 4 builds per frame) keyed by heat bucket, so faster heat changes only reuse existing buckets (fine) but make bucket changes jump; the flock loop is O(n^2) up to 110 shapes; shortening lifetimes/hesitation changes the density the flock behaviour (alignment, cohesion within 160 px) sees and thus the look of the whole scene; threats' shove w depends on resp and age. Liebesleid uses it ('accents' flee), so any change must be opt-in.

onAttack: onChord feeds the bass guess (hist[ch.lo%12] += (0.4+min(2, duration of the lowest note))*(0.5+pw) if lo<64), kicks lv=max(lv,pw) and flash=max(flash,0.35+0.65*pw), for chords of >=3 notes accumulates the 'flip' knob and swaps which half is the source (side^=1) on that frame (an instant switch of the mirror), for a loud chord (pw>0.72 and >=2 notes) sets bump (an extra fold that relaxes), and adds one stitch per note at a distance by pitch (d=0.04+0.92*pitch01). Seen in its own frame as a white-hot flash of the seam and per-note stitches on the same frame; the mirror image of whatever other widgets drew is redrawn every frame.
decay: flash*=0.5^(dt/0.09) (tau 0.13 s) drives the seam colour (to white), line width (1+1.6f) and stitch length (1+1.4f). Stitches: life=0.5+0.7*pw s, alpha=few*pow(1-u,1.5)*min(1,0.3+seam) with u=age/life, length st.len*(0.4+0.6*seam)*(1-0.5*u), width 1.2+2.2*seam*(1-u). bump=max(0,bump-dt/0.6) linear 0.6 s, applied as smoothstep b^2(3-2b) to the extra fold's alpha. lv*=0.5^(dt/3) (half-life 3 s), driving the mirror strength a=strength*(0.6+0.4*clamp((lv-0.1)/0.35,0,1)). The axis: ang chases target with half-life 0.22 s, echo (lagging seam) chases ang with half-life 0.9 s, hist (bass guess) *= 0.5^(dt/1.2). The mirrored picture itself decays however the other widgets' content decays (the copy is of the shared canvas, so it inherits the 0.12/frame fade and the other widgets' envelopes); fold has no envelope of its own on the mirror besides lv.
lowPass: Partly. The mirror strength is smoothed by lv (half-life 3 s), so quiet passages fade the mirror to 60 percent only after several seconds without a loud chord; the axis chases its target with half-life 0.22 s and the bass guess averages over about 2 s (hist half-life 1.2 s), so the line turns slowly with harmony, not with single notes; the 'flip' knob quantises (flipAcc) which chords swap sides. Per-note stitches and the flash are immediate; pw=0.1+0.9*loud(vel) is relative to this song's 93rd percentile velocity (VQ=max(70, v[0.93])).
snapKnobs: seam: the line of light along the fold, 0..1, default 0.6; scales stitch/seam brightness, not the time constants
strength: opacity of the mirror image, 0..1, default 1
flip: how often a chord swaps the source half, 0..1, default 0.5
turn: how much the fold turns with the bass, 0..1, default 1
folds: 1..6 mirror lines
howToSnap: The seam flash is already sharp: flash tau 0.13 s, stitches 0.5 to 1.2 s. To snap it: shorten the stitch life (0.5+0.7*pw to about 0.2+0.25*pw) and steepen pow(1-u,1.5) to about 2.5; halve flash half-life 0.09; shorten bump (0.6) and lv (3 s) so the mirror's brightening fades faster; the ang chase (0.22 s) is what makes the line turn late, so a snap mode could shorten it to about 0.08 s. These are all literals, so a global scaling works. But the mirror image itself belongs to the other widgets, so fold cannot make the picture snappier than its sources.
risk: Low to medium. It is a post-pass (queueMicrotask from frame(), RENDER_POST in render mode) that copies the entire canvas, so it only changes the seam/stitches/strength; the mirror image and its fades are determined by other widgets. No randomness, deterministic. Care: ang/echo/hist/side/lv are persistent state across frames, so a seek in time is not reproducible (the state is not rebuilt, unlike gliss), and lv 3 s memory is read at the frame of the post pass. Not in either scene, so changes are free, but note that it relies on k read in frame() (knobs) before the post.

onAttack: onChord is empty. Nothing is made in response to the attack as it arrives: planNow() builds a plan once from the global CHORDS (hits {t, m, v}), splits it into sweeps (a silence >=0.8 s ends one; a stretch >6 s is searched for fast climbs), and frame() steps a fixed 1/60 s fluid up to song time x.t. For each hit, K.number (default 18) pulses are scheduled at tk=n.t+rnd(...)*0.07 s, each a small dye splat and a shove away from the unseen point on the bell (the point at time tk), all injected in the frame that crosses tk. Seen in its own frame as up to 18 small warm puffs spread over 70 ms (mean 35 ms after the attack) along the bell, not as a flash.
decay: Dye: advect keep exp(-dt*ln2/linger) per 1/60 s step, i.e. half-life = linger = 0.6 s by default (tau 0.87 s; the knob goes 0.2..3 s, less 0.25), with extra numerical diffusion from the 5-tap blur in advect (0.4 centre + 4*0.15 at 0.3 texel) and a glow pass (5 blur iterations at 256x144) added to the picture. Velocity: keep exp(-dt*TIRE), TIRE=1.1 (tau 0.91 s); vorticity confinement SWIRL=10 each step; warm lift velocity.y += LIFT*dt*dye with LIFT=14, so the dye keeps accelerating itself upward while it exists. Pulse sizes: dye v*(0.2+0.24c) with v=n.v/70, velocity push f=760*push*v*(0.55+0.9a), radius r=0.000045*size^2*(0.5+1.1b). Display: e=(dye*1.5+glow*1.2)*1.6, c=1-exp(-e*tint) with tint about 4.2, so dye above about 0.3 is saturated white and dye must fall far below that to disappear (visible life about 5 tau, several seconds). Window: the sim only runs while a run exists: run.end = last sweep's t1 + tail, tail=clamp(linger*6,1.5,12) (3.6 s default), and the picture is faded to nothing over the last 0.4 s (uAll = 1-smooth((t-(end-0.4))/0.4)), so it ends in a hard cut.
lowPass: Yes, strongly. (1) SPREAD=0.07: a note's pulses are spread uniformly over 70 ms after it (so attack = a smear), (2) no response between notes except via the path, (3) the dye/glow saturation and slow decay (half-life 0.6 s, saturating display) smooth over note boundaries, so a fast run merges into one cloud (that is what the widget was made for), (4) the bell shape: position of pulses follows heightAt/pathX (smooth), not the note, so individual notes are not separately visible; only their time offset along the bell. Everything is also dependent on the note set via the plan: sweeps need >=1 hit; MAX_SWEEP=6 s. No gate on velocity, but v=n.v/70 is absolute, not ranked.
snapKnobs: linger: seconds until the light has half faded, 0.2..3, default 0.6, less 0.25; the only existing way to shorten the dye life, also shortens the tail window (tail=clamp(linger*6,1.5,12))
number: pulses per note, 2..40, default 18, less 4
push: how hard pulses shoot away, 0..3, default 1
size: radius of each pulse, 0.2..3, default 1
hue: colour only
presence: leads number and linger
howToSnap: Everything that smears the attack is a constant: SPREAD 0.07 to about 0.01 (all pulses of a note at the attack), linger lower by default for a snap mode (0.2 gives tau 0.29 s), TIRE 1.1 to about 3, and the display curve (the saturating 1-exp(-e*tint)) gain lowered or a power applied so low dye is invisible sooner. LIFT (14) should be reduced or the dye keeps pushing itself. A global attack/decay scaling can multiply SPREAD, linger-derived keep, TIRE and the tail, but not the bell path (heightAt/pathX are song-time curves), and the per-note identity is lost anyway because pulses are placed on the bell by time, not on the note. It is not the right widget for 'each note readable'; for that the pulses would need to be at the note's own pitch position.
risk: Medium to high. The sim is replayed from the start of the sweep after a seek (REPLAY=6 s, fixed STEP=1/60), so it is a deterministic function of song time and knobs, and that must be kept: changing constants must be baked into the knobs/K values, not into wall time. The plan comes from the global CHORDS and is cached at module level (plan) and reset() only clears simT, so if the harness changes the note set (picks) the plan is not rebuilt unless the harness reloads the module; I did not check how the studio does it with five instances in the Rachmaninoff scene. One shared WebGL context for all instances (window.__glissGl); both scenes use it (liebesleid x2, rach x5), so defaults must stay pixel-identical.

onAttack: blow(ch,x) ranks the attack against the whole piece (percentile) and against the last 2.5 s (local rank, dense), then calls addWedge once per kept note (at most 5 per chord, only the outer 2 in a dense jab); each wedge is a body sliver plus a needle plus k=round(4+11p+3(1-s)) strands, and a 'full' blast (raw>=0.98, >1.1 s since the last) adds 10 afterburn strands, a 44-needle front at 2900 px/s, and a lurch of the picture. In its own frame the wedge grows in the same frame as the attack: front = L*q.tip*ease with ease = 1-(1-min(1,a/0.1))^3, i.e. 42% of its length after one 60 Hz step, 87% at 50 ms, 100% at 0.1 s, while push() writes the wedge into the air grid at once (V = 320+1500*own px/s) and the body sliver is solid only for brief = 0.07+0.14p s.
decay: Wedge life = (0.34+0.95*own)*(jab ? 1-0.35*dense : 1)*linger*(full ? 2 : 1) s (0.34-1.29 s at linger 1, up to 2.58 s on a full blast). Decay does not start at the attack: after = max(0, a-hold), hold = n.d>0.25 ? min(n.d, 0.6+3*own) : 0.05 (so a held loud note burns up to 3.6 s; in a dense run hold -> min(held, jab ? 0.08 : 0.5)). A strand dies when after > life*q.long (long 0.65-1.1; body 0.42 but cut by brief; needle 0.6; afterburn 0.9-1.5, so up to ~3.9 s). Shapes: fade = 1 - after/(life*long) (linear), width scale (0.35+0.65*fade), heat = round(top*(1-t01)^2), body scale = 1 - a/brief (linear, 0.07-0.21 s). Air grid: dec = 0.5^(dt/0.34) per step (half-life 0.34 s, advected). Dashes relax to the flow with k = 1-exp(-dt*(gs>50 ? 11 : 1.6)) (tau 0.09 s while pushed, 0.625 s otherwise) and then carry on and curl. Shove spring: shoveV += (-shove*90 - shoveV*11)*dt (omega 9.5 rad/s, zeta 0.58, envelope tau about 0.18 s, lurch = p^3*(full?34:15)*26 only when p>0.5). Full front lives about (2048+800)/2900 = 0.98 s.
lowPass: No time delay or smoothing, but heavy gating and ranking: loudness is a percentile of this piece's attacks, a dense run (>2.5 attacks/s, smoothstep to 6) turns most attacks into short jabs with hard = (0.1+0.26*rank)*clamp(since/0.8,0.45,1), accents need since>=0.45 s and rank>=0.86-0.3*clamp((since-0.5)/1.5,0,1), full blasts are at least 1.1 s apart, hold collapses to 0.5/0.08 s in dense runs, one 'gale' mouth/heading is held through a run (reset after a 0.6 s lull), and MAX_WEDGES 26, MAX_SLIVERS 420, a painted-area budget (W*H*0.2, squeeze) and half of the air dashes are dropped under a heavy climax.
snapKnobs: linger (0.25-3.5, default 1): multiplies wedge life, so 0.25 gives life 0.085-0.32 s; does not touch hold, the air grid, the shove or the afterburn separately
reach (0.4-1.6): shorter wedges, less area to shed
power (0-1): scales how hard every attack blows (lift curve), so smaller, shorter-lived wedges
air (0-1): number of dashes, 0 removes the cloud the wedges push
presence (leads): sets air, reach, linger and power together (less values 0.1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.25)
howToSnap: Attack is already alert (same frame, 42% grown after one step, body sliver brief). To die quicker, three constants carry it: line 143 `life: (0.34 + 0.95 * own) * ... * x.p('linger')` (and the afterburn `long` 0.9-1.5), line 139-141 `held`/`hold` (cap `held` to about 0.12-0.2 s in snap mode, otherwise a held piano note burns up to 3.6 s regardless of linger), and line 263 `dec = Math.pow(0.5, dt / 0.34)` (about 0.12-0.15 for a short air memory), optionally the shove spring `-shoveVX*11` (raise damping to ~18). A global decay scale would work: every duration is a plain number (life, hold, 0.34, 11/1.6, the brief and the spring) applied to age-integrated objects, so one multiplier `snap` read from a knob, with default 1.0 leaving all formulas unchanged, does it; linger alone cannot, because of hold and the air grid.
risk: The scene's two gust clips must stay pixel-identical at defaults, so every change has to be opt-in (a new knob whose default reproduces today's numbers). The random stream is order-sensitive: x.rnd is consumed per wedge and per sliver (k depends on p), so changing sliver counts or call order shifts every later blast of the whole song; do not change how many rnd calls happen. Note Math.random() already sets each dash's curl sign (non-deterministic at creation), module-level state (time, sinceFull, recent, gale, dashes) is not all cleared by reset(), the eviction rule uses u.hold and u.life (shorter lives change which wedge is dropped over the 26 cap), and the painted-area budget/thinning (painting, squeeze, AIR_THINS) is tuned for long lives, so much shorter lives make it rarely engage and changes the climax look and cost.

onAttack: onChord makes one wave per note for the 3 loudest notes of the chord plus the lowest note (so up to 4), each with x placed by pitch (W*(0.06+0.88p)+-30), random y, amp=(0.42+0.5*low)*vv where vv=0.4*n.v/110+0.6*min(1.3,n.v/max(50,ref)) and ref is a slow running loudness (ref += (vel-ref)*0.08), speed sp=140+900p^2 px/s and ring width w=22+120*low^2; chords with vel>=96 and >=4 notes also add kick (+0.6+(vel-96)/30, cap 1.2) and vel>=100 with >=5 notes flip the red plate to negative (>=1.2 s apart). In its own frame the wave is seen at once as a source blob of swelling dots at its origin, src = amp*1.15*exp(-age/0.16), which is about 90% on the first step, then a ring front R = sp*(0.85+0.7*feat.rate)*age expanding outward with a crest and a fainter trailing crest.
decay: Ring amplitude env = exp(-age/(life*(0.6+0.4*min(2, dur+0.4)))) with life = p('life')*(1-0.3*feat.rate) (default 2.2 s), so tau is 1.76 s for a short note (dur 0.1) up to 3.08 s for dur>=1.6 s, before the feat.rate factor; a wave is skipped when env<0.03 and deleted at age >= life*2.5 (5.5 s); at the left end of the knob (0.4) tau is 0.32-0.56 s. Source blob exp(-age/0.16) (tau 0.16 s). kick *= 0.5^(dt/0.12) (half-life 0.12 s) raising base = 0.06+kick*0.06 and kickRot *= 0.5^(dt/0.25) (rotation 0.05 rad), flip *= 0.5^(dt/0.09) (half-life 0.09 s, neg = flip*0.6). Held-chord stripes: a = (n.v/110)*min(1,age/0.25)*exp(-age/5) for the 6 loudest of x.sounding(), a ramp up over 0.25 s then tau 5 s, and gone the moment the note leaves sounding(); they add min(0.26, standing*0.3*st). The ring keeps travelling at sp*speed after the envelope fades.
lowPass: Partly: the standing stripes ramp in over 0.25 s and last 5 s (but follow sounding); the contrast knob is driven '+level' so after a loud note the print stays harder for the shared pulse's 0.8 s half-life; life shrinks and speed grows with feat.rate (slow 1 s half-life); ref is a running mean; only the loudest 3 notes plus the bass print; ink is shared across a crowd of waves (k = 1/max(1,sa/3.2)^0.68), so a dense passage prints each wave fainter; flip has a 1.2 s cooldown; waves capped at 36. Nothing delays the attack itself.
snapKnobs: life (0.4-6, default 2.2, less 0.8): the wave tau scales with it, 0.4 gives a quick pulse of 0.3-0.6 s
contrast (0-1, drive +level): high = hard stamp, each dot full or gone, which reads sharper
standing (0-1.5, drive +density, less 0.1): 0 removes the sounding-based stripes
grid (10-44) and shape: dot size and form, bigger dots read as a quicker pulse
presence (leads): sets life and standing together
howToSnap: Attack is already immediate (source blob exp(-age/0.16) in the first frame). The decay is one formula: line 92 `env = Math.exp(-age / (life * (0.6 + 0.4 * Math.min(2, w.dur + 0.4))))` plus the removal `life * 2.5` on line 98, and the knob alone reaches 0.4; for a stronger snap add a multiplier on that tau (e.g. x0.3), shorten `exp(-age/0.16)` in line 96 to about 0.07, and make the stripes skip the 0.25 s ramp and exp(-age/5) (line 108) so they end with the note. A global attack/decay scale would work for the waves because they are closed-form functions of age (nothing precomputed), but the ring speed would then want to scale too, otherwise the ring dies near its origin; kick and flip are already quick.
risk: The rach-concerto-2 halftone clip must stay identical at defaults, so any change is opt-in. The ink-sharing normalisation (sa over live waves) means that changing life changes total ink and the whole look of a passage; waves are removed by a hard age cut at life*2.5. Time is the widget's own clock (time += x.dt, waves use closed-form age so substeps agree), but kickRot uses Math.random() so the kick direction is not deterministic, and the standing pattern depends on x.sounding() (seek behaviour). Dot paths are rebuilt every frame, so there is no persistence to break.

onAttack: onChord tunes the pendulums to the chord (or a lone note against x.sounding()) and then only nudges shared state: pen.Et = min(1.1, Et + push*k*0.6*(1.12-Et)) with k=(vel/110)^1.3, press = max(press, min(1.5, push*(0.2+1.1k))), rush = min(2.2, rush+0.18+0.5k), a knot {r=(1.4+6k)*min(1.3,push)} when k>0.12, and a melody bend; a change of harmony retunes and dims the old ink by 10% at most every 0.6 s. There is one pen and one continuous line, so in its own frame the attack shows only in the newly drawn segment of that frame (pen advance = speed*rate*dt, about 0.03 turns per step): thicker (wk includes 0.75+2.2*pr), brighter and white-hot, with a radial-gradient bead at pts[1] and a stronger glow on the pen head.
decay: press *= 0.5^(dt/0.16) (half-life 0.16 s) and rush *= 0.5^(dt/0.6) (half-life 0.6 s; rush speeds the pen: rate=(0.7+0.65reg)*(0.75+0.55*min(1.6,rush))). The swing size decays along the line, not in seconds: Et *= exp(-damp*d) per pen advance d (damp 0.2) and E follows Et with min(1,d/0.12), so the e-fold time is about 1/(damp*speed*rate) = 1.4-6 s (3 s typical). What was drawn persists on its own canvas: fade per frame ease(dt, stay) = 1-0.5^(dt/stay) with stay 4.5 s default (half-life 4.5 s) plus a colour-burn, so a thick knot and bright stroke stay, then fade, over several seconds; the pen head tail (48 points) is redrawn each frame. Retune of pendulums: ease(dt,0.22); abs colour ease(dt,0.35); tilt ease(dt,2); amplitude weights ka=min(1,d/0.25).
lowPass: Strongly: the figure melts between harmonies over about a quarter second (ease 0.22), E follows Et over 0.12 of pen advance, Et saturates (1.12-Et factor, cap 1.1) so repeated attacks add less, press is a max not a sum, rush adds only 0.18+0.5k up to 2.2 and decays slowly, knots only for k>0.12 (about vel>22), retune happens only when the interval set changes, the old-ink dimming is limited to once per 0.6 s, and the picture is path-dependent (a seek rebuilds from x.sounding()).
snapKnobs: push (0-1.5, default 0.8): scales press, the swing bump and the knot, 0 = notes do nothing
damp (0.02-0.6, default 0.2): how fast the line winds in toward the centre between notes
stay (0.3-8, default 4.5, less 0.3): the half-life of the drawn line; 0.3 leaves only a comet tail
speed (0.3-5, default 1.6, less 0.4): how fast the pen draws, so how much line one attack makes
presence (leads): sets speed and stay together
howToSnap: With existing knobs the response is already shortenable (stay about 0.5, damp 0.6, push 1.5), but two constants cannot be reached: line 237 `press *= Math.pow(0.5, dt / 0.16)` and line 238 `rush ... 0.6`, and the attack is only as sharp as one frame of pen line. Smallest opt-in change: add a flash drawn at the moment of the attack (a one-frame bead or ring at the pen position independent of pen speed, using knots which already exists) and scale stay, damp and the 0.16/0.6 half-lives by one factor (lines 154, 165, 237, 238). A global scale would work for the time-based parts (stay, press, rush) but the swing decay is arc-based (exp(-damp*d)), so damp must be scaled as well; the figure geometry and retune speed (0.22 s) should stay.
risk: The figure is a path integral (phases th accumulate, Et/E are states), so any change to push, damp or the swing envelope alters every later figure, not just the response; rendering at different dt splits steps differently (n, rem), so seek and playback already differ slightly. The offscreen canvas holds history in pixels (stay, colour-burn floor; supersampled renders differ at thin old lines, see the in-file note), so a short stay changes the drawn picture globally and the harness's own fade does not apply. Not in either scene, so low scene risk.

onAttack: For every note in the chord, onChord finds the nearest mass (by pitch x and a little by height) and weighs on it: swell += w*fat^2*7 (fills over seconds), weigh(near, 2+6*w*fat, T) which adds to the sink targets sqT and hangT by drop*0.5 (capped) and sets glow = max(glow, T/(1+0.05*rate)), where T=0.3+0.6*min(1,0.5w+0.5w/max(lvl,0.2)) and lvl is a 3 s running mean of the weight; its threads get dipT += 1+2.5w, V up and the same glow. Only some notes make a new object (a bud, or a grown mass), gated by quantile(n.v)>=(1-busy)*0.9 or a 3-7 s wait, 0.5-1.1 s since the last bud, max 2 per chord. In its own frame the mass and its threads flush pale at once (glow up to about 0.9, blended as 0.6*glow toward the pale tone) and the lower lobes begin to sink within a tenth of a second.
decay: Flush: n.glow *= exp(-dt*(1.3+1.07*n.rate)) with rate += 1 per attack and rate *= exp(-dt/1.5), so tau = 1/(1.3+1.07*rate): 0.77 s with no recent hits, 0.42 s after one, 0.22 s in a run; threads l.glow decays the same. The sink: sq += (sqT-sq)*(1-exp(-dt/0.04)) (half arrives in about 0.03-0.1 s), and sqT relaxes by min(sqT*0.35, 1.1)*sqrt(tk)*dt (35% per second, at most 1.1 units/s, so seconds); tk=2^((0.5-thick)*3.4). The other half of a drop: hang follows hangT at rate 0.8*sqrt(tk) (tau about 1.25 s) and then creeps into n.y at 0.06*tk per s (tau about 17 s), never returning. Thread dip: dip follows dipT with tau 0.25 s, dipT relaxes like sqT. Volume fill: swell converts at 1.3*sqrt(tk)/s (tau 0.77 s); vol decays 0.013/s (tau 77 s), thread V 0.018/s (tau 55 s), thread sag follows at 0.22*tk/s (tau 4.5 s).
lowPass: By design, a heavy low-pass of the music (droopy, viscous, slow): attacks add to targets that are followed slowly, the volume fills over about 0.8 s and then a bud crawls out slowly, T is normalised by a 3 s mean, glow is divided by (1+0.05*rate) and decays faster in a run (explicit 'each attack in a run still shows'), new masses are gated (busy quantile cut, 3-7 s wait, 0.5-1.1 s spacing, <=2 per chord, MAX_NODES 11, moving<4), notes pick the nearest mass so several notes weigh on the same one, and sq/dip are additive-capped (<=10 units).
snapKnobs: thick (0-1, default 0.5): tk=2^((0.5-thick)*3.4) from 0.31 to 3.25 scales the sink relaxation, fill, sag, dip and drift rates; does not scale the glow decay
load (0.25-2.2, less 0.25): how heavy a note is (sink and flush strength)
busy (0-1, less 0): how many notes push out a new shape
stretch (0-1, less 0.2): how far a thread stretches before it snaps
presence (leads): sets busy, load and stretch together
howToSnap: The visible attack is the flush plus the 0.04 s sink, and the slow part is the flush decay and the sink relaxation. Raise the constant in line 251 `n.glow *= Math.exp(-dt * (1.3 + 1.07 * n.rate))` (and the same in line 289 for threads) from 1.3 to about 6 (tau 0.15 s) for a flush that is gone in about 0.4 s; speed the sink back in line 248 `Math.min(n.sqT * 0.35, 1.1)` (e.g. 2.0 and 6) and the dip in line 288; leave hang/creep (permanent drop) alone. A global attack/decay scale is possible on those few exp(-dt*k) constants, but a global scale on the whole widget would destroy its character and the topology (buds, melts), so it should apply to glow and the transient sq/dip only.
risk: Topology is stateful and random-driven (nodes, links, bud/grow/melt/snap, x.rnd call order), so touching gating or anything that feeds n.y, n.R or distances (hang, creep, vol, swell) changes the whole later picture; glow, sq and dip feed only drawing (collisions use x, y, R), so those are safe to change. The metaball field is a 640x360 CPU loop with putImageData every frame; glow is carried in a second field G, so a shorter glow makes the pale patches smaller but costs nothing extra. Path-dependent state is not reproducible by a seek except by re-running chords after reset(). Not in either scene.

onAttack: onChord first gates by presence (hardEnough: only notes above the percentile cut (1-pres)*0.95 of this piece) then does flash = min(1.2, flash+0.35*(vel/115)^1.5*pres), a bloom when vel>70 (amp=min(1.3,((vel-70)/50)^1.4*sh*pres), radius 160+70*min(6,n)+rnd(0,60), life 2.6+0.6*min(4,n)), and one glint per note: x by pitch (W*(0.1+0.8p)+-40), amp=sh*vel/127*(n>3 ? 0.55+1.4/n : 1)*(0.55+0.45p), len (26+110(1-p))*..., runner speed (50+160p)*..., life (1.6+2.8*min(1,d/2))*(0.7+0.3sh), and a water trace for vel>0.66. In its own frame the glint strikes at once as a short bloom at its x (alpha amp*env*0.55*max(0,1-age/0.6), so full on the first step) and two runners then travel both ways along the horizon, while flash lights the horizon line itself in the same frame; a bloom ramps in over 0.08 s.
decay: Glint envelope env=(1-u)^1.8 with u=age/life, life 1.6-4.4 s at shimmer 1 (x(0.7+0.3sh)), runners d = sp*age*(1-0.35u) and length L=len*(0.7+0.8u); the strike bloom fades linearly over 0.6 s; water trace amp refl*env*0.3. flash *= 0.5^(dt/0.45) (half-life 0.45 s, lights the line with 0.45*flash). Bloom env = min(1,age/0.08)*(1-u)^2.2 over life 3.2-5 s. Contrast: con += (tgt-con)*(1-0.5^(dt/((rising ? 0.3 : 2.2)/pres))) (quick up, 2.2 s down; the contrast knob is driven '+level'). Harmony tint ease half-life 1.4 s (kh), per-note weight (0.35+0.65*exp(-(t-start)/1.5)) while sounding; horizon position is critically damped with omega 2.2*max(0.25,pres) (tau about 0.45 s). The sea drifts at 3-5 px/s and breathes with 0.21/0.087 rad/s sines.
lowPass: Intentionally nearly everything: the picture is meant to be almost still. Glint and bloom lives of 1.6-5 s, flash half-life 0.45 s, contrast and tint smoothers (0.3/2.2 s and 1.4 s), the critically damped horizon, a presence gate (only the hardest notes at low presence) with calm/glow scaling that slows and dims the glints, chords of more than 3 notes get less amp each, and a cap of 140 glints / 12 blooms. Attack onset is not delayed except the bloom's 0.08 s ramp.
snapKnobs: shimmer (0-2, default 1): scales glint amp, length, speed and (x(0.7+0.3sh)) life, 0 leaves only the line light
presence (0-1, default 1): fewer, harder-only notes, slower (calm) and dimmer glints; also sinks the whole picture toward black
contrast (drive +level): sky/sea separation, how stark
soft: how sharp the line is (sharp line = a crisper hairline for the flash)
howToSnap: Shorten the glint and the flash: line 140 `life: (1.6 + 2.8 * Math.min(1, no.d / 2)) * ...` to roughly 0.3-0.8 s, the envelope exponent 1.8 on line 231 (up to about 3), the strike bloom window `1 - s.age / 0.6` on line 234 (to about 0.15), `flash *= Math.pow(0.5, dt / 0.45)` on line 158 (to about 0.12), the bloom life 2.6+0.6n on line 128 and its 0.08 ramp on line 217 (to 0.01). A global scale would work because all the dynamic parts are age/life based objects (glints, blooms) plus the flash half-life, and a snap multiplier with default 1.0 would leave the current formulas unchanged; it stays at odds with the widget's intent (quiet, meditative), so it should be a separate opt-in 'quick glints' knob rather than a change of default.
risk: Horizon is unshifted to be painted first and repaints the whole frame (so it ignores the harness fade and everything below belongs to it); its film grain uses Math.random() for the pattern offset each frame, so frames are not deterministic or hash-stable; the horizon spring and contrast smoother are explicit integrators dependent on dt; time += dt*pres; glints/blooms hold arrays and a 140 cap; flash also lights the line, so changing flash changes the whole picture's light, not just glints. Not in either scene, so low scene risk.

onAttack: For each note with v>=softest(pres), onChord pushes {m, v, t0, end: t + max(0.6, n.d)} to the barcode list and injects two inverted glyphs at the right edge of a data row picked by pitch; loud attacks (vel >= max(80, ref-8), cooldown 0.1 s) add round(k*(2+(vel-78)*0.35)*(0.6+0.2n)) single-pixel slam lines, k=slam*pres^2, and attacks with vel >= max(90, ref-3), cooldown 1.4 s, pass a hash gate (hh(t*991) < flash*1.15*(2*pres-1)) set flashT=0.1 for a full-screen difference flash. In its own frame it is the most direct of the six: the screen is repainted on a black ground every frame, and the barcode spans the whole height (top=0, bottom=H) at alpha 1 for age<0.12 s with an on/off strobe at 30 Hz between 0.03 and 0.16 s (hidden when hh < 0.45*wall), a hairline frame, and slam lines shooting out (reach=min(1,age/0.05+0.35)).
decay: Barcode erosion: while sounding erode = 0.2*min(1,age/max(0.5,end-t0))*(1-v/160), then after n.end = t0+max(0.6, n.d): erode = 0.2+0.8*((t-n.end)/life)^1.4 with life default 1.2 s (each bar e<erode disappears, e random per bar), so a note is on screen at least 0.6 s + 1.2 s, and a held note stays for its transcribed length + life; pruned at t >= end+life+0.05. Settling: from age 0.12 the code collapses from full height into its note-name row with k = 1-(1-min(1,(age-0.12)/0.5))^3 (0.5 s cubic ease-out), the label glyphs show when k>0.6 and erode<0.6. Fresh data glyphs: inverted for 0.35 s, then baked into the row strip, which scrolls away at (36+21r)*speed px/s (9-35 s). Slam lines visible for 0.22 s, flash 0.1 s, fresh dot on the roll 0.25 s, data-column glow near = 1-(t-t0)/0.4 (0.4 s linear), lastVel falls 90/s and ref sinks 2.2/s (min 80).
lowPass: No smoothing or delay of the attack; it only gates: slam cooldown 0.1 s, flash cooldown 1.4 s plus a random-looking but deterministic hash gate, 'loud' judged against ref (the recent maximum, which only sinks 2.2/s, so a run of equally loud notes after a louder one does not slam), the presence gate (softest = percentile of this piece), notes capped at 160. The decay is tied to the note's transcribed end (n.d), which with the pedal is unreliable.
snapKnobs: life (0.1-3, default 1.2): erosion time after the note ends (the 0.6 s floor and the note length still hold the code first)
slam (0-1, drive +level): number of one-pixel lines on loud notes, 0 = none
flash (0-1): how often the loudest attacks turn the screen white, 0 = never
speed (0.3-2.5): how fast the score and data rows scroll
busy (drive +rate): how much data
presence: fewer notes (hardest only), strobe stops, everything fainter and slower
howToSnap: The attack is already as sharp as it can be (full-screen code at alpha 1 in the same frame, own black ground). What stops it dying quickly is the hold: line 146 `end: t + Math.max(0.6, n.d)` (0.6 s floor and the note length) followed by the 1.2 s erosion (line 270 `Math.pow((t - n.end) / life, 1.4)`); for snap use end = t + a short constant (e.g. min(n.d, 0.1)) and an exponent below 1 (about 0.7) so the first bars go at once, and shorten the 0.5 s settle on line 277 (0.12 s strobe then 0.5 s ease). A global scale works here: add one `hold`/`snap` knob multiplying the 0.6 floor, n.d, life and the 0.5 settle, with default 1.0; the life knob alone already reaches 0.1 s but not the hold.
risk: Low: it repaints its own black ground, all randomness is hash-based (hh) and ICON.rng-seeded, nothing uses wall time, so frames are deterministic and a short hold would not break seeks; the roll reads window.NOTES directly including future notes. The risks are cosmetic: with a shorter end the settled labelled row bands and the 'near' column glow shown after the attack would rarely appear, the notes pruning bound (end+life+0.05) shifts, and presence scaling (wall = pres^2) interacts with strobe and settle. Not in either scene.

onAttack: onChord ranks each note's pitch among all song pitches to pick one of ~8-14 big fields and calls pressNote (up to the 5 loudest notes, after the presence velocity-rank cut): it sets s.goal=max(s.goal, amp*press), s.wg and s.flush=max(.., amp*gentle) with amp=sqrt(clamp(v/112,.06,1)), and s.tw=max(s.tw, stay*0.42*(0.55+min(4,n.d)*0.55)) on one of the field's 2 slots (merges into the existing press unless a slot has come back: d<0.08 and wg<0.1). It also starts one 'blush' (b.a=0, b.goal=sqrt(vm/112)*(0.3+0.7*F.f)*min(1.4,press)/(1+max(0,rate-5)*0.25)) on the field of the highest near-loudest note, and a 'sigh' for chords of 4 or more notes. In its own frame the colour warmth rises at once (warm follows wg with tau 0.05 s, 'steepest in the very frame of the attack'), the blush rises with tau 0.06 s, but the edge dimple (s.d) rises slowly on purpose.
decay: All first-order, 'overdamped, nothing overshoots'. Edge press goal: s.goal *= exp(-dt/1.7); dimple s.d chases it: up if goal>d: s.d += min((goal-d)*(1-exp(-dt/0.17)), 2.4*dt), down: s.d += (goal-d)*(1-exp(-dt/0.35)). So the dimple takes at least 0.42 s to reach d=1 and about 5 s to come back (tau 1.7 s then 0.35 s). Warmth: s.wg *= exp(-dt/max(0.3, s.tw)) with tw=stay*0.42*(0.55+min(4,n.d)*0.55) = 2.1*(0.55+0.55*d) s at default stay=5 (about 1.7 to 2.3 s for typical notes; min 0.3 s); s.warm += (wg-warm)*(1-exp(-dt/0.05)). Flush: s.flush *= exp(-dt/0.42), s.fl follows with tau 0.05. Blush: b.goal *= exp(-dt/0.45), b.a += (goal-a)*(1-exp(-dt/0.06)) so it peaks near 0.15 s and dies with tau 0.45 s. Sigh: sighGoal *= exp(-dt/2.2), sigh follows with tau 0.5 s. lamp follows x.level with tau 3 s. Field centres chase their wander targets with K=1-exp(-dt/1.1). Body radius F.R=R0*(1+amp*0.62*sin(phase-delay) - 0.05*min(1.4,sag) - 0.014*sigh); breath period 10 s default.
lowPass: Several: (1) gentle=1/(1+max(0,rate-3)*0.05) scales wg and flush in fast music; (2) the blush is divided by (1+max(0,rate-5)*0.25); (3) amp=sqrt(v/112) compresses loudness ('a fortissimo is a deeper sigh, not a hit'); (4) only the 5 loudest notes of a chord; presence cut drops notes by velocity rank (cut=(1-pres)*0.95); (5) the dimple rise is rate-limited (tau 0.17 s plus a hard cap of 2.4*dt per second) so 'a dimple never twitches'; (6) slots merge: a repeat note on a field with an active press raises s.goal by max(), not a new object, so repeats blur together; (7) blushes are a pool of 7, each attack replaces the weakest, and their sum is capped (room2=BLUSH*min(1,2.4/max(2.4,held))); (8) the whole layer is drawn at S=0.22 scale and blurred (SOFT 4.6 px) then scaled up, so edges are melted.
snapKnobs: stay (1.5..15, default 5): scales the warmth hold tw=stay*0.42*(...); this is the one existing knob that shortens the colour tail (stay=1.5 gives about 0.35-0.7 s)
press (0.15..2, default 1): scales the depth of the edge dimple (s.goal) and the blush size (goal*min(1.4,press))
presence: the velocity-rank cut (only the hardest notes press at low presence)
There is NO knob for the dimple return (goal tau 1.7 s, d down tau 0.35 s), the rise (tau 0.17 s, cap 2.4/s) or the blush decay (0.45 s)
howToSnap: Everything is a plain exp(-dt/tau), so a single 'speed' multiplier (default 1) that divides these taus works as a global attack/decay scaling: 1.7 (goal), 0.17 and the 2.4 cap (rise), 0.35 (return), 0.42 (flush), 0.45 and 0.06 (blush), the 0.3 floor and the stay-based tw, 0.05 (warm/fl rise). Smallest targeted change for a sharp, quick-dying response: goal tau 1.7 -> ~0.5, rise tau 0.17 -> 0.05 and cap 2.4 -> ~8, return tau 0.35 -> 0.15, stay default 5 -> ~1.5, blush decay 0.45 -> 0.2. Keep the warm rise at 0.05 s, it is already instantaneous. Comfort is not in either protected scene, so defaults may change; the 'overdamped, never overshoots' design stays valid because only taus change. Repeated-pitch merging (slot reuse via max) is the remaining thing that hides individual notes: widget is poor at per-note legibility because each field has just 2 slots and notes map to fields by pitch rank.
risk: Deliberately slow, gentle design (the header says 'never a flash', 'overdamped'): speeding up risks twitchy dimples and turns the Rothko-like calm into flicker, which the author explicitly guarded against (the 2.4*dt clamp). Pitch ranks come from window.NOTES via loadSong, so the field a note lands on is fixed per song. Field layout/wander is built per song seed (songSeed), and F.cx chases targets with state that depends on history (snap flag only on the first frame / after reset), so seeks are history-dependent; x.rnd is used for spot() (deterministic), no Math.random. The blur-and-upscale buffer pass would not be affected by envelope changes. Persistent state: forms, slots, blushes, lamp, sigh (reset() clears them).

onAttack: Pushes one hill object per NOTE of the chord into hills[] (cap 90): {x,y (by circle-of-fifths position across, octave up, mirrored, plus Math.random jitter), amp=pow(rel,1.3)*(1+0.8*sparse-0.25*busy)*thick*sign with rel=0.5*v/105+0.5*v/max(55,avgV), sig, age:0, life=decay*(0.75+0.2*min(3,n.d))*(1+0.6*sparse-0.5*busy)}; softer-than-average notes get negative amp (pits). Also flash=max(flash, vel/127). In its own frame: the hill is a gaussian added to a scalar field F; the topographic isolines (marching squares, levels at multiples of 1/count) appear as the field value crosses those levels, so a new hill shows as rings bursting out of a point while amp rises over 0.09 s; plus all lines brighten and thicken with flash.
decay: Per hill: age a; rise = a<0.09 ? a/0.09 : 1+0.22*exp(-(a-0.09)/0.12)*sin(min(PI,(a-0.09)*14)) (linear 0.09 s ramp then a small overshoot bump); amp = h.amp*rise*exp(-a/h.life): a pure exponential with tau = life seconds, life = x.p('decay')*(0.75+0.2*min(3,d))*(1+0.6*sparse-0.5*busy) = 2.4*(0.75..1.35)=1.8 to 3.2 s at default (up to x1.6 when sparse, x0.5 when busy). Width: sig = h.sig*(0.55+0.45*min(1,a/0.3))*(1+0.06*a) (grows from 55% to 100% over 0.3 s, then keeps spreading 6% per second). Culling: removed when age>=5*life or (age>=1 and |cur amp|<0.01). Global brightness flash: flash *= pow(0.5, dt/0.12) (half-life 0.12 s, tau 0.17 s), line colour *(1+0.55*flash), lineWidth*(1+0.6*flash). Ground swell and the rings' outward drift (phase -= dt*0.45*flow) are continuous background.
lowPass: (1) linear 0.09 s rise ramp + sigma grow-in over 0.3 s soften the onset (at 60 Hz the first drawn frame already has rise=0.18, since age is advanced before drawing); (2) rel mixes absolute and relative-to-avgV loudness, avgV += (vel-avgV)*0.12 so a repeated loud note in a loud passage gets less; (3) thick=1/sqrt(max(1,notes/3)) so big chords are not louder per note; (4) sparse boosts size and life, busy shortens life: a rate-dependent lengthening; (5) F = 1.7*tanh(F/1.7) saturates stacked hills so a climax flattens; (6) the isoline levels are a threshold function: a hill whose peak is below 1/count spawns no rings, and level lines fade by al=min(1,|e|*2.2); (7) knob drives: lines +level, size +bass (both read the slow feat pulses, half-lives 0.8 s / 0.25 s), flow -level.
snapKnobs: decay (0.5..10, default 2.4, less 0.8): the hill's exponential tau, already the main decay knob; 0.5 gives tau 0.4 to 0.7 s
lines (3..24, default 7, drive +level): fewer lines mean the hill must be taller to show rings, so it vanishes sooner
size (0.4..1.8, drive +bass): narrower hills
flow (0..2, drive -level): less drift
presence (leads): sets lines and decay together (decay less 0.8, lines less 3)
howToSnap: Already per-note and already has a decay knob, so the cheapest snap is: decay default 2.4 -> ~0.6-0.8 (tau about 0.45-1 s), and shorten the 0.09 s ramp to ~0.02 (even 0: give the hill full amp in the attack frame, and keep the overshoot bump 0.22*exp(-(a-0.09)/0.12) as a flash), start sig at full (0.55 -> 0.9 over 0.3 s -> 0.1 s), and raise the flash multiplier. The decay shape is exponential, which is right for a piano; a bump of extra fast decay (e.g. amp*(0.5*exp(-a/0.15)+0.5*exp(-a/life))) would give a quick strike and a short held tail. A global scaling works: decay tau, 0.09/0.12/14 (rise), 0.3 (sig), 0.12 (flash) are all independent constants.
risk: Uses Math.random for hill positions, chordY, and reset() time (not x.rnd), so it is already non-deterministic between renders/seeks; any snappiness test must accept that. Hills accumulate into a field then tanh-saturate, so shortening life will make the map empty quickly (the rings only exist where the sum exceeds 1/count), and with few overlapping hills the screen may mostly show the ground swell. Marching-squares cost grows with hill count (cap 90, but culled by life*5). No precomputed plans or fluid sim; state is hills[], phase, flash, avgV, time.

onAttack: No per-note objects. Per chord: (a) voices are ranked top to bottom and mapped to threads; each hit thread's energy h.e = min(1.6, h.e + 0.45*(v/110) + 0.2*min(1,n.d)); the hit strands (i>0) get h.tph += (0.6+0.4*nv)*dir*max(0.3,steer)/(1+rate*0.12), a phase jump the strand eases toward; (b) the main thread turns: main.ta += stepM*0.13/(1+rate*0.15), stepM=clamp(ch.hi-lastTop,-7,7); local rate += 1 (cap 12); (c) splatVel(main - 14*dir, normal push of 10*loud cells/s, sigma 3 cells) and splatDye(main, [1,.9,.7], 0.5*loud, r 1.8), flash=max(flash, 0.5*loud); (d) chords of 2 or more notes or vel>=84 pour coloured dye amt=(0.5+0.3*min(4,n))*loud, r=3.5+min(6,n); (e) vel>=88 and >=3 notes tear a vortex pair (splatSwirl) and set flash=1.2. In its own frame the attack is seen as the head's glow disc (radius 16*(1+flash*2.5), alpha 0.3+0.4*min(1,flash)), a bulge of thread brightness/width laid in the wake (point intensity uses e), and a nudge in the water that the dye then carries.
decay: flash *= pow(0.5, dt/0.15): half-life 0.15 s, tau 0.22 s. Thread energy: h.e = max(h.e*pow(0.5,dt/0.35), i ? x.level*0.45 : 0): half-life 0.35 s (tau 0.5 s), with a floor tied to the slow feat.level (half-life 0.8 s) for strands. Local rate *= pow(0.5, dt/0.6) (half-life 0.6 s). Strand phase eases h.ph += (tph-ph)*(1-exp(-dt/0.18)); main heading main.a eases with tau 0.16 s. Thread points: life=(2.6+4*exp(-rate/3))*persist/(1+rate*0.15) s = 6.6 s at rest, about 2.6-3 s in busy music; point brightness I=pow(max(0,1-age/life),1.3)*(0.3+0.7*min(1,e)) with e frozen per point when laid. Fluid: velocity keep=exp(-dt*0.45) per step (tau 2.2 s); dye kd=exp(-dt*0.5/persist) (tau 2 s at persist=1); the pressure p*=0.9. Dye is re-drawn each frame at globalAlpha 0.2 with a tone map 1-exp(-x/160). Vortices persist for a few seconds (viscosity tau 2.2 s + vorticity confinement).
lowPass: Heavy: (1) the fluid itself is the low-pass: velocity tau 2.2 s, dye tau 2 s, pressure projection, semi-Lagrangian advection (smears); (2) threads are a record of the last 2.6-6.6 s, so an individual note is only a local bulge in a long line; (3) rate damping: /(1+rate*0.15) on turning, /(1+rate*0.12) on strand jumps, life/(1+rate*0.15); (4) heading and strand phase eased with taus 0.16/0.18 s, plus headAt(0.06*i) lag per strand; (5) strand amplitude uses h.e with a level floor; (6) gain=min(1,sqrt(1300/total points)) dims a dense tangle; (7) loud(vel/110) is linear velocity only, so no ranking; (8) the knob drives read slow feat pulses (width +level, flow +rate, curl +density, swirl +bass).
snapKnobs: width (0.3..2.5, drive +level): thread thickness, a rough gauge of thread visibility
flow (0.2..3, drive +rate, less 0.4): water speed and thread speed; faster means shorter visible streaks
braid (0..220): the strand swing amplitude scales with (0.55+0.45*min(1,h.e))
threads (1..5): fewer threads, fewer things to see
presence (leads): sets threads, braid and flow together
PERSIST, VISC and STEER are fixed constants, not knobs (they are the main sluggishness and would be the new snap knobs)
howToSnap: Cheapest: make PERSIST (dye tau 2/persist, thread life) and VISC (0.45) knobs or lab switches; lowering persist to ~0.4 cuts thread life to ~1.1-2.6 s and dye tau to 0.8 s. For alertness: raise the head flash (flash halving 0.15 -> 0.08 s) and add a same-frame bead/ring at the head scaled by the note velocity; make h.e decay half-life 0.35 -> 0.12 s so the bulge dies quickly; set e on the point nearest the head (q.e=max) immediately instead of rising only for future points. A global attack/decay scaling does NOT work cleanly: it is a Navier-Stokes style sim with dt-coupled advection, a pressure solve and a persistent dye field; scaling dt would speed the whole river and scrambles its look. Only the explicit exps (flash, e, rate, ph, a, kd, keep, life) can be scaled together.
risk: A real-time fluid: path-dependent state (u, v, R, G, B, thread points), so a seek or render needs the sim replayed from the start with the same dt sequence (semi-Lagrangian + Gauss-Seidel are not dt-invariant), so determinism between live play and 60 Hz renders is already approximate. Math.random is used for vortex sign (turn) in onChord. Changing dye decay or velocity damping alters the overall level of the dye layer (the tone map and additive 0.2 alpha draw can wash out to white or vanish), the gain/total-points dimming and the 5-thread point caps (cap 1300/3200 per T) interplay with shorter life. Cost is high (128x72 solve, 10 Gauss-Seidel iterations).

onAttack: Per NOTE (those passing the presence velocity-rank test hardEnough): picks the disc by pitch (m<48, <72, else), the ring by floor((m-d.lo)/4), and the segment by the note's pitch-class position on the circle of fifths as the ring has turned. paint() sets the whole segment's q.lit=max(q.lit, 0.55+0.45*vk) and q.fl=max(q.fl, 0.6+0.4*vk) (vk=clamp01(v/110)), q.mem=1, and recolours slots if the old colour is dimmer; with contrast>0.02 the neighbouring segment gets the opposite colour (lit (0.4+0.45*vk)*con, fl 0.25*con). The struck ring jumps: ring.wk += dir*(0.5+1.4*vk*vk)*pres. A swell is queued: for rings j>=k kicks.push({a: A*0.82^(j-k), wait: (j-k)*0.045}) with A=pulse*pres*(4+20*vk*vk)*(d.fr/0.47*0.6+0.4); when wait expires r.vel += a*13. In its own frame the colour is lit at full strength immediately (cream flash mixes in via fl*0.55), the ring begins to spin, and the first ring's spring is kicked at once, the outer rings 45 ms apart.
decay: Colour: q.lit *= exp(-dt/mem) with mem default 3.5 s (range 0.4..8); the displayed mix is v = glaze + (full-glaze)*min(1,lit). Flash: q.fl *= exp(-dt/0.12) (cream mix fl*0.55, tau 0.12 s). Glaze memory: q.mem *= exp(-dt/(mem*7+6)), tau 30.5 s at default, the dark glaze brightness is gl=0.15+0.2*mem+0.1*level. Jump spin: ring.wk *= exp(-dt/0.45); rot += dt*(w*spin + wk*(0.6+turn)). Swell: damped spring per ring, r.vel += (-170*off - 9*vel)*dt, off += vel*dt (two half steps): omega0=sqrt(170)=13.0 rad/s, zeta=9/(2*13.04)=0.345, underdamped, envelope tau 2/9=0.22 s, ring period about 0.51 s, it overshoots and rings about 2 cycles; ring radius accumulates r1 = R*(k+1)/RINGS + sum(max(-6,off)) outward. Disc glow: 0.1*feat.level*pres brightens the glaze; disc radius *(1+0.025*level*pres).
lowPass: (1) hardEnough rank cut by velocity at presence<1; (2) paint keeps max of old lit and new, so repeating the same pitch on an already-lit segment adds only fl and a kick (notes of the same pitch class landing on one slot merge); (3) the segment draws its brightest slot among its group, and a ring cut into only 2 or 4 segments (cut default 0.25: cuts like [2,4,2,4,4,8]) lumps neighbouring pitches into one segment; (4) kicks capped at 400, staggered 0.045 s per ring, which spreads the swell over up to 0.225 s; (5) the spring itself is a resonator (period 0.51 s, ring-down tau 0.22 s) so a swell lasts about 1 s; (6) lit has a long tau (3.5 s) which dominates how long any note stays visible; (7) pulse is a knob with drive +level, read at onChord time: it scales swell with the (slow) feat.level; (8) spin has drive +rate.
snapKnobs: memory (0.4..8, default 3.5): lit tau; at 0.4 colours die in about 0.4 s, though the glaze memory tau (mem*7+6 = 8.8 s) stays long
pulse (0..1, default 0.45, drive +level): amplitude of the outward swell
cut (0..1, default 0.25): finer segmentation makes individual notes more distinct
turn (0..1, default 0.3, drive +rate): spin speed; the jump wk adds (0.6+turn)
presence: velocity-rank threshold and swell/jump scale; low presence means only the hardest notes count
the 170/9 spring, the 0.12 s flash tau, 0.45 s jump tau and the 0.045 s stagger are constants, not knobs
howToSnap: This is already the most attack-alert widget of the six (colour is set at full in the attack frame, one object per note, kick fires in the same step). To make it snap and die quickly: (1) set memory default to ~0.6-0.9 (existing knob, tau for lit); (2) retune the swell spring to nearly critical damping and shorter: e.g. stiffness 170 -> 400, damping 9 -> 40 (zeta about 1, ring-down tau about 0.05 s... or just damping 9 -> 26 for zeta=1 at the current stiffness) so the ring jumps and returns in about 0.25 s without ringing; (3) set the stagger 0.045 -> ~0.015 s so the swell reaches the outer rings within about 0.075 s; (4) wk tau 0.45 -> ~0.2 s; (5) shorten the memory-of-glaze tau (mem*7+6) so unlit segments return to dark glaze faster. Because every time constant is an independent constant, a single 'snap' knob (default 0) that divides memory, 0.45, and the spring's damping/stagger by (1+k*snap) would work as a global scaling, provided stiffness and damping are scaled together to keep zeta (omega0 up by sqrt(s), damping up by s... for zeta fixed use damping*sqrt(s)).
risk: The spring uses half steps with an explicit Euler: at high stiffness or long frame dt (live dt up to 0.05) it can go unstable (stiffness 400 at dt/2=0.025: omega*dt=0.5, OK; much higher stiffness would need more substeps). kicks are queued objects with wait, so seeks and live play agree only if all steps are fed in order (no precomputation). Disc geometry is fixed and ring.rot is integrated state from reset (build uses a seeded R1(17) so layout is deterministic, though ring rotation depends on history). Fast-decaying lit with the cream flash can make the whole image flicker between near-black glaze and full colour, which the original painter feel avoids. presence feeds multiple formulas (jump, swell, spin, dimming). No Math.random use.

onAttack: One verdict per attack: verdict() scores the interval classes of the chord's notes against everything x.sounding() (CONS/DISS tables), cons = score>=0. mood is moved at once: mood += ((cons?1:-1)-mood)*min(1,reach), reach=(0.08+0.26*loud+0.5*|score|)*(cons? (mood<0?0.6:1) : 1.3), loud=clamp((vel-30)/85,0.05,1). flash=max(flash, loud). Notes below split (default 60) move mass A (thick, slow), others B (thin, quick), each via answer(): velocity impulse f.v += n*J*sign, J=(cons? pull*(120+460*power) : push*(190+820*power))*(0.35+0.65*dense), and an instant position shift f.x += n*sign*J*0.012 ('seen in the attack's own frame', about 12 px at J=1000), f.lit=max(lit, 0.35+0.65*power), a velocity kick of J*(0.5 thick, 0.8 quick) to each drop (sideways swirl for consonance, away for dissonance), spatter (dissonant only): up to 7 'loose' drops start at 1.45*R from the centre. Held notes (note length d>0.6) set a swell target and mood hold.
decay: Mass velocity: damp=exp(-2.1*h) per substep, tau 0.48 s, plus a spring toward a target separation (k=3.2+3.2*min(1.5,pull) when too far, 11 when too close) so the mass returns to the seam position over about 0.5-1 s. Drops: spring stiffness 16 (thick) / 30 (quick), velocity damping exp(-2.6*h) / exp(-3.4*h): omega0=4.0 / 5.5 rad/s, zeta about 0.33/0.31, underdamped sloshing (period 1.6 s / 1.15 s, envelope tau 0.77 s / 0.59 s). Brightness: f.lit *= exp(-dt/0.22); la=0.2+0.8*lit adds to k1 (0.3*lit*depth) and +90*lit*depth^2. Seam flash: flash *= exp(-dt/0.3). Mood relaxes to m0=0.32*min(1,pull) with tau 2.0 s after holdEnd. Swell eases tau 0.45 s. Spatter: lifetime 0.5-1.1 s, velocity *exp(-2.4 dt), radius r*(1-age/life). The mood hold for a consonant held note lasts min(4, d) s (min(1.2,d) s for a clash).
lowPass: (1) dense=max(1/(1+2.2*x.feat.rate), jolt) multiplies J by (0.35+0.65*dense): in fast music (rate 4/s) hits are cut to about 41%, unless it is an accent well above its neighbours (jolt=clamp((loud-velAvg-0.06)/0.2,0,1), velAvg += (loud-velAvg)*0.12); (2) the masses are liquid with inertia: the spring/drop dynamics (zeta 0.3, 0.6-1.2 s sloshing) smear the response; (3) the verdict aggregates two masses, not individual notes; (4) mood is a state with 2 s memory and hysteresis (consonance after a clash reconciles only 60%; clash reach x1.3), and 'a bare note carries the last verdict on'; (5) velocity capped at 1200; drop offset capped at 1.25*R*sw; (6) the field rendering thresholds (EDGE 0.46, GIVE 0.72) make the surfaces only change gradually; (7) 12-22 drops per mass per frame stamped onto a 320x180 grid and upscaled, which blurs.
snapKnobs: push (0.2..2, default 1, less 0.4): impulse and spatter strength of a clash
pull (0..2, default 1): impulse and cohesion for consonance
size (0.5..2.2, default 1): the mass radius R=size*92
split (30..90): which notes drive which mass
presence (leads): sets size, push, and spatter
no knob shortens the damping (2.1), the drop damping (2.6 / 3.4), lit tau 0.22 s, flash tau 0.3 s, or mood tau 2 s
howToSnap: Duet is in the Liebesleid scene, so the defaults must stay: add a new opt-in knob 'snap' (default 0, so exact current behaviour, say 0..1) that scales: the position jump J*0.012 up to ~0.03-0.04 (a clearer same-frame jump), damp exp(-2.1*h) up to ~exp(-5*h), drop damping 2.6/3.4 up to about 6-8 (ideally critically damped: c=2*sqrt(stiff)=8 / 11), lit tau 0.22 -> 0.08 s, flash 0.3 -> 0.12 s, mood relaxation 2 -> 0.8 s, spatter life x0.5. Also raise the dense factor floor (0.35+0.65*dense -> mostly 1) so fast passages keep individual hits. A global attack/decay time-scale works reasonably: scale all the exp rates and spring constants (stiffness times s^2, damping times s) but it also speeds up the ambient wander (w, the 0.5*sin drops) unless only the attack-driven parts are scaled.
risk: It is in the protected Liebesleid scene: every change must default to the current pixel-identical behaviour (a knob with default 0 = old constants; stored knob values never change meaning). The sim is explicit Euler with substeps n=clamp(ceil(dt*120),1,8), h=min(dt,0.1)/n, so stiffer springs/dampers (higher damping, stiffness) can go unstable at high frame dt in live play (the render path at 60 Hz is safe). It uses Math.random in newMass (drop sizes and phases) and x.rnd for spatter/swirl sign, so it is not fully deterministic from the song time alone already; renderFrameHash may depend on reset. State is path-dependent (positions and velocities, mood, holdEnd) so seeks replay history. Spatter drops cap 16. Power curves (pa, pb) depend on a single loudest note per mass.

onAttack: Per attack, per field (register band) touched, not per note: onChord pushes ONE glow per band: {b, u (position along the field = velocity-weighted mean pitch within that band's slice, low left, high right), wid=clamp(0.11+0.1*p+0.5*(hi-lo)/span+0.025*(cnt-1),0.1,0.42), a=0.2+0.8*p*p with p=clamp(vmax/max(64,runMax)), age:0, life=0.55+0.9*p+min(2.6,dur)*0.7 (dur = longest note length d in that band)}. It also bumps f.flare = min(1, flare + 0.35*max(0,1-0.7*back)*min(1,0.3+per)*punch) for each field touched, f.imp and the harmony vectors, and may start a colour 'wash' on a chord change (jump>=0.4 rad and >=0.9 s since the last). In its own frame the glow is drawn on a 320x180 buffer with 'screen' composite: its alpha rises as min(1, age/0.05+0.15), so it starts at 15% and is at full after 0.0425 s, and the field flares (size swell sw=flare*2.5 buffer px, lighter l, inner light alpha +0.4*flare).
decay: Glow: al = min(1, age/0.05 + 0.15) * (1 - k)^1.7 * a * gg with k=age/life: a power-law fade over life = 0.55+0.9p+0.7*min(2.6, d) s (about 0.6 to 1.5 s for a short note, up to 3.4 s for a held note at full velocity); width grows rx*(1+0.35k); gg=min(1,1.3*dyn)*(1-0.55*back) = 0.76 at defaults (back 0.4, dyn 0.75). Flare: f.flare *= pow(0.5, dt/0.5) (half-life 0.5 s, tau 0.72 s). Edge hardness 'hard' (very loud chords): hard *= pow(0.5, dt/0.6), cool 0.3 s. The wash: life 2.4+0.2*n s, alpha min(1,k*8)*(1-k^4). The body of the painting is deliberately slow: f.e eased with half-life 1.6 s (kS), f.light 0.7 s (kL), hue glide 0.9 s (kG), imp/mx/my decay half-life 1.4 s, loudEnv rises half-life 0.35 s and falls over 4 s, warm eases 4 s, layout shares 1.6 s, runMax -2.5 per second. Final blit onto stage with 'lighten' at alpha 0.95-0.2*back.
lowPass: (1) the body is smoothed with half-lives 0.7 to 4 s (what is sounding, via x.sounding(), sets f.e and the harmony), so the painting itself responds slowly, only the glow and flare are fast; (2) glows merge notes in a band into one blob with a mean pitch position (individual notes in a chord are not separate); (3) brightness a is relative: p=vmax/max(64,runMax), runMax decays only 2.5/s, so after a loud passage soft notes are dim (a=0.2+0.8p^2); (4) screen compositing saturates in busy playing, many glows 'shimmer without burning out'; (5) glows cap 56; (6) glow life uses note length d, so long notes keep the glow; (7) the dyn knob (gg) scales everything, 'less' sets dyn 0.2; (8) buffer is 320x180 with blur filters, then upscaled, so detail softens.
snapKnobs: dyn ('the playing shows', 0..1, default 0.75, less 0.2): scales glow alpha (gg=min(1,1.3*A)) plus loudness light and edge hardness
back (0..1.9, default 0.4): scales flare (1-0.7*B), glow (1-0.55*B), blit alpha
n (1..4, default 3, less 1): number of fields
chords (0..1, default 0.7): colour wash/hue movement
home (-1..1, default -0.2, drive +level)
presence (leads): sets n and dyn together
there is NO knob for glow life, rise or the flare half-life

A global scaling is possible just for the glow/flare constants (glow life, flare half-life, hard half-life) but NOT for the painting's smoothing half-lives (1.6, 0.7, 0.9, 1.4, 4 s), which are the Rothko slowness and affect the scene's look; scaling those would change the whole picture. Individual notes are not separable (one glow per band), so for per-note legibility push one glow per note instead of per band when snap>0.
risk: It is in the protected Rach 2 scene: defaults must remain pixel-identical (knob default = old behaviour). The glow uses Math.random for dh (hue offset) and mk() ph, so it is already non-deterministic (renderFrameHash may not be stable for the scene as-is); the edge strips' wobble depends on hum (accumulated dt*(0.6+3.2*rate)) and so on history. onAttack: onChord feeds the key histogram (hist*=0.985 per attack, key() with 1.08 hysteresis) then calls burst() once per note: n = round(burst * (4+20*(eff(v)/127)^1.5) * (big?1.5:1) * sparse * thin) dots, sparse = 1+1.3*(1-feat.rate), thin = 1/sqrt(max(1,notes/2)), plus a complementary 'ring' halo for chords >=2 notes (FIX.comp 0.35). Each dot is pushed into `fresh` with age = -R(0,0.04) (held: 0), fly = R(0.08,0.2); in its own frame it is drawn at once at 1.6x radius (r = q.r*(1+0.6*(1-t))), popping from halfway to its target with ease-out e = 1-(1-t)^3, with a white 'lighter' flash alpha 0.45*(1-t)^2; at t>=1 it is committed to the open epoch's crisp canvas (full alpha) and to the quarter-res wash canvas (alpha 0.55). Big chords (>=2 notes, vel >= max(80, min(100, avgVel+16))) also kick pulse += 0.5+max(0,vel-85)/30 (max 1.5).
decay: Fly-in 0.08-0.2 s (+0-0.04 s stagger); white flash dies over the same fly time as 0.45*(1-t)^2. Then the dots sit at FULL alpha in the open epoch until it closes: epoch length = life/(K-1) = life/7, life = stay*(1-0.45*feat.rate), default stay 8 => ~1.14 s (life itself eases to target with half-life 1.5 s: life += (target-life)*(1-0.5^(dt/1.5))). After closing, a = (time-closed)/life and alpha crispA = (1-a)^1.3 * (1 - 0.75*bleed*min(1,1.6a)); with life 8 s, bleed 0.55 the dots reach ~50% at a~0.3 (~2.4 s after closing, ~3.5 s after the attack) and are gone at a=1 (8 s, so up to ~9 s total). Wash: washA = bleed*min(1,0.25+3a)*(1-a)^0.8, stamped faintly right away (25% of bleed) and blooming to full by a=0.25 (~2 s), then fading by 8 s; drawn at 0.5 alpha after blur(2+5*bleed px). pulse *= 0.5^(dt/0.12) (flinch of field scale 0.018*pulse). Held notes keep adding dots after 0.15 s: rate burst*7*v/127 dots per second per sounding note.
lowPass: Yes, several: (1) the key/hue is a decaying histogram (0.985 per attack) with 8% hysteresis, so colours lag harmonic change; (2) dot count per note is damped by feat.rate (sparse = 1+1.3*(1-rate): busy music paints fewer dots per note) and by chord size (thin); (3) loudness is relativised to a running average (avgVel += (vel-avgVel)*0.06; eff(v) lifts soft notes to min(105, v*72/max(45,avgVel))), so dynamics are compressed; (4) life (stay) is smoothed with 1.5 s half-life and shortened up to 45% by feat.rate; (5) fresh capped at 2500; (6) the epoch scheme makes the whole last ~1.1 s of dots one undifferentiated layer; (7) the blurred wash smears onsets.
snapKnobs: stay (how long the painting stays, 1..25, default 8, less 2.5): scales life, hence epoch length life/7 and the whole dot/wash decay; at 1 s epochs are ~0.14 s and dots vanish in ~1 s. Not a drive; the life value is eased with a 1.5 s half-life so changes are not instant
bleed (0..1, default 0.55): at 0 there is no wash and old dots are not extra-dimmed (crispA loses its 0.75*bleed term), so pure dots; also changes wash blur
burst (dots per note 0.2..3, less 0.25, drive +level): fewer dots makes each note a sparser, crisper mark
dot (1.5..10, drive -rate): dot size
presence: writes burst and stay together (less values 0.25 and 2.5)
