risk: Scene widget in liebesleid: any change to defaults breaks pixel-identity, so it must be a new knob with default = today. Uses Math.random (R, gauss) for positions/colours, so it is not pixel-deterministic even today. State is the K=8 epoch canvases (crisp at 0.75 res, wash at 320x180) plus the epoch rotation clock (time, cur, born/closed), which is tied to life; changing life or the alpha curves changes when canvases are recycled and clearRect'ed (an epoch is cleared on rotation, and recycled only once age01>=1, so a shorter life with a very large K-1 divisor risks dots being cut off or clearing live layers). reset() primes the key from the last 30 s of window.NOTES (seek-safe) but does not rebuild dots. Sprite cache (SPR) is quantised; fresh capped at 2500.

onAttack: onChord pushes one hit {m, v, age:0, fresh:true} per note and sets flash = max(flash, (vel/127)^1.5 * min(1.4, 0.6+0.12*notes)). In its own frame each hit adds a narrow peak at its pitch on the live front slice: peak(live, h.m, 1.15*v*k, sig*0.75) with v = (vel/127)^1.1, k = exp(-age/0.11), on top of the sounding peaks; and (fresh) registers a 'spark' glint {i, v} (one per spot, louder wins, deduped within 2 index points ~1 semitone) in pendGl, which is carried by the line currently being built and rides back into the stack as a glowing dot on that line's crest. The front line also flares: width 1.4+0.8*level+2.2*flash, alpha min(1, 0.9+flash), glow alpha 0.05+0.12*min(1,flash).
decay: Hit peak: exp(-age/0.11) (tau 0.11 s), hits dropped at age 0.5 s (k<0.02 beyond ~0.43 s). Flash: flash *= 0.5^(dt/0.12), i.e. tau 0.173 s. Sounding notes on the live slice: peak amp vv*(0.32 + 0.68*exp(-age/1.6)) with vv = 0.15+0.85*(v/127)^1.1, age from note start, tau 1.6 s toward a 0.32 floor, held for as long as the transcribed note sounds (x.sounding(), up to 8 s). The attack is then baked into the stack: each frame the max of the live slice is held in `pend`, and every 1/speed s (speed 11 lines/s default, ~0.09 s) a row is stamped; the row keeps what it was made with and rolls back; rows are visible for about N/(speed*mean gap) = 46/(11*~0.9) ~ 4.6 s (gap = 0.5+0.95*min(1,level) per line), fading by brightness (0.95-0.5*far^2)*edge*loud, never exponentially. Sparks live as long as their row.
lowPass: Mild: `pend` is a max-hold over the 1/speed s slice window (about 90 ms), so attacks are not smoothed, only quantised to a row; pendLvl = max(f.level) per row and floor = 0.015+0.04*level+0.07*density (feat.level has 0.8 s half-life, density 0.25 s); row gap depends on feat.level; spark dedupe (louder wins within a semitone); `lift` soft-compression of tall peaks; the sounding component (1.6 s tau) dominates over the 0.11 s hit when notes are held, blunting the individual attack; hits capped to 0.5 s.
snapKnobs: speed (how fast the lines roll away, 4..30, default 11, less 4, drive +rate): at 30 lines/s each slice is ~33 ms and the stack passes faster
lines (16..80, default 46, less 16): stack depth; stack memory ~ lines/(speed*gap), so 16 lines at 30/s is under 1 s
height (0.3..2.5, drive +level): bakes peak height into new lines
sharp (0..1): thin needles vs hills, narrower peaks separate notes better
depth: perspective
howToSnap: Change four constants, all explicit: hit tau 0.11 -> ~0.04 (`Math.exp(-h.age / 0.11)`, drop at 0.5 -> 0.2), sounding envelope `0.32 + 0.68*exp(-age/1.6)` -> floor ~0.05 and tau ~0.25 so held notes die away instead of standing, flash half-life 0.12 -> 0.05, and make the spark/peak amplitude larger on the first frame. With the knobs alone: speed 25-30 and lines 16-24 shortens stack memory to about a second. A global attack/decay scale (a single `snap` divisor on those three tau's) works cleanly because live-slice state is stateless per frame apart from `hits` and `flash`; the stack part (rows/gaps) is geometric and unaffected, so use lines/speed (or a time-based alpha on rows) for its life.
risk: Not in either protected scene, so freedom to change. Hidden state: `rows` (up to 170 baked arrays), `pend`/`pendNoise`/`pendGl`, `since` counted in lines so speed changes do not lurch; Math.random noise rows (not deterministic). It paints its own black and redraws everything each frame (no canvas persistence), so envelope changes are safe; the thing to watch is that rows keep the height/loudness baked at creation, so a shorter sounding envelope changes the stack look too (sparser, brighter), and shorter hit tau might make the 'no attack slips between lines' max-hold the only carrier of the spike if speed is low.

onAttack: onChord, with vel = loud(ch.vel) (velocity / 93rd-percentile of the recording * 100), creates up to three kinds of object per attack (by chord, not per note): a bass LENS for notes below MIDI 50 (one lens at the lowest bass note's x, peak = min(2.6, 0.9+sum(v/127 of bass notes)) * vel/100); a melody RIPPLE from the top note if ch.hi>=55 (a0 = 0.35+0.65*top.v/110, life = 1.4+min(2.5, top.d)); and for chords of >=3 notes, vel>=100, or 2 notes with vel>=88, 1-3 KINKS (chevron displacements at random positions, a0 = +-(0.6+0.12*notes)*vel/100); vel>=92 and >=4 notes also add an inverted CUT band. They are not drawn on the attack frame itself: the field is rebuilt from these objects every frame, a warp of the stripe polylines.
decay: Lens: `L.a = 1.7*Math.tanh(depth*L.peak*(1-Math.exp(-L.age/0.07))*Math.exp(-L.age/2.0)/1.7)`, rise tau 0.07 s, decay tau 2.0 s (peak at ~0.24 s), removed at age 6 s, max 4. Ripple: `r.a = min(depth*w*1.6, (0.9/r.k)*max(1,depth)) * r.a0 * min(1, age/0.08) * max(0, 1-age/life)`: linear 0.08 s ramp-up, then linear fade over life = 1.4 to 3.9 s (1.4+min(2.5,note duration)); the front travels at 240+120/wave px/s. Kink: `k.a = depth*1.2*w*3*k.a0*exp(-age/0.45)*cos(age*9)`: instantaneous full amplitude, tau 0.45 s, oscillating at 9 rad/s (period 0.70 s), removed at 2.2 s, max 8. Cut: width w0*(1-age/0.7)^1.5, instant onset, 0.7 s, max 3. Global: brightness bright += (0.5+0.5*min(1,feat.level*1.1) - bright)*(1-exp(-dt/0.3)) (tau 0.3 s on a level with 0.8 s half-life); drone lens bassHold tau 0.6 s of feat.bass; standing wave waveA = depth*w*(0.25+1.2*feat.density); shimmer vibA = shimmer*w*0.45*(0.3+feat.level).
lowPass: Yes: brightness and vibration follow feat.level (0.8 s half-life) and bright adds a 0.3 s tau; drone lens bassHold 0.6 s tau; standing wave follows feat.density (0.25 s half-life); lens/ripple/kink/cut counts are capped (4/8/8/3, oldest dropped) so rapid passages replace rather than add; the tanh soft-cap (1.7) compresses loud lenses; ripple amplitude capped by slope (0.9/k) so it cannot fold; lens ramp 70 ms and ripple ramp 80 ms blunt the onset, only kinks and cuts are instantaneous; ripples use only the top note and lenses the lowest bass (chord reduced to two features); velocity is rescaled by the 93rd-percentile (loud()), a global rank-like normalisation.
snapKnobs: bend (how much the music bends it, 0..2.5, default 1, less 0, drive +level): scales depth, hence amplitude of lenses, ripples, kinks, wave, but no time constants
shimmer (0..2, default 0.3, drive +rate): fine trembling amplitude, tied to feat.level
stripe (5..60): stripe width (smaller = finer, a more sensitive-looking field)
pattern / colours: no timing effect
presence: writes stripe, bend and shimmer
howToSnap: All the time constants are literals in frame(): lens `1-exp(-age/0.07)` -> ~0.02 and `exp(-age/2.0)` -> ~0.4-0.5 (and age<6 -> <1.5); ripple `age/0.08` -> age/0.02 and `1-age/life` -> life ~0.5-0.8 s (the expanding front distance shrinks accordingly, so raise the front speed 240 -> ~400 px/s if the reach should stay); kink `exp(-age/0.45)` -> ~0.15 and keep cos(age*9) (or raise to 14-18 so there is one sharp overshoot, age<2.2 -> <0.8); cut 0.7 -> ~0.3; bright tau 0.3 -> 0.1 and drive it from a faster level. A global attack/decay scale is easy: it is just a scale on `L.age`, `r.age`, `k.age`, `c.age` increments (dt*snap) for the decay, with a separate attack scale on the ramps; amplitudes (bend) stay the same.
risk: Not in the protected scenes. The field is fully redrawn each frame from object lists (stateless apart from lists and `drift`, `wavePh`, `bright`, `time`), so envelope changes are safe to render. Risks: the warp is geometric, so faster rises/decays make big instant displacements (a kink with 0.45 s -> 0.15 s tau and unchanged amplitude is a sharper pop; strong lens a with fast attack can fold stripes, the ripple amplitude is slope-limited for this reason, kinks and lenses are only soft/tanh limited); rendering cost grows with the margin `m` (sum of |k.a|*0.5), polylines are walked with `warp()` per point (ripples only 'act' when |a|>0.4 px); it uses x.rnd and Math.random mixed (kink sign, vibPh via x.rnd, kink side Math.random), so renders are not strictly deterministic.

onAttack: onChord: for each note below MIDI 50 (FIX.split, max 2 per chord) it calls bloom(): 3-5 swelling 'lobes' (R: 8-24*big, start r=2, e.g. ellipse), 6-22*big*feath 'creep' tendrils, a wet-sheen disc and a `centres` entry, and pulse = max(pulse, min(1.5, big*v/100)); each note >=50 calls spatter(): floor(amt*(violent?2:1)) (+probabilistic remainder) flecks flung from a random existing blot centre (or a random spot) at distance src.R*R(1,1.6)+(m-50)*0.35, speed s*6 with s = (0.4+1.5*v/110); if no low note and sinceBlot>1.2 the lowest note blooms as a fallback; violent chords (vel >= 112-8*amt and >=3 notes) additionally call burst(): a ragged core with streaks and spray drawn straight into the ink canvas, a lobe, a hard wet sheen, shake = max(shake, 5+6*pow), pulse>=1.2. Ink is drawn onto a persistent 320x360 'ink' canvas (one fundamental domain) and mirrored 2/4/2n times; in its own frame an attack is seen as ink starting to soak into the blurred persistent canvas plus a brief sheen, not as a crisp object.
decay: Lobe: `l.r += (l.R - l.r)*min(1, dt*l.k)` with k = R(2.5,5)*soak (swell tau 0.2-0.4 s / soak), deposits ink alpha dep*max(0,1-age/life) every frame, dep = min(0.5, dt*3.2*soak^0.7), life = R(1.4,2.6)*longer*(1/soak)^0.7 with longer = 0.75+0.35*min(2, n.d); soak = clamp(1+0.5*(3-0.2)*feat.rate, 0.2, 3) = 1+1.4*rate. Creep: life R(1.0,2.2)*longer*(0.6+0.4*feath), speed sp*(1-age/life) (linear slowdown), alpha 0.7*f; feath = 0.8+1.25*feat.density. Fleck: moves for 0.25 s (f = max(0,1-age/0.25)), alpha 0.9 for 0.05 s then 0.25*f; it is painted INTO the ink canvas, so the speck stays as ink. Persistent ink: every 0.4 s `destination-out` with alpha 1-exp(-acc/fade), i.e. exponential tau = fade knob (default 9 s, drive -level, min 1). Bleed every 1.1/soak s: blur(0.2+0.45*feath px), drift, and paper destination-out at 0.25*0.35 alpha. Wet sheen: 1-age/0.6 (hard 0.35 s), alpha 0.16 (hard 0.3). pulse: 0.5^(dt/0.3) (sheet scale 1+0.7*0.06*pulse). shake: 0.5^(dt/0.12).
lowPass: Strong: (1) the ink canvas is a leaky integrator with tau = fade (9 s) and the blur/bleed passes smear every mark; (2) bloom/spatter amounts depend on feat.rate (soak) and feat.density (feathering), i.e. busy music changes speed and amount; (3) only 2 low notes per chord bloom, `centres` max 6, `wet` max 5, fallback bloom only if sinceBlot>1.2; (4) positions are random (spot()/centres), so a given note is not located by pitch; (5) the fade is applied in 0.4 s steps and bleed steps every 1.1/soak s, so envelopes are quantised; (6) lobe swell (0.2-0.4 s) makes blots rise rather than snap; (7) violent threshold (vel>=112-8*amt, >=3 notes).
snapKnobs: fade (how long the ink stays, 1..13, default 9, less 1.6, drive -level): tau of the whole persistent ink canvas; 1 s makes the ink gone in a couple of seconds
size (blot size 0.3..2.5, less 0.45): smaller blots are a faster, crisper hit
spatter (0..3, default 1, less 0, drive +level): how many crisp flecks each high note throws, and whether loud chords splatter
sym (mirror pattern 1..8)
presence: writes size, spatter and fade
howToSnap: No-code: fade 1-2 s (and a small size). Code: lobe swell `k: R(2.5,5)*soak` -> R(12,25)*soak, lobe life R(1.4,2.6) -> R(0.4,0.8), creep life R(1.0,2.2) -> R(0.3,0.7), the fade step (fadeAcc > 0.4 -> 0.1 so short tau does not look chunky), wet sheen `1-age/0.6` -> 0.25 and pulse half-life 0.3 -> 0.12, and make the first deposition immediate (dep alpha higher on age<0.05). A global attack/decay scale would work only partly: lobes, creep, flecks, wet, pulse and shake are explicit-age objects, but the ink canvas decay is exp(-acc/fade) with a coarse step and the bleed loop is a separate clock (1.1/soak s), so a scale should multiply the fade knob and the bleed cadence too.
risk: Not in the protected scenes, but state is a persistent offscreen ink canvas (plus tmp/rim/sheen/paper canvases) that is cleared only on reset()/mode change, so seeks and renders are history-dependent; it uses Math.random and R() everywhere (not x.rnd), so it is not deterministic or pixel-comparable. The 8-bit alpha problem the author flags (fade in steps so alpha actually moves) means very short fade values with small per-step alpha stall or band; the fade, bleed, rim blur filters and mirrored 'layer' passes (per-frame 1280x720 scratch canvas, 2-16 copies) are expensive; shake translates g without a visible restore (relies on host save/restore). Changing lobe/creep lifetimes changes how much ink is deposited (dep * (1-age/life) integrated), so ink density changes with envelope changes.

onAttack: onChord, in the same frame: pushes a glint {s: pitch01(ch.hi) mapped to 0.08..0.88 of the stroke, age 0, v = 0.45+0.55*r} (max 5), where r = rank(ch.vel) is the velocity's percentile among all notes of the recording; flash = max(flash, 0.3+0.7*r); and EVERY mark in the court hops forward and flares at once: q.hop = max(q.hop, 0.4+0.6*r), q.flare = max(q.flare, pulse) with pulse = (0.2+0.8*r^2)*mix(0.6,1,fresh), fresh = max(smooth(0.1,0.4,sinceNote), (sinceBright>0.35 && r>0.85) ? 1 : 0), plus a random y jolt of +-H*0.012. It may also spawn 1-5 new marks from the edge (gated by sincePet >= gap, gap = mix(0.9,0.04,sqrt(crowd))*(r>0.8?0.4:1)), start the slow 'lift' gesture (r >= bar, bar = max(0.58, 0.9-0.022*max(0,sinceTurn-5)), sinceTurn>6 s) or, if already lifting past 75% of liftDur, trigger the 0.2 s flick that sends one side's marks off the page (this is the only attack-locked gesture); a tick of the tip if pitch01(hi)>0.42 and sinceTick>1.2.
decay: hop *= 0.5^(dt/0.13) (tau 0.19 s); flare *= 0.5^(dt/0.1) (tau 0.144 s); a mark's x follows its target with kx = 1-exp(-13 dt) (tau 77 ms) and y with ky = 1-exp(-8 dt) (tau 125 ms); hop moves a mark forward by hop*H*0.075 (54 px at 720). Figure: flash *= 0.5^(dt/0.11) (tau 0.159 s) driving sheen alpha 0.17+0.2*flash, bristle alpha 0.1+0.6*flash^2, edge alpha 0.68+0.32*flash and edge width x(1+1.6*flash); sting *= 0.5^(dt/0.16); glint: k = 1-age/0.42, alpha k^2*v, length grows by smooth(0,0.3,age) up to 5+34*v nodes. Gesture (deliberately slow): lift smoother(stT/liftDur) over liftDur = 0.55+1.0*r^2 s (waits 1.2 s more, then sinks), flick 0.2 s, hold holdDur = 1.1+0.9*r, return RET = 2.2 s, tick 0.9 s. Marks live: wait R(7,15) s then leave over 1.2 s; sent-away marks fly ~1.3 s.
lowPass: Yes, deliberately: (1) rank() normalises loudness to the piece's percentile; (2) repeated attacks inside 0.1-0.4 s get 0.6x flare (fresh = smooth(0.1,0.4,sinceNote)), unless a top (r>0.85) attack spaced >0.35 s apart; (3) the gesture needs r >= bar (0.58-0.9) and sinceTurn > 6 s, and the state machine ignores everything while not at rest (refuses to be hurried); (4) spawning is rate-limited (gap) and the court is capped (maxAlive 2..46); (5) position easing tau 77-125 ms; (6) independent 'timid' darts: every R(0.9,3.4) s each mark does hop = max(hop, R(0.3,0.7)) and a random y move with NO note, which looks like an attack (the user's 'no fake attacks' verdict), plus constant trembling and drifting.

onAttack: onChord -> write(ch, x, 0): turns the attack into figures pushed at the pen (x = W*0.84 minus age*speed): for 1-2 notes each note is its own figure (filled note head when v>=72 with radius 2+8*v^2 at pitch height Y(m); a disc for deep loud bass, m<40 and v>=90; hollow when soft) plus a growing beam when the note is held (nt.d >= 0.22; beam length speed*1.15*sqrt(d), growing at L/d so it ends when the note ends, i.e. uses the transcribed duration known at the attack); for bigger chords one figure per 'hand' (gap > 9 semitones) such as stems with dashes and end heads, a black block (gv>=92, >=3 notes), an open box (gv<64), a disc, a bracket with numeral, a big ring, and a 'link' curve between successive top notes. Also lvl = max(lvl, vel/115) which swells the continuous line, and pop = 1 (the pen hairline) if age<0.2. A token bucket (tokens refill gap*ink per second, capped 3, cost 1 per attack; vel>=108 may borrow to -0.5) turns excess attacks into 'specks' (r = 0.8+v/127) or a faint stem for strong ones. Silence >2.2 s begins with a double bar.
decay: Figures do not decay in time; they scroll left at speed px/s (default 48, 20..140) and fade by position: draw() alpha a = clamp(f.x/170, 0, 1) * clamp(f.age/0.08, 0.15, 1): fades in over 0.08 s from 0.15 and fades out linearly over the last 170 px before x=0 (at 48 px/s: full alpha for (1075-170)/48 = 18.9 s, then 3.5 s fade, ~22 s total; at speed 140 ~7.7 s). Removed when x+len+r < -260. Overshoot pop: note radius x(1+0.35*max(0,1-age/0.15)), disc x(1+0.25*max(0,1-age/0.15)). Pen hairline: pop *= 0.5^(dt/0.08), alpha 0.1+0.35*pop. Continuous line: lvl *= 0.5^(dt/0.8), sampled every 0.05 s into `life` points that scroll with the page (so a loudness bump stays on the line for the whole traverse); a 60 px gradient masks the left edge.

Loudness is the raw velocity (no ranking), the continuous line has the 0.8 s half-life. Chords are grouped into hands, so inner notes are not separate figures.
